stories.title: 5 killed after being run over by train in Prayagraj:Were standing below after getting down from coach; hit by 2 trains
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, 5 people died after being hit by a train around 7:30 PM on Wednesday evening. Upon receiving information, police and railway teams reached the spot and took possession of the bodies, sending them for post-mortem. According to the police, efforts are being made to identify the deceased. The accident occurred at Pachdeora Halt in the Karchhana area. Passengers had got down from the train at a halt station Akash (19), son of Giriraj and a resident of Prithvipur village under Khairgarh police station in Firozabad, was travelling to attend a wedding at a relative’s house in Kolkata. Ajay, son of Munna Pasi and a resident of Kolkata, was also with him. Near Pachdevara, a man fell from the same train, after which the emergency chain was pulled and the train stopped. All the passengers got down to relieve themselves. At that moment, the Kalka Mail sounded its horn and people started moving back towards the train. Meanwhile, the Purushottam Express, coming from the Mirzapur side, hit five people, killing all of them. Two of the deceased have been identified as Akash Kumar from Firozabad and Sunil Kumar from Mirzapur. Three bodies remain unidentified. As soon as the information was received, the Karchana police, ACP Sunil Kumar Singh, GRP and railway officials reached the spot. See 3 pictures Passengers had alighted from the train at Halt station A train stopped for a while near Pachdeora Halt. A passenger got down and went to the other track to use the toilet. Just then, the Kalka Mail arrived, and the young man died on the spot after being hit by it. Seeing this incident, passengers on the train raised an alarm. The deceased's family members got down in a panic, and then another train also arrived, and all three were hit by it. They also died on the spot in this accident. After the incident, another person is reported missing. It is suspected that he was also hit by the train, although this has not been officially confirmed yet. Upon receiving the information, police from Karchhana police station, ACP Sunil Kumar Singh, GRP, and railway officials reached the spot.

stories.title: UP to have 120 Lok Sabha seats in next election:Currently 80 seats; change after Delimitation Commission is formed
stories.summary: The special session of Parliament in New Delhi is starting tomorrow (Thursday). The government is going to form a Delimitation Commission and introduce the 131st Constitution Amendment Bill. If both these bills are passed by a two-thirds majority in the House, then the picture of UP regarding the 2029 Lok Sabha elections will also become clear. UP's seats in the Lok Sabha can be increased from 80 to 120. Meanwhile, the Assembly seats can increase from 403 to 550-600. The number of Lok Sabha seats in UP has been increased from time to time based on the recommendations of the Delimitation Commission. What is the 131st Constitution Amendment? The Constitution Amendment Bill proposes to increase the Lok Sabha seats from 543 to 850. Of these, a maximum of 815 seats will be for states and 35 for Union Territories. A Delimitation Commission will be formed to determine the number of seats. The commission will also decide how many seats each state will have. According to sources, the 2011 census will be considered the basis for the new delimitation. The distribution of seats will be determined based on population. In 2011, Uttar Pradesh's population was 16% of the country's total population. In this regard, if the Lok Sabha has 835 seats for states, then based on population, UP's seats could increase from 80 to 120-130. 40 seats will be reserved for women If the Lok Sabha seats in UP reach 120 after the new delimitation, then 33% of those seats will be reserved for women. This means only women MPs will be elected on 40 seats. This will also give an opportunity to women workers of political parties to go to Parliament. Assembly Seats Will Increase to 600 Experts believe that the current number of UP Assembly seats is based on the 1971 census. The population has increased significantly in the last 55 years. In 2026, the estimated population of UP has been assessed at 24.82 crore. In five and a half decades, migration from villages to cities has also been very high. The number of cities has increased. In UP, on average, there are more than 4 lakh voters in one assembly constituency. However, in the recently conducted Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the voter list, the number of voters has decreased. Still, the number of voters in UP's assembly constituencies is higher than in other states. If the formula of increasing seats according to population and reducing the burden of voters in existing assembly constituencies is implemented, the assembly seats here will increase to 550 to 600. Among these, 33% of seats (from 181 to 198) will be reserved for women. Assembly election seats could increase from 2032 In 2027, the assembly elections will be held on 403 seats only, but in the 2032 assembly elections, the number of seats will increase. Experts believe that if One Nation-One Election is implemented, the assembly seats in UP will increase even before 2032. Currently 12% Women MLAs in the Assembly Currently, there are 51 women MLAs in the UP Assembly compared to 403 seats. Among these, there are 30 from BJP, 15 from Samajwadi Party, 4 from Apna Dal (S), one from RLD, and one woman MLA from Congress. Assembly constituencies will be within the ambit of a single Lok Sabha constituency After the new delimitation, a major problem of political parties will be resolved. There are many Lok Sabha constituencies in UP whose assembly constituencies are within the boundaries of more than one district. In the new delimitation, it will be ensured that all assembly constituencies under a Lok Sabha constituency are within the boundaries of a single district. An assembly constituency will also not be divided between two Lok Sabha constituencies.

stories.title: Massive fire guts over 50 huts in Lucknow:LPG cylinders explode; man claims 4 children charred to death
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in the Vikasnagar area of Lucknow on Wednesday evening around 5:30 pm, destroying over 50 slum huts and triggering explosions of more than 30 LPG cylinders. The flames were so intense that they were visible from nearly 10 kilometres away. As the fire spread rapidly, around 20 nearby houses were evacuated as a precaution. Fire brought under control after 3 hours Around 20 fire brigade vehicles were deployed to control the blaze, which was finally brought under control after nearly three hours. Electricity supply in the area was cut off during the firefighting operation to prevent further hazards. A local resident claimed that his four children were burnt alive in the fire, though official confirmation is awaited. Several families lost all their belongings as their huts were reduced to ashes. Those affected were seen wailing in distress as they watched their homes burn down. Allegations of deliberate fire Some residents alleged that the fire may have been deliberately set, though authorities have not confirmed this. An investigation into the cause of the fire is underway. CM orders swift action Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took cognisance of the incident and directed officials to immediately reach the spot and oversee relief efforts. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak also visited the site and instructed authorities to expedite rescue and relief operations.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Sabarimala women entry case hearing on Day 4: Adv Singhvi says court can’t rule on religious beliefs A hearing is underway in the Supreme Court of India concerning the entry of women into the Sabarimala Temple. 2. Parents plan to sell their newborn fails: Grandmother rescues child; mother had struck a deal with a businessman for 2.5 lakhs In Agra, a mother made a deal to sell her two-day-old newborn baby. The price of the baby was fixed at Rs 2.5 lakh. A businessman even reached the hospital to take the baby, but the grandmother and aunt got wind of it. 3. Woman remains unidentified 5 days after her dead body recovery: Post-mortem report shows 17 injury marks The post-mortem report of the unidentified woman's body found by the roadside in the Kakori area has arrived. The report shows two severe injury marks on the front and back of the woman's head, while about 15 injuries were found on other parts of the body. 4. 'Har ghar bhagwa chhaega, Ram Rajya aaega', says BJP's Suvendu Adhikari Suvendu Adhikari, Leader of the Opposition in West Bengal and BJP candidate from Nandigram and Bhabanipur, said that “the public is ready”. He raised a slogan while campaigning, ‘Har ghar bhagwa chhaega, Ram Rajya aaega’. 5. Women DMs, SSPs in 25 UP districts:33% posting plan before 2027 polls Efforts are underway in Uttar Pradesh to increase women’s participation in governance, with the first impact likely to be seen in district-level administration. 6. 4-year-old girl shows no fear of water: Swims 900 metres across the Yamuna River in 21 minutes In Prayagraj district of Uttar Pradesh, 4-year-old Satya Bharti from the Mahewa West area has achieved a feat that even seasoned swimmers often find challenging. She swam across the Yamuna river in just 21 minutes and 28 seconds. 7. Dalal Street cheers Modi-Trump call over Hormuz Strait trade Following the conversation between US President Donald Trump and his India counterpart PM Modi, the Indian benchmark indices advanced in early deals on Wednesday, 15 April, 2026. Sensex soared 1,300 points at opening. 8. Misleading video sparks FIR on 2 RJD women spokespersons After two days of unrest, factories in Noida reopened on Wednesday, with the situation returning to normal. Heavy security has been deployed, with surveillance through CCTV cameras and drones. 9. 3 years after Atiq’s killing, wife Shaista is still missing:2 other family members are absconding Three years on, the UP Police has failed to trace Atiq Ahmed’s wife, Shaista Parveen. Raids were conducted across nine states, with support from ATS and RAF teams, but she remains untraceable. 10. India's wholesale inflation rises for the 5th month in a row to 3.88% Wholesale prices of goods in India have gone up again in March 2025, increasing by 3.88%, the government data showed. This marks the fifth month in a row that prices have climbed.

stories.title: Woman climbs water tank for boyfriend, threatens to end life:Family conducts garland ceremony in Gorakhpur; wedding was fixed elsewhere on April 21
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, an 18-year-old girl climbed a 70-foot-high water tank on Tuesday evening, demanding to marry her boyfriend and threatening to end her life. She shouted from the top, asking people to call her boyfriend and warned that she would kill herself if anyone tried to stop her. Soon, a large crowd gathered at the spot and tried to convince her to come down, but she refused. Police also reached the scene after getting information, but their efforts failed to calm her. After nearly two hours, her boyfriend was brought there and both families agreed to the marriage. Only then did the girl come down safely. Later, the couple exchanged garlands and got married on the spot. After the ceremony, the girl was sent to the boy’s house. The incident took place in Mahavir Chhapra village under Belipar police station area. The couple had been in a relationship for four years, but the girl’s family had fixed her marriage elsewhere, scheduled for April 21. Met during college studies The girl said - she was studying intermediate, and during that time, she met a young man (19) from the same village. In 2022, we first became friends, and then gradually fell in love with each other. We have been in a relationship for four years. My family was not ready for the marriage. They fixed my marriage with another boy. The wedding procession was due to arrive on April 21st. I refused the marriage, but my family did not agree. They also stopped me from leaving the house. I tried to convince my parents, but they didn't agree. On April 14, Tuesday, at 3 PM, I reached near the water tank of the Jal Jeevan Mission located in Jotbagahi village. I thought that if my family didn't agree today, I would jump and end my life. People bowed to the girl's stubbornness, pressured the family to agree Villagers said that many attempts were made to get the girl down, but she did not agree. The police also tried to explain. Seeing her stubbornness, we talked to her family. Both families were called. The police spoke to both families and then they agreed to the marriage. After the family agreed, the girl was brought down. The varmala ceremony was arranged right there. And the two were married in front of everyone. After this, the girl was sent with the boy. After the marriage, the young woman was sent with her husband SP South Dinesh Puri said - The young woman was safely brought down. She was handed over to her family. Then, on the spot, both families were talked to and consent for the marriage was obtained. After this, the young woman was married. After the varmala ceremony, the girl was sent with her boy.

stories.title: Big setback for Baahubali Dhananjay, Abhay Singh acquitted:Varanasi court verdict in 24-year-old Taksal case, firing allegation involved
stories.summary: Strongman Dhananjay Singh has suffered a setback in the 24-year-old Taksal Cinema incident of Varanasi. The MP-MLA Court on Wednesday acquitted all 6 accused, including Abhay Singh and Mirzapur MLC Vineet Singh. Dhananjay had alleged that Abhay and Vineet Singh, along with 4-5 associates, had indiscriminately fired upon his convoy. In this, he, his gunner, and driver were injured. On April 13, Special Judge (MP-MLA Court) Yajuvendra Vikram Singh had reserved the verdict. Security was beefed up in and around the court premises in view of the verdict. More than 350 policemen, including 2 IPS officers and 3 ACPs, were deployed. One company of PAC (Provincial Armed Constabulary) was also called. Meanwhile, on Tuesday night, before the judgment, Dhananjay Singh bowed his head at Baba Vishwanath Temple and performed Rudrabhishek. He also offered prayers at the Kalbhairav Temple. He had said - 'We will definitely get justice.' Know the full story 1- Abhay got Dhananjay a hostel by calling him his maternal aunt's son According to Abhay Singh, Dhananjay Singh, who graduated from Karra College in Jaunpur in 1992, was first introduced by Dharmendra Singh, the president of Tilakdhari Singh College. It was the day of Dussehra. It was then that he said Dhananjay was also going to Lucknow to study, and asked to help him. According to Abhay Singh, Dhananjay's admission was arranged by his close friend Piyush Singh. Piyush was also studying at Lucknow University. However, Dhananjay Singh has himself narrated the story of his admission. According to him, admission was then through an entrance exam. He had passed the entrance test in both Prayagraj and Lucknow universities, but he decided to take admission in Lucknow University. At Lucknow University, Abhay Singh was one year senior to Dhananjay Singh in studies. He was already living in room number 51 in the hostel. He lied to the hostel warden that Dhananjay was his aunt's son. After this, Dhananjay Singh was allotted room number 18 on the lower floor of Abhay Singh's hostel. 2- The friendship of the three was famous in the university Arun Upadhyay, also from Jaunpur, was studying at Lucknow University. He was active in student politics. Due to their connection with Jaunpur, Abhay and Dhananjay were friends with him. According to Abhay Singh, his dream was to qualify for UPSC. Meanwhile, Dhananjay Singh says that he had only two dreams from the beginning: first, to join the army, and second, to enter politics after retirement. This trio became famous on the university campus. The three were seen together in protests against the Mandal agitation. At that time, Lucknow University had dominance across the entire state. Arun Upadhyay was preparing for the General Secretary election. Their friendship lasted until 2002. After this, their relationship started to sour. In 2002, Dhananjay Singh was subjected to a deadly attack in Banaras. Dhananjay Singh filed an FIR, naming his close friend Abhay Singh as the accused. 3- How Both Got the Title of Strongman Former Jaunpur MP Dhananjay Singh of Jaunpur and Abhay Singh, MLA from Goshainganj, Ayodhya, are known as strongman leaders in politics. Dhananjay Singh claimed in an interview with Dainik Bhaskar that after meeting Abhay Singh, he also became an accused in every one of Abhay Singh's cases. Later, when he became active in politics, cases kept piling up due to political reasons. On the other hand, Abhay Singh claims that before Arun Upadhyay's student elections, only one assault case was registered against him. After this, all other cases were registered. Many cases were registered even without any crime. In many, he was also made an accused in Dhananjay Singh's crimes. 4- In 1996, Abhay went to jail, and Dhananjay absconded In 1996, Hemant Singh was murdered. At that time, the then SSP Surya Kumar Shukla in Lucknow made both Abhay and Dhananjay accused. However, Abhay Singh claims that both of them were falsely implicated in this case. On January 11, 1996, Abhay Singh went to jail in a case registered for attempted murder and remained there for 4 and a half years. Dhananjay Singh remained absconding till February 1999. 5- Dispute in jail, both went their separate ways After Dhananjay surrendered in February 1999, he met Abhay in jail. There, a dispute arose between the two over old incidents, tender money, and the murders of Santosh and Abhishek. From there, both went their separate ways. In 2000, Abhay was released on bail. He met Naseemuddin Siddiqui in jail. Through him, Abhay Singh got his first MLA ticket from BSP in 2002. But he lost. Meanwhile, Dhananjay Singh contested the Rari assembly election as an independent in 2002 and won. On October 4, 2002, Dhananjay Singh's convoy was attacked. Dhananjay filed a case against Abhay, and since then, their paths diverged. Whenever they get a chance, they keep showering accusations on each other. When Dhananjay's close associates Alok Singh and Manish Singh Tata were caught in the codeine cough syrup case, Abhay had then taunted him by calling him 'Codeine Bhaiya'.

stories.title: 4-year-old girl shows no fear of water:Swims 900 metres across Yamuna river in 21 minutes; stuns onlookers
stories.summary: In Prayagraj district of Uttar Pradesh, 4-year-old Satya Bharti from the Mahewa West area has achieved a feat that even seasoned swimmers often find challenging. She swam across the Yamuna river in just 21 minutes and 28 seconds. The historic swim began at exactly 7am on Saturday. Displaying remarkable confidence and courage, Satya battled the strong currents of the Yamuna river and swam from one bank to the other, leaving everyone astonished. A video of her achievement is rapidly going viral on social media, with people widely praising her determination and bravery. Her parents and coach are extremely proud of her accomplishment. Training under coach Tribhuvan Nishad Satya is the daughter of Devendra Kumar and has been training regularly under her coach, Tribhuvan Nishad. According to him, she has shown discipline, eagerness to learn and strong confidence from a very young age. At an age when most children are just getting familiar with basic play, Satya has crossed a major river like the Yamuna, proving that with determination and proper guidance, age is no barrier to success. She has now become an inspiration not just for Prayagraj, but for the entire state. A promising future ahead Her coach believes that with advanced training, Satya has the potential to win medals for the state and the country. Meanwhile, her video continues to gain traction online, with people encouraging her and urging support to help her reach greater heights.

stories.title: Misleading video sparks FIR on 2 RJD women spokespersons:Unrest-hit Noida factories reopen after 2 days with heavy security
stories.summary: After two days of unrest, factories in Noida reopened on Wednesday, with the situation returning to normal. Heavy security has been deployed, with surveillance through CCTV cameras and drones. Around 16 companies of Rapid Action Force (RAF) and Pradeshik Armed Constabulary (PAC) have been stationed, while police conducted flag marches in Sectors 63, 80, 84, 85 and Phase 2. Notices on salary hikes have been put up outside several companies. However, some units remained shut for the day, informing employees through notices that operations would resume later, with further updates to be shared in advance. Meanwhile, an FIR has been registered at Noida’s Cyber Crime Police Station against two RJD women spokespersons, Kanchana Yadav and Priyanka Bharti. They have been accused of sharing misleading videos on social media to incite unrest and damage the image of law enforcement. District Magistrate (DM) Medha Rupam said- If any outsourcing agency or its employee causes disturbance or mischief, the agency will also be held responsible. In such a situation, the agency can be blacklisted. Its license can also be revoked. Actually, factory workers created a ruckus on Monday-Tuesday over salary increases. Stone-pelting occurred at more than 80 places. Vandalism occurred in 350 companies. Minister Anil Rajbhar said, “There is a strong whiff of a big conspiracy in this entire incident. Some anti-national forces might be involved in this.” Meanwhile, the company owners say that outsiders instigated the atmosphere. Workers can never resort to violent protests. They cannot harm the place from where they earn their livelihood. Currently, the police have arrested 396 people, including 4 women. See pictures- DM said, ‘Contractors should follow guidelines’ Union leader says, ‘No connection with agitation’ Amar Singh, District President of All India Centre Council Trade Union, says that the union has no connection with the violence and agitation. The agitation was carried out by the workers. Surendra Nahata, President of MSME Industrial Association Noida, informed that industries from Sector-1 to 6 are opening. The remaining factories will also open. Situation completely normal, no law and order problem Regarding the workers' protest in Noida, Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police (DGP) Rajiv Krishna said that the situation in the district is completely normal. There is no law and order problem anywhere. All senior officers are present on the spot. The situation is being continuously monitored.

stories.title: 3 years after Atiq’s killing, wife Shaista still missing:2 other family members absconding; search continues for co-conspirators in Umesh Pal murder case
stories.summary: Three years on, the UP Police has failed to trace Atiq Ahmed’s wife Shaista Parveen. Raids were conducted across nine states, with support from ATS and RAF teams, but she remains untraceable. A reward of ₹50,000 has been announced for information on Shaista, who has been underground since the Umesh Pal murder case. She continues to feature on the UP Police’s most-wanted list of women criminals, yet her whereabouts remain unknown. Apart from Shaista, Atiq’s sister Ayesha Noori and brother Ashraf’s wife Zainab are also absconding. All three have been accused of conspiring in the Umesh Pal murder and aiding the attackers. The police have announced rewards of ₹25,000 each on Ayesha and Zainab. While there were initial suspicions that they may have fled to Dubai, officials later ruled out that possibility. Notably, Atiq Ahmed was killed on April 15, 2023. Even after three years, the police have not been able to arrest the three key accused women linked to the conspiracy. What happened over these three years, and why have they remained beyond the police’s reach? Read the full report. On February 24, 2023, lawyer Umesh Pal and his two police gunners were killed in a brutal shooting and bombing in Prayagraj’s Dhumanganj area, setting off one of Uttar Pradesh’s biggest crime probes. CCTV clues and widening conspiracy CCTV footage showed Atiq Ahmed’s son Asad firing, while Guddu Muslim hurled bombs. Others, including Ghulam, Shabir and Usman, were also seen shooting. At the time, Atiq was lodged in Sabarmati Jail, and investigators alleged he orchestrated the attack from there. He, along with brother Ashraf, son Asad and nine others, was named in the case. Within days, Atiq’s wife Shaista Parveen, sister Ayesha Noori and Ashraf’s wife Zainab were also accused of conspiracy and aiding the attackers. Notably, all three were still in the Dhumanganj area even two days after the murder. Shaista later wrote to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the Allahabad High Court Chief Justice, calling the case a political conspiracy aimed at keeping Atiq’s family out of local elections. Manhunt without breakthrough After CCTV footage was released on February 26, showing Asad firing, Shaista, Zainab and Ayesha went underground. Police launched an extensive crackdown—encounters followed, properties were demolished, and rewards were announced for information. Multiple teams carried out raids across Uttar Pradesh before expanding the search to nine states. Within weeks, more than 500 locations were searched. Several accused were caught, but the three women remained untraceable. No trace even after key killings On April 13, 2023, Asad was killed in a police encounter in Jhansi. Two days later, Atiq Ahmed and Ashraf were shot dead in Prayagraj during a medical visit. Despite these developments, none of the three women surfaced—not even for the last rites, despite heavy police surveillance. Repeated inputs placed Shaista in parts of Kaushambi, where police conducted searches using drones and combing operations, but found no trace. Assets seized, leads go cold As the search continued, authorities seized properties worth nearly ₹3,000 crore linked to Atiq’s network, many allegedly held in benami names. Investigators believe the total value could be significantly higher. CCTV clues from Meerut suggested Guddu Muslim had taken shelter at a relative’s house linked to Ayesha Noori, leading to one arrest, but Ayesha herself remained absconding. Later inputs from Odisha and Delhi also failed to yield results, though police ruled out any foreign escape. Meanwhile, the trial in the Atiq-Ashraf murder case continues, largely through video conferencing due to security concerns.

stories.title: DMs, SSPs in 25 UP districts are females:Govt plans 33% women reservation in postings before 2027 polls
stories.summary: Efforts are underway in Uttar Pradesh to increase women’s participation in governance, with the first impact likely to be seen in district-level administration. The state government is preparing to assign more women IAS and IPS officers to key positions such as Divisional Commissioner, District Magistrate (DM), and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP). At present, women account for around 16% of DMs and about 12% of SSPs across the state’s 75 districts. Even before the implementation of the ‘Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam’, the government is planning to increase women’s representation in bureaucracy to 33%. The move is aimed at sending a strong political message on women’s empowerment. Officials believe this step could help strengthen trust among women voters ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The move is being seen as part of a broader strategy: Message of empowerment: Extending ‘Nari Shakti’ beyond Parliament and Assemblies to decision-making roles like DM and SSP Targeting women voters: Of UP’s 13.39 crore voters, nearly 6.5 crore are women From beneficiaries to decision-makers: After schemes like free ration, Ujjwala and Mission Shakti, focus now shifts to representation Governance branding: Women officers are often associated with stricter law enforcement and greater sensitivity in social issues Countering opposition narrative: Aimed at addressing criticism on jobs, governance and social balance Currently, 12 out of 75 districts (16%) have women District Magistrates. This number could increase to 20–25 districts in the coming reshuffle. In policing, women IPS officers are posted in only 8 districts, indicating significant scope for expansion. Who could get key postings? Several women officers are being considered for district leadership roles, including: Annapurna Garg (IAS, 2016 batch) Kavita Meena, Vice Chairman, Muzaffarnagar Development Authority Saranjit Kaur Broca, Director, Women and Child Welfare Isha Priya, Special Secretary, Tourism Transfers likely before elections Transfers were restricted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) period from October 27, 2025 to April 10, 2026, with changes requiring Election Commission approval. With the 2027 Assembly elections expected in February–March, a major reshuffle of Commissioners, DMs and police chiefs is likely before the Model Code of Conduct comes into force, possibly by late January or early February. Election rules may trigger reshuffle As per Election Commission norms, officers posted in the same district for over three years ahead of elections are typically transferred. Apart from election-related changes, DMs of several districts—including Ambedkar Nagar, Chandauli, Hapur, Chitrakoot, Shravasti, Bhadohi, Mahoba, Sultanpur, Hathras, Barabanki and Lalitpur—may also be shifted for administrative reasons. Some may be moved to other districts, while others could be assigned roles such as Director or Special Secretary in government departments.

stories.title: Woman remains unidentified 5 days after her dead body recovery:Post-mortem report shows 17 injury marks, rape suspected
stories.summary: The post-mortem report of the unidentified woman's body found by the roadside in the Kakori area has arrived. The report shows two severe injury marks on the front and back of the woman's head, while about 15 injuries were found on other parts of the body. Doctors have stated the cause of death as severe head injury. Given the suspicion of rape, doctors have prepared slides and sent them for examination. Only after the report comes will it be known whether rape occurred or not. However, the woman has not yet been identified. Body was covered in blood On the morning of 9 April, outside Madarpur village in Kakori, the blood-soaked body of an unknown woman, approximately 35 years old, was found in a field by the roadside. Looking at the condition of the body, murder after rape was suspected. According to Inspector Satish Rathore, the woman's head had been struck with a stick or a heavy object. Injury marks were also found at several places on the body, which point towards a violent incident. So far, the woman has not been identified. For identification, photos have been pasted in public places in the city and surrounding districts. CCTV camera footage from toll plazas on Agra Expressway and other major highways is being scrutinized. No concrete clue has been found from the crime scene or the woman's clothes that could help identify her. The investigation into the case is ongoing. Unidentified body was cremated Due to lack of identification, the police cremated the woman's body on April 13. DNA samples have been preserved for future identification. A case of murder has been registered against unknown persons in the matter. ACP Kakori Shakeel Ahmed said that so far, footage from more than 500 CCTV cameras has been scanned for the identification of the woman. Pictures of the body have been circulated on social media platforms. Missing person cases registered in nearby districts are also being investigated.

stories.title: Parents plan to sell their newborn fails:Grandmother rescues child; mother had struck a deal with businessman for 2.5 lakhs
stories.summary: In Agra, a mother made a deal to sell her two-day-old newborn baby. The price of the baby was fixed at Rs 2.5 lakh. A businessman even reached the hospital to take the baby, but the grandmother and aunt got wind of it. Both of them filed a complaint on the Child Helpline. As soon as the information was received, the team reached the spot. Immediate action was taken with the help of police. The newborn and family members were taken into custody. Everyone was presented before the magistrate of the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). On Monday, the magistrate had the couple fill an affidavit. After this, the newborn was handed over to them. Now know the complete case A call came to Childline's helpline number 1098 on Friday night. The woman who called, identified herself as Rajkumari. Rajkumari said that her son Manoj lives in Shastripuram, Sikandra. Manoj works as a laborer in a factory. His wife Kumkum has a son from before. “Kumkum gave birth to a second son at the hospital on Wednesday. The child is being sold right after birth. A deal has already been made with a trader from Kamla Nagar. A deal has been fixed for two and a half lakh rupees to hand over the newborn. The trader was supposed to reach the hospital on Friday night to take the child,” she said. Childline team reached the hospital, couple denied the allegations As soon as the complaint was received, the Childline team reached the hospital with the police. The team spoke with the woman who gave birth to the newborn and her husband. The couple flatly denied the allegations of selling the child. They claimed that some relatives were making false allegations as part of a conspiracy. After this, with the help of police, the child and family members were presented before the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). Here, an affidavit was filled by the couple. After completing the procedure, the newborn was handed back to the couple. Grandmother said - They were selling the newborn for two and a half lakh Grandmother Rajkumari said - On Friday, my daughter-in-law gave birth to a son at Lady Lion Hospital. Just a short while later, some people arrived at the hospital to see the child. Those people were talking about buying the child. I wanted to bring my grandson home. The son, daughter-in-law, and father-in-law were going to give away the child for two and a half lakh rupees. I opposed this, but no one listened to me. Angered by this, I returned home. After some time, my daughter called, so I told her the whole matter. Child reunited with family after two days of surveillance Rajkumari said that my daughter immediately complained to Agra Child Helpline number 1098 from Meerut. After this, the team reached the spot and action was initiated. Due to Saturday and Sunday being holidays, further proceedings could not take place. The Childline team deployed police personnel outside the hospital. The police kept surveillance for two days so that no one could take the child away. On Monday, we were presented before the magistrate of the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). After filling out an affidavit there, further action was taken. Now the child is at our home and we are happy. Child will have to be presented again after 15 days Childline coordinator Brajesh Kumar Gautam said- On Monday, the couple was presented before the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). Here, a written affidavit was taken from the couple. It was clarified in the affidavit that they will not give the newborn to any other person for adoption. After completing the procedure, the child has been handed over to the couple. They have been instructed that the child will have to be presented before the committee again within 15 days.

stories.title: ATS raids Varanasi doctor’s house in terror funding probe:Team questions son, Pakistan links traced
stories.summary: A joint team of the Uttar Pradesh ATS and the Intelligence Bureau raided the house of a doctor in Varanasi on Tuesday afternoon over suspected terror funding. The team stayed at the house for nearly seven hours. Officials seized a mobile phone, laptop and printer from the premises and questioned the doctor’s family members, including his son. Police forces were deployed outside the house during the operation to maintain security. Digital evidence and financial trail under scrutiny Preliminary investigation has revealed transactions worth several lakhs of rupees in the doctor’s bank account. Agencies are examining possible links to individuals in Pakistan and organisations based in Kashmir. Investigators said several suspicious contacts were found saved in the doctor’s phone. Call records, chats and other digital data are being analysed for further leads. See 2 pictures... Son questioned over alleged online contacts The doctor, identified as Dr Arif Ansari, is a paediatrician who runs a local hospital. His 20-year-old son, Abu Bakr, who is preparing for NEET, is also being questioned. Sources said Abu Bakr was allegedly in touch with a Kashmir-based handle through WhatsApp and had communicated with some suspicious individuals, including contacts linked to Pakistan. His electronic devices have also been seized for examination. Heavy police deployment, officials remain tight-lipped As news of the raid spread, a crowd gathered outside the house. Police restricted entry into the lane, allowing only local residents. Senior officers, including ACP Kotwali Vijay Pratap Singh and Adampur Inspector Vimal Kumar Mishra, have not issued any official statement. An ATS officer present at the spot declined to share details, citing the ongoing investigation. Locals express shock, vouch for family Residents in the area described Dr Ansari as a respected and well-behaved person. A local resident said the family has a good reputation and the son is known to be focused on his studies. Many expressed surprise over the development, saying they found it difficult to believe the allegations. Link to Lucknow arrests under investigation The raid is linked to inputs obtained after four suspects were arrested by the ATS near Charbagh railway station in Lucknow on April 10. During interrogation, agencies found possible links between the suspects and Pakistan’s intelligence agency ISI, along with other terror outfits. Investigators believe a wider network involving terror funding may be active across cities such as Mumbai, Lucknow and Varanasi. Based on these inputs, multiple locations are being probed. Agencies are now examining bank transactions, call records and digital evidence to establish the full extent of the network.

stories.title: Ambedkar statue vandalism sparks violence in Lakhimpur:Stone-pelting at police, vehicles smashed; cops allege illegal installation
stories.summary: Tension gripped Uttar Pradesh’s Lakhimpur Kheri on Tuesday evening after a statue of B. R. Ambedkar was allegedly damaged, triggering clashes between villagers and the police in the Bankeganj area. According to officials, an angry crowd gathered in Motipur village under the Gola Gokarnnath police station limits and began pelting stones at police personnel. Several police vehicles were vandalised, and at least one vehicle was overturned during the unrest. Police teams, along with additional forces, were rushed to the spot to bring the situation under control. Authorities said a tense calm prevails in the area, with senior officers deployed and monitoring the situation. See 2 pictures... Dispute over statue installation Villagers alleged that a community feast was underway and a statue of Ambedkar was being installed on land near a Buddhist vihara that had remained vacant for years. After the installation, most men reportedly left for a rally, leaving women at the site. Residents claimed that police, accompanied by a local woman, arrived and removed the statue, during which it was damaged. Some women also alleged that they were subjected to a baton charge when they tried to intervene. Violence escalates, woman assaulted The incident sparked outrage among villagers, who accused local police officials and the woman of triggering the confrontation. In the ensuing chaos, the woman was allegedly assaulted by the crowd before police personnel intervened and escorted her to safety. Officials confirmed that multiple government vehicles, including those used by the Circle Officer (CO) and the tehsildar, were damaged in the violence. Police response Police officials said the statue had been installed without prior permission at a disputed site, and action was taken to remove it. They added that discussions are ongoing between the village head, residents, and officials from the police and revenue departments to defuse tensions. Security remains tight in the area as authorities continue efforts to restore normalcy.

stories.title: Judge who made ‘kathmulla’ remark to retire before impeachment:Case pending in Rajya Sabha for 1.5 years; farewell at Allahabad HC tomorrow
stories.summary: Justice faced criticism over remarks at VHP event; SC had sought clarification Justice Shekhar Kumar Yadav of the Allahabad High Court will retire on Wednesday, April 15, while an impeachment motion against him remains pending in the Rajya Sabha for nearly a year. The motion, however, is expected to lapse automatically after his retirement. Controversy over remarks at VHP event Justice Yadav had attended an event organised by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad’s legal cell in Prayagraj on December 8, 2024. During his speech, he said that India runs according to the wishes of the majority and made remarks referring to “hardline fundamentalists,” which drew sharp criticism. The Supreme Court of India sought clarification from him and reportedly asked him to express regret. Justice Yadav, however, refused, stating that he had said nothing wrong. Impeachment motion: What happens next The impeachment motion was moved in the Rajya Sabha on December 13, 2024, with signatures of 55 opposition MPs, exceeding the required threshold. No action has been taken on it so far. With Justice Yadav retiring before proceedings could begin, the motion will become null and void. Full court reference scheduled A full court reference will be held at the Allahabad High Court on Wednesday at 3:45 PM in the Chief Justice’s courtroom to mark his retirement. Judges, bar association members, and registry officials will attend the ceremony. Justice Yadav was appointed as an additional judge on December 12, 2019, and became a permanent judge on March 26, 2021. Former CJI’s remark on judicial conduct Former Chief Justice of India D Y Chandrachud had emphasised that judges must be cautious in their public statements, noting that remarks should not create an impression of bias in the judiciary. Key remarks that drew criticism Previous controversial statements Profile: Justice Shekhar Kumar Yadav Appointed additional judge in 2019, permanent judge in 2021our personal law permits this, it will not be accepted. stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Noida unrest flares again, stones hurled at police; BJP's Samrat Choudhary named new Bihar CM more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Samrat Chaudhary to be Bihar’s new CM, oath ceremony tomorrow Samrat Chaudhary will be the new Chief Minister of Bihar. He has been chosen as the leader of the BJP legislative party. A formal announcement will be made after the NDA meeting. The swearing-in ceremony will take place tomorrow, 15 April, at Lok Bhavan. 2. Noida unrest flares again, stone-pelting at police; heavy force deployed Fresh protests erupted in Noida as factory workers demanding higher wages clashed with police, pelting stones at multiple locations. Over 300 arrests were made, heavy forces deployed, and surveillance intensified. Rahul Gandhi called the unrest workers’ “last cry” amid escalating tensions. 3. Dalit vote in focus on Ambedkar Jayanti, parties step up outreach On Ambedkar Jayanti, all major parties in Uttar Pradesh reached out to Dalit voters. Mayawati held a show of strength in Lucknow, while BJP, SP and Congress announced schemes and campaigns to win support. 4. Centre plans Lok Sabha expansion to 850 seats The central government on Tuesday, April 14, proposed increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats after the delimitation of constituencies. As per the news agency ANI, the total number of seats will be increased to 850. Out of these, 815 seats will be allocated to the states. 35 seats will be reserved for Union Territories (UTs). 5. UP ATS to probe 26 arson cases over terror link, NIA steps in Uttar Pradesh ATS will re-investigate 26 fire incidents after terror links emerged from arrests in Lucknow. Suspects allegedly filmed arson acts and sent videos to Pakistan-based handlers. National Investigation Agency has issued lookout notices against three accused as the probe widens. 6. Kidney racket busted: Kingpin charged ₹30 lakh, ‘Commando Surgery’ code used in Kanpur hub Police have exposed a kidney racket operating across multiple cities, with the kingpin charging up to ₹30 lakh per transplant. The network used the codeword “Commando Surgery” to avoid detection. Illegal transplants were carried out in Kanpur. Several accused have been arrested. 7. Petrol may become expensive by ₹18 Diesel ₹35 Due to rising crude oil prices, petrol could become expensive by ₹18 and diesel by ₹35 per liter. A report by foreign brokerage firm Macquarie states that despite expensive crude oil, petrol-diesel prices in the country remain stable. 8. Noida film city to benefit Saharanpur populace, says Yogi; ‘those who divide can’t deliver development’ Yogi Adityanath said Saharanpur youth will get opportunities closer to home with the upcoming Noida film city. Addressing an expressway event, he also attacked those “dividing society”, while highlighting improved connectivity and economic boost from the Delhi–Dehradun corridor. 9. Kanpur constable booked for rape, blackmail of MSc student A Kanpur constable has been booked for allegedly raping an MSc student after luring her with job and marriage promises. He filmed obscene videos and threatened to make them viral. FIR registered at Kotwali; police say the accused will be arrested soon. 10. ‘Dhurandhar' becomes first franchise to earn ₹3,000 crore worldwide Ranveer Singh-starrer films Dhurandhar and Dhurandhar 2 have together earned over ₹3,000 crore worldwide, making it the first Indian film franchise to cross the ₹3,000 crore mark.

stories.summary: BJP MLA Shyam Prakash stirred controversy after making remarks on idol worship and Dalit leadership at an Ambedkar Jayanti event in Hardoi. Addressing the gathering, Prakash said, Worshipping stones will get you nothing. If you must worship, then worship Yogi and Modi. From them, you will get something. Criticism of dalit leadership The Gopamau MLA said leaders who speak in the name of Dalits often work for their own interests. “No Dalit leader can ensure your welfare. Big leaders mislead people to secure power,” he said. Read what else the BJP MLA said ‘I have been in all parties’ Prakash added that his views were shaped by political experience. “I have drunk water from every ghat. I have been in all parties and seen everything. You have to establish yourself on your own,” he said. Praise for yogi, modi Praising Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, he said he considers “living people as God” and suggested they have the capacity to help people. Mla calls it personal opinion Responding to questions later, Prakash said the remarks reflected his personal views. He clarified that he was referring to stones kept unnecessarily in homes as family deities.

stories.title: Kanpur constable booked for rape, blackmail of MSc student:Lured victim with job and promise of marriage; filmed obscene videos of her
stories.summary: A constable in Kanpur has been booked for allegedly raping an MSc student after luring her with promises of a job and marriage, police said. The accused also filmed obscene photos and videos and later threatened to make them viral. FIR registered after complaint at Kotwali The student approached Kotwali police station late Monday night. Based on her complaint, an FIR has been registered against constable Yogendra Singh, who is posted at the Reserve Police Lines. Met on train, built trust with false assurances According to the victim, she met Yogendra on January 19, 2026, while travelling from Kanpur Central to Agra for an exam. During the journey, he claimed to be undergoing constable training and offered to help her get a job. The two exchanged numbers and stayed in touch. She alleged that Yogendra later proposed marriage and even spoke to her mother, assuring both a job and marriage. Assault, repeated threats over two months The student alleged that on February 22, the constable called her near the Reserve Police Lines and raped her. During the assault, he recorded obscene photos and videos. She said he continued to sexually assault her for nearly two months by threatening to leak the videos. On April 8, he allegedly raped her again and refused to marry or help her with a job, while repeating threats to make the videos viral. Police action underway Kotwali station in-charge Jagdish Prasad Pandey said an FIR has been registered and efforts are underway to arrest the accused. “He will be arrested and sent to jail soon,” he said.

stories.title: Kidney racket kingpin charged ₹30 lakh per transplant:‘Commando Surgery’ codeword used, Kanpur hub of illegal network
stories.summary: The alleged mastermind of the Kanpur kidney racket, Rohit Tiwari, has revealed key details during police interrogation, exposing how an organised network carried out illegal kidney transplants across multiple cities. ₹25–30 lakh per transplant, agents handled deals Police said Rohit charged between ₹25 lakh and ₹30 lakh for each transplant. He told investigators that agents arranged donors and recipients, while he managed hospitals and medical teams. The gang used the codeword “Commando Surgery” to refer to kidney transplants in conversations. Agents active across major cities The network included agents operating in Delhi, Mumbai, Kanpur, Prayagraj and Meerut. These agents brought cases to Rohit, who then decided the hospital, timing, and medical team for each operation. From factory worker to racket operator Rohit, a Class 12 pass from Hardoi, initially worked as a labourer in Ghaziabad. He later became a receptionist at a clinic in Meerut, where he came in contact with doctors linked to illegal transplant work. He then worked as a ward boy and gradually became involved in managing transplants. Kanpur hub identified for illegal surgeries After a dispute between two doctors, Rohit was given responsibility to arrange transplants in Kanpur. He identified Kalyanpur as a location where such operations could be conducted with ease. Over 30 transplants, multiple hospitals involved Police said several transplants were carried out at different hospitals, with more than 10 at one facility alone. Rohit claimed he had conducted over 30 transplants in Kanpur and nearby districts. Dedicated team handled surgeries Interrogation revealed that a team of five to six people carried out the procedures. Some handled anaesthesia, while others performed the transplant. The team would arrive, complete the surgery, and leave immediately. Donors found through Telegram, no direct contact Rohit said he avoided direct interaction with patients. Agents handled negotiations, while he used platforms like Telegram to find donors. He also managed logistics, including operation theatre preparation and scheduling. Large payments and spending trail In one case, a transplant deal was fixed at ₹60 lakh, out of which Rohit received ₹30 lakh. He used the money to pay team members and cover expenses. Police said he spent significant amounts on travel after such operations. Deaths and foreign patient under probe Investigators are also examining cases involving a foreign national and a patient who died after complications following surgery. Arrests made, search on for others Police tracked Rohit through his girlfriend after he went into hiding and destroyed his phones. Several accused, including doctors and associates, have been arrested. Raids are ongoing to trace other suspects. Rohit will be taken on remand for further questioning.

stories.title: Yogi unveils Noida film city plan:UP CM says Saharanpur youth won’t need to migrate; slams ‘divisive politics’
stories.summary: Travel between Delhi and Dehradun will now be completed in just two-and-a-half hours, significantly reducing travel time and boosting connectivity in western Uttar Pradesh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on Tuesday. He was addressing a gathering in Saharanpur on the occasion of the inauguration of the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway. A 135-kilometre stretch of the corridor passes through Uttar Pradesh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi travelled to Dehradun to formally inaugurate the project. Before that, the Prime Minister held a roadshow in Saharanpur, offered prayers at Maa Daat Kali temple, and inspected the wildlife corridor via helicopter. Governor Anandiben Patel, CM Yogi Adityanath, and Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak were also present. After the events in Saharanpur, the Prime Minister left for Dehradun, while CM Yogi and other leaders stayed back and watched the inauguration programme live from the venue. UP emerging as a hub of employment and security Addressing the gathering, Yogi said Uttar Pradesh has emerged as a new centre of employment, security, and investment under the “double-engine government”. He also noted that the day marked the 135th birth anniversary of Dr B R Ambedkar, who ensured equal rights for citizens through the Constitution. The Chief Minister announced that statues of social reformers such as Babasaheb Ambedkar, Ravidas Maharaj, and Maharishi Valmiki would be provided with protective canopies by the state government. Boost to western UP economy Yogi said the corridor would prove beneficial for districts such as Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Meerut, and Baghpat, helping local products gain wider recognition. He added that the improved connectivity would enable farmers and producers to access not only the national capital but also international markets. Political remarks without naming opposition Without naming any party, Yogi criticised those who “divide society on the basis of caste and family”, saying such forces cannot deliver development. He added that those who encouraged mafias and unrest in the past cannot be expected to provide employment or progress. Key features of the expressway The 213-kilometre Delhi–Dehradun Economic Corridor has been built at a cost of around ₹12,000 crore. Once operational, it will reduce travel time between the two cities from over six hours to about 2.5 hours. The project includes: Advanced traffic management systems A 12-kilometre elevated wildlife corridor — among the longest in Asia — has also been constructed to ensure safe animal movement and reduce human-wildlife conflict. Additionally, the expressway features multiple animal passes, elephant underpasses, and a 370-metre tunnel near the Daat Kali temple. Security and arrangements Ahead of the Prime Minister’s visit, elaborate security arrangements were made, with over 3,000 personnel deployed. The temple premises were decorated with flowers brought from Vrindavan and West Bengal, and special पूजा arrangements were made. The project is designed with a strong focus on environmental sustainability, incorporating measures to minimise ecological disruption while improving infrastructure.

stories.summary: UP Politics: डॉ. भीमराव आंबेडकर की 135वीं जयंती (14 अप्रैल 2026) पर उत्तर प्रदेश की सियासत गरम हो गई है। बहुजन समाज पार्टी ने लखनऊ में भव्य शक्ति प्रदर्शन की तैयारी की है। समाजवादी पार्टी और भाजपा भी बड़े कार्यक्रम आयोजित कर रही हैं। 2027 के विधानसभा चुनाव से ठीक पहले बाबा साहेब की जयंती क्यों अचानक इतनी अहम हो गई? इसका जवाब है, 21 फीसदी दलित वोट बैंक। यह वोट बैंक सीएम कुर्सी का गेमचेंजर साबित होता है। उत्तर प्रदेश में कुल 403 विधानसभा सीटें हैं। इनमें 84 सीटें अनुसूचित जाति के लिए आरक्षित हैं। दलित आबादी राज्य की कुल जनसंख्या का करीब 21 फीसदी है, यानी लगभग 3.20 करोड़ वोटर। ये वोट सिर्फ आरक्षित सीटों पर ही नहीं, बल्कि 150 से ज्यादा सामान्य सीटों पर भी निर्णायक हैं। पूर्वांचल और बुंदेलखंड में कई सीटों पर दलित वोटर 30 फीसदी से ज्यादा हैं। अगर दलित वोट एक तरफ हो जाए, तो 80-100 सीटें सीधे प्रभावित होती हैं।

stories.title: Sara Ali Khan explores snow-covered hills in Uttarakhand’s Tehri:Walks 18 km, camps overnight in remote area
stories.summary: Bollywood actress Sara Ali Khan trekked in the snowy hills of Uttarakhand. She walked 18 kilometers in Tehri. She witnessed snowfall and beautiful valleys in Panwali Kantha Bugyal. She spent the night in a tent amidst heavy snowfall. She enjoyed local mountain food, spending time with the locals. Trekker Kuldeep Rawat informed that Sara Ali Khan arrived in Ghuttu, Tehri on April 11. She stayed here for 3 days and left on Monday, April 13. Sara started an approximately 18-kilometer long trek from Gwana village. This trek passes through natural beauty, dense forests, and high mountains. He mentioned that during the trek, Sara spent the night at a place called Dophan. There are no hotel or restaurant facilities in this area. Because of this, Sara spent the night staying in a tent. Sara spent time with the local people. She got to know the mountain culture up close. While returning, she said - "It is always beautiful to come to Uttarakhand. It is very beautiful. Coming here is very exciting and peaceful. I will come here again." See Pictures- Sara enjoyed trekking through dense forests and high mountains. She relished the natural beauty. Sara ate red rice, Mandua roti, and Lingdi vegetable Sara visited Rudranath Dham in October Sara Ali Khan visited Rudranath Dham, the fourth Kedar located in Chamoli, in October before its gates closed. During this time, Sara walked 20 kilometers to reach the temple. Sara started her journey from Gangol village in Gopeshwar, Chamoli. After that, a day later, she reached Lwinti Bugyal, where after an overnight stay, she resumed trekking and then reached Rudranath Baba's temple. Throughout this entire journey, Sara passed through many rocky and narrow paths, and in between, she met many local villagers who were very happy to see Sara. Sara Ali Khan stopped at hut-like dhabas during trekking, drank tea, and conversed with local people. She learned about the religious beliefs, folk life, and traditional cuisines of the place. The actress was greatly impressed by the natural beauty of the mountains and the rural culture, calling it a memorable experience. Sara Ali Khan has visited Kedarnath many times Sara Ali Khan has a special connection with Kedarnath Dham. After the making of the film 'Kedarnath', she has visited the shrine many times for darshan and has been performing puja without any hindrance so far. However, after the proposed new system is implemented, she may also have to follow the prescribed procedure like other devotees. Sara's first spiritual and professional connection with Kedarnath happened in 2017 during the shooting of her debut film 'Kedarnath'. Since then, she has been continuously visiting here. In October 2024, just before Diwali, she performed puja at Kedarnath temple and shared photos. In 2023, she visited the shrine twice, performing darshan at Kedarnath and Tungnath on May 6, 2023, while about six months later, in October 2023, she again reached Kedarnath. Additionally, in November 2021, Sara Ali Khan also visited Kedarnath for darshan with her friend and actress Janhvi Kapoor.

stories.title: Caste politics takes centre stage on Ambedkar Jayanti:Mayawati shows strength in Lucknow, BJP unveils statue scheme
stories.summary: Caste equations play a decisive role in Uttar Pradesh politics, no party can secure power without the support of the Scheduled Castes. On 14 April, the birth anniversary of B. R. Ambedkar, all major parties, including BJP, SP, BSP and Congress, are organising events to engage with Dalit voters. In the lead-up to this, Congress held programmes on the birth anniversary of Jagjivan Ram, the country’s only Dalit Deputy Prime Minister, as well as on social reformer Jyotiba Phule. The Uttar Pradesh government has announced the Dr Ambedkar Statue Development Scheme, while the Samajwadi Party (SP) plans to conduct door-to-door campaigns centred on the Constitution. These initiatives are clearly aimed at consolidating the Dalit vote bank. Why the Dalit vote matters ? Dalits constitute approximately 20–21% of Uttar Pradesh’s population. Of the total Assembly seats, 84 are reserved for Scheduled Castes, but their influence extends beyond these constituencies, affecting outcomes in over 124 seats. Senior journalist Ratan Mani Lal notes that since the political weakening of Mayawati after 2012, there has been no single dominant Dalit leader capable of unifying the community. As a result, all parties are competing to attract Dalit voters. Senior journalist Akhilesh Bajpai adds that Dalit communities revere Ambedkar almost as a deity. Parties that consistently honour his legacy tend to find greater acceptance among Dalit voters. BJP’s strategy: Schemes and Symbolism The BJP-led Uttar Pradesh government has announced the Dr B.R. Ambedkar Statue Development Scheme. Under this, ₹1 crore will be allocated in each Assembly constituency for the conservation and beautification of 10 memorials dedicated to Ambedkar and other social reformers. Across the state, garlanding ceremonies and seminars will be organised at Ambedkar memorials. In Lucknow, for the first time, 11,000 lamps will be lit at Ambedkar’s memorial at Hazratganj, an initiative led by BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary. A seminar is also scheduled for 15 April at Ambedkar’s urn site, to be addressed by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Last year’s approach: In 2025, BJP organised cleaning and garlanding drives at Ambedkar memorials and ran the ‘Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Samman Abhiyan’ from 13 to 25 April. BSP: Demonstrating core strength The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) plans to showcase its core voter base on Ambedkar Jayanti. Its main programme will be held at the Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Social Transformation Site in Gomtinagar, Lucknow. Party workers and officials from 18 divisions across Uttar Pradesh have been invited along with their families. Leaders, including state president Vishwanath Pal, zonal coordinators, district presidents and Assembly in-charges, will attend. The gathering is expected to draw between 150,000 and 200,000 participants. Interestingly, BSP chief Mayawati and her nephew Akash Anand will not attend the main event. Instead, Mayawati will pay floral tribute to Ambedkar at her Mall Avenue residence at 8 AM and issue a message to party workers. Akash Anand will be in Chhattisgarh. Last year’s approach: BSP organised events in Noida and Lucknow, drawing workers from 6 and 12 divisions respectively. This year, all divisions are converging in Lucknow. SP: Constitution-centric outreach The Samajwadi Party is focusing on Ambedkar’s constitutional legacy. It plans to organise seminars in every village, discussing his life and ideas while targeting the BJP through 'Constitution dialogues'. SP leaders will tell voters that the BJP intends to alter the Constitution and weaken reservation policies. Party chief Akhilesh Yadav is expected to hold a press conference as part of the campaign. Last year’s approach: Akhilesh Yadav garlanded Ambedkar’s statue in Lucknow and emphasised that unity among PDA (Pichda, Dalit, Alpasankhyak—Backward, Dalit and Minority groups) is essential to safeguard the Constitution and reservation. Changing Dalit voting patterns 2017 Assembly Elections- The BJP fielded candidates in 85 of 86 reserved seats and won 75, indicating a major shift of Dalit voters away from BSP. 2022 Assembly Elections- The BJP contested all 86 seats but won 63, suggesting that some Dalit votes had shifted towards SP. 2024 Lok Sabha Elections- Out of 17 SC-reserved seats in Uttar Pradesh, SP won 7. Chandrashekhar Azad won from Nagina, while Congress candidates secured victories in Barabanki and Sitapur. This reflected a relative decline in the BJP’s performance among Dalit voters. SP’s PDA formula and BJP’s concerns SP is continuing with its PDA strategy, uniting Backward Classes, Dalits and minorities, which proved effective in recent elections. The party is emphasising slogans such as 'Save the Constitution' and 'Protect Reservation' to attract Dalit voters. Meanwhile, dissatisfaction among Dalits regarding their representation in government, party organisations, the Legislative Council and the Rajya Sabha has added to the BJP’s concerns. Expert views: Symbolism and Strategy Akhilesh Bajpai highlights that symbols play a crucial role in politics. Ambedkar represents not only Dalits but also broader marginalised communities. Political parties understand that invoking his legacy resonates deeply with these groups. Ratan Mani Lal observes that Mayawati has become active again after a period of relative silence. There are signs of renewed Dalit inclination towards her leadership. This sends a strong message to both BJP and SP: if Dalit votes consolidate behind BSP or split into multiple directions, it could significantly alter electoral outcomes.

stories.title: How Noida factory workers' protest turned violent without leadership?:Communication gap fuelled unrest, rumours of rejected demands triggered escalation
stories.summary: Factory workers in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, had been protesting for three days, demanding a wage increase. On Monday, the agitation escalated into violence, with hundreds of workers taking to the streets carrying sticks and batons. Protesters pelted stones and vandalised more than 350 factories across multiple areas. Over 150 vehicles were damaged, more than 50 were set on fire, and several police vehicles were overturned. Police personnel were also targeted, with around 30 people reported injured. Authorities have registered cases against 60 individuals so far. The violent escalation has significantly disrupted industrial activity, with factory owners estimating losses of nearly ₹3,000 crore due to halted operations and damage. Allegations of instigation and administrative gaps Factory owners have alleged that workers were provoked into violence. Meanwhile, a lack of effective communication between the administration and labourers is being seen as a critical factor behind the unrest. Notably, workers were reportedly not informed about a key meeting held on Sunday, where their demands had allegedly been addressed. This communication failure has raised concerns over administrative handling of the situation. The primary trigger for the protest was a decision by the Haryana government. On 9 April, it approved a 35% increase in minimum wages, with notification issued on 10 April. Following this, workers in Noida’s industrial belt began demanding similar wage hikes. Wage comparison- Haryana- Unskilled: ₹11,275 → ₹15,220 Semi-skilled: ₹12,430 → ₹16,780 Skilled: ₹13,704 → ₹18,500 Highly skilled: ₹14,389 → ₹19,425 Uttar Pradesh (Noida)- Unskilled workers earn around ₹11,313 Daily wages- Haryana: ₹580–₹750 Noida: ₹435–₹535 How did events unfolded ? 10–11 April Around 1,000 workers began protesting at Hosiery Complex and Surajpur–Dadri Road. Tensions escalated following a police lathi-charge. The matter reached Lucknow, and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed officials to resolve it within 24 hours. 12 April Noida District Magistrate Medha Roopam and labour officials met industry representatives. Companies were instructed to comply with labour laws and ensure timely wage payments. A control room was established. 13 April (Monday) Workers remained dissatisfied, as no concrete decision was taken on wage increases. By morning, thousands gathered, and the protest turned violent. Why did the protest turn violent? At around 9 AM, approximately 300–400 workers gathered outside the Motherson company in Sector-81, Phase-2. The protest had no formal leadership, with workers organising themselves. During sloganeering, frustration grew over the lack of response to their demands. A rumour then spread that their demands would not be accepted, triggering anger. Stone-pelting and arson soon followed. Workers entered several factories, halted operations, and forced employees to leave. Female workers reportedly hid under benches in fear and later returned home after the situation calmed. Social media further fuelled tensions, with false reports of deaths and injuries circulating widely. Administrative lapse and communication gap A crucial meeting was held on Sunday at the Noida Authority, attended by officials from the administration, police, and industry. The meeting was chaired by CEO Krishna Karunesh, with Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh and DM Medha Roopam present. Senior officials, including Principal Secretary (Labour) MKS Sundaram and Labour Commissioner Markandey Shahi, joined virtually. Key decisions included strict enforcement of minimum wages, timely payments, equal pay for equal work, overtime compensation, EPF-ESI benefits, gratuity, and workplace safety under new labour codes. However, workers were not informed of these decisions until Monday morning. This information gap significantly contributed to the escalation of unrest. Hour-by-hour escalation of violence 9:00 AM – Motherson Gate (Phase-2) The protest began with 300–400 workers. The situation quickly turned violent, with four police vehicles vandalised and set ablaze. Around 10 other vehicles were also torched. Police used tear gas, and PAC and RAF forces were deployed. 10:00 AM – Streets Blocked Within an hour, hundreds of workers from Sectors 1–6 took to the streets, blocking DSC Road and halting traffic towards Delhi for nearly an hour before police cleared the route. 1:00 PM – Sector-57 Rampage Around 600 individuals armed with sticks and stones targeted industries in B-Block, Sector-57. More than 50 factories were vandalised within 30–35 minutes. Police presence proved insufficient, necessitating RAF deployment. 3:00 PM – Arson in Sector-63 Vehicles outside Vipul Motors were set on fire. Reports of vandalism continued from Labour Chowk to Sectors 62, 63, and 65. Fire services eventually brought the blaze under control. Most rioters were aged between 18 and 25 and carried sticks, stones, petrol-filled bottles, and even firecrackers to create smoke. Business Impact: ₹3,000 crore loss According to Sudhir Srivastava of the Noida Entrepreneurs Association, about 80% of industries were operational in the morning. However, by afternoon, most units shut down as mobs entered factories, halted production, and forced workers out. Business losses are estimated at around ₹3,000 crore in a single day. Industry representatives claim that workers have been influenced or incited. Police action and digital investigation Uttar Pradesh DGP Rajiv Krishna stated that over 50 bot handles had been identified, created within 24 hours to spread misinformation and provoke unrest. The Special Task Force (STF) will investigate the digital trail, with initial findings suggesting an organised attempt to create panic. Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh said- Around 42,000 workers protested at 83 locations. Violence occurred at only two sites, while 78 locations were peacefully resolved through negotiations. She added that individuals from outside districts attempted to incite violence, and arrests have been made. Others are being identified through CCTV footage Additional CP (Law and Order) Rajiv Narayan Mishra confirmed that cases have been registered against 60 individuals, with around 200 detained.

stories.title: Fresh protest erupts in Noida, stone-pelting at police:Paramilitary forces deployed; Rahul Gandhi calls it workers’ 'last cry'
stories.summary: Factory workers in Noida (Gautam Buddh Nagar) again took to the streets on Tuesday, demanding higher wages. Clashes broke out when police attempted to stop them. In two to three locations, the crowd pelted stones at police vehicles. The situation was brought under control shortly, and protesters were dispersed. Police and paramilitary forces have been conducting flag marches in industrial areas since 5 AM. Monitoring is being carried out through CCTV cameras and drones. Additionally, 15 companies of PAC and RAF, along with 26 officers (8 Additional SPs and 18 DSPs), have been deployed in Noida. Most companies remain shut. The Uttar Pradesh government increased minimum wages by up to ₹3,000 late Monday night, effective from 1 April, following a high-level committee meeting with workers. Strict warning from police DGP Rajiv Krishna is monitoring the situation from the Lucknow control room. He said strict action will be taken against those involved in violence and arson, and losses will be recovered from those responsible. Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh said over 300 arrests have been made. Several groups spreading rumours have been identified, with some individuals found active at multiple locations. Around 50 X accounts were used to incite violence. Rahul Gandhi said the unrest reflected workers’ ‘last cry’ after being ignored. On Monday, 42,000 workers vandalised over 350 factories, set more than 50 vehicles ablaze, damaged 150, and pelted stones at police. See photos from today's protest- Recap of Monday’s violence On Monday, factory workers staged violent protests across various parts of Noida. Around 42,000 workers, who had been agitating since 9 April over wage demands, came out onto the streets. They vandalised more than 350 factories, set over 50 vehicles on fire, and damaged around 150 others. Police personnel were also targeted with stone-pelting during the unrest. stories.title: ATS to probe 26 arson cases over terror link:NIA issues lookout notices against three suspected terrorists
stories.summary: The Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) in Uttar Pradesh will investigate around 26 incidents of arson across the state from a terror perspective. This decision follows inputs obtained from four suspected terrorists recently arrested in Lucknow. Many of these cases, involving vehicles catching fire in different districts, were previously treated as accidents. They will now be re-examined in detail. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) will also be involved in the probe. Arrest of 4 suspects in Lucknow The Uttar Pradesh ATS arrested four individuals in Lucknow on 2 April, before they could execute a major planned attack. During interrogation, it emerged that they had been carrying out small-scale arson incidents, recording videos, and sending them to handlers in Pakistan. The suspects were identified as Saqib alias Devil (the alleged gang leader), Vikas Gehlawat alias Raunak, Lokesh alias Babu alias Papla Pandit, and Arbab. Investigators recovered several key pieces of evidence from their mobile phones, which are now central to the ongoing inquiry. Arson as ‘proof of work’ for handlers According to investigators, the accused used these minor arson incidents as “trial runs” to demonstrate their capabilities. They would film the incidents and send the footage to a Pakistani handler identified as Abu Bakar. In return, they allegedly received payments via QR code-based transactions. Authorities believe their objective was to create fear and communal tension through repeated small-scale incidents. Reinvestigation of past incidents ADG Law and Order Amitabh Yash stated that fire incidents are often reported as accidental. However, after discovering a possible link between arson and financial transactions, authorities have begun reviewing cases from the past six months. A total of 26 incidents across districts, including Aligarh, Ghaziabad, Bulandshahr, Kanpur, Bareilly, and Prayagraj, have been identified for re-examination. In one confirmed instance, the accused allegedly set fire to a pickup truck in the Kiratpur area on 4 March and recorded the act. Investigators are now analysing seven mobile phones recovered from the suspects to trace the location, timing, and details of similar incidents. Forensic challenges in old cases The probe is expected to be complex, as many of the incidents are several months old. Authorities may face difficulties in retrieving forensic evidence or CCTV footage. Records of arson incidents involving vehicles, shops, and small establishments in districts such as Bulandshahr, Bijnor, Meerut, Baghpat, and Hapur are being reviewed. In the absence of strong physical evidence, statements from residents are likely to play a critical role. Financial trail under scrutiny Investigators have uncovered suspicious transactions in the bank accounts of the accused. These are now being matched with the dates of arson incidents to establish a direct link between payments and criminal acts. This financial trail is expected to provide crucial evidence regarding the operational structure and external support for the network. Links to wider network and foreign handlers During the investigation, ATS identified several suspicious phone numbers linked to other states. This information has been shared with the NIA. Some of these contacts are reportedly based in Maharashtra. Additionally, videos recovered from the suspects’ phones show other individuals carrying weapons. These individuals have been identified as Aakib, Mahjul, Azad, and Ubaid Malik. A case has been registered against them in Bijnor through a central agency. Lookout notices have been issued for Mahjul, believed to be in South Africa, and Aakib and Azad, reportedly based in Saudi Arabia. Use of encrypted communication tools The accused allegedly used multiple methods to communicate with their Pakistani handler- Planned attack on Lucknow Railway Station According to ATS officials, the group had planned a major attack targeting infrastructure near Lucknow Railway Station. Their objective was to damage the signal system and cause a large-scale explosion on 2 April, potentially leading to significant casualties. However, the ATS acted on prior intelligence and arrested the suspects before the plan could be executed. Online radicalisation and bomb-making searches Analysis of the suspects’ mobile phones revealed concerning online activity. Their YouTube search history included queries such as 'How to make a time bomb?', ‘How to make a chemical bomb?’, and 'What are the techniques for accurate targeting?'. Investigators also found that their handler, Abu Bakar, had shared links and instructional videos. The extent of their technical preparedness will become clearer after the completion of their five-day police remand.
