stories.title: PM Modi inaugurates Delhi–Dehradun Expressway:Says, 'women’s rights priority for 2029 polls; calls infrastructure ‘Modi’s guarantee’
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday inaugurated the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway corridor. On the occasion, he said that there was a time when villagers in Uttarakhand had to wait generations for roads, but under the double-engine government’s efforts, connectivity is now reaching even remote villages. He added that areas which were once deserted are now becoming inhabited again. The Prime Minister said that if seen in terms of national development, roads, highways, airways, railways and waterways are the “lifelines of the nation”. He described these as not just present-day facilities but a “guarantee of Modi” for future generations. He also reiterated the government’s commitment to ensuring women’s rights, stating that steps are being taken in Parliament to secure their due representation by 2029. See pictures- Longstanding association with Uttarakhand Since assuming office in 2014, Modi has maintained a strong connection with Uttarakhand. His first visit to the state as Prime Minister was on 11 September 2015, when he met Swami Dayanand Giri in Rishikesh. Over the years, he has frequently visited prominent religious sites, including Kedarnath, Badrinath, Mukhba, and Adi Kailash, reflecting both administrative and spiritual engagement with the region. Expressway designed for seamless travel The Delhi–Dehradun Expressway has been developed with a focus on uninterrupted and efficient travel. A total of 14 wayside facilities have been established along the route, offering amenities such as parking, food courts, toilets, and essential services. These facilities are intended to minimize the need for frequent stops during long journeys. Additionally, the corridor includes seven interchanges, enabling smooth connectivity to various cities and highways, thereby improving accessibility across the region. Advanced engineering and infrastructure A key feature of the expressway is its 18.6-kilometre elevated corridor, designed to allow traffic to bypass congested and environmentally sensitive areas. The project also includes 19 major underpasses, 57 minor underpasses, and four significant bridges, ensuring both smooth vehicular movement and preservation of local connectivity. To support local communities, service roads have been constructed alongside the expressway. Safety measures such as secure U-turns, crash barriers, and an Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS) have been implemented to enhance monitoring, traffic control, and emergency response capabilities. Travel time reduced to 2.5 hours The expressway is set to dramatically reduce travel time between Delhi and Dehradun. Currently, the journey via the traditional route, covering approximately 235 kilometres through Delhi, Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Roorkee, and onward, typically takes around six hours due to congestion and mixed traffic conditions. With the new expressway, the distance will decrease to approximately 212 kilometres, saving around 23 kilometres. More importantly, travel time is expected to be reduced to just 2.5 hours, offering a faster and more predictable journey. Regions set to benefit The expressway will significantly improve connectivity across Delhi-NCR, Western Uttar Pradesh, and Uttarakhand. Areas in East Delhi, such as Akshardham and Sonia Vihar, will gain high-speed access, potentially boosting employment opportunities and real estate development. Districts including Baghpat, Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, and Saharanpur in Western Uttar Pradesh will be directly linked, benefiting sectors such as sugarcane farming, agro-industries, and logistics. In Uttarakhand, Dehradun will receive a direct six-lane connection, while Haridwar, Roorkee, and Rishikesh will be connected via spur routes, supporting tourism and religious travel. Asia’s longest wildlife corridor One of the most notable aspects of the project is the wildlife corridor passing through Rajaji National Park and the Shivalik forest range. This includes an approximately 12-kilometre elevated stretch, allowing animals to move freely beneath the roadway. Special measures have been implemented to protect wildlife, including noise barriers and light control systems to minimise disturbance during night-time. These provisions aim to preserve the natural habitat while maintaining infrastructure efficiency. Key features of the wildlife corridor Boost to tourism and business The expressway is expected to significantly enhance tourism by reducing travel time from Delhi-NCR to popular destinations such as Mussoorie, Rishikesh, Haridwar, Dhanaulti, and Chakrata. Improved access via the Haridwar–Rishikesh spur will also facilitate travel to major religious events and sites, including the Kumbh, Char Dham pilgrimage, and Ganga bathing ghats. From a commercial perspective, the expressway will connect industrial hubs in Delhi-NCR with those in Western Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, including Roorkee, Haridwar, Saharanpur, and Muzaffarnagar. This is expected to streamline freight movement, reduce logistics costs, and create new investment opportunities in sectors such as FMCG, pharmaceuticals, automotive components, and agriculture. Toll structure and charges Toll rates for the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway have been set at approximately ₹3 per kilometre for cars. For a full journey from Delhi to Dehradun, motorists will pay around ₹675 for a one-way trip. If the return journey is completed within 24 hours, the return toll is reduced to ₹335. For light commercial vehicles such as minibuses, the one-way toll is approximately ₹1,100. Larger buses and trucks will be charged around ₹2,275, while heavier vehicles may incur tolls of up to ₹4,000. Standard toll exemptions applicable to other expressways will also apply here. Transformational project for North India Overall, the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway is poised to be a transformative infrastructure project for North India. By significantly reducing travel time and improving connectivity, it is expected to drive growth in tourism, commerce, and regional development, while also incorporating environmentally sensitive design features.

stories.title: ‘Multiple WhatsApp groups created overnight to incite Noida violence’:Commissioner says crowds gathered from nearby villages, over 150 detained
stories.summary: Authorities in Uttar Pradesh’s Gautam Buddh Nagar district (Noida/Greater Noida) have suggested that a ‘deep conspiracy’ may have fuelled the violent protests that erupted on Monday. According to Noida Police, those involved in arson and vandalism were not factory workers but miscreants posing as employees. Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh, speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, said there was ‘a strong indication of a large and organised conspiracy’. She noted that the situation had earlier calmed down, but violence suddenly reignited when unidentified groups, allegedly not labourers, emerged from nearby villages and began rioting. Sudden escalation raises questions The abrupt shift from a peaceful protest to widespread violence has raised several questions: how did the situation spiral so quickly, who orchestrated it, and whether intelligence agencies had prior inputs. There is also uncertainty about the actual target of the protest, whether it was company management, contractors, the administration, or the government. WhatsApp groups used to incite violence Commissioner Singh revealed that thousands of WhatsApp groups were allegedly created overnight to mobilise and radicalise workers. Employees were reportedly added via QR codes and incited to turn the protest aggressive. She added that the police had remained vigilant following similar unrest in Haryana and had deployed forces at sensitive locations. However, there was no prior indication of external elements being involved, which allowed the situation to deteriorate briefly before it was brought under control. Over 150 detained, probe underway More than 150 individuals have been taken into custody in connection with the violence. Police are interrogating them to determine how many are actual employees and how many are outsiders. Investigators are also examining the motives of those involved and whether any organised groups were behind the unrest. Leaderless protest added to chaos Sources indicate that the protest, which had been ongoing for four days since 9 April, had no identifiable leadership. Workers from various companies would gather at a common location, gradually swelling the crowd. When officials attempted dialogue on the first day, several participants refused to engage, stating they were not leaders. This absence of leadership appears to have complicated negotiations and crowd management. Government claims prior agreement The Uttar Pradesh government maintains that discussions had already taken place with workers and agreements were reached on several demands. However, some protesters argue that the agreement reflected only employees’ views and lacked the consent of industry owners. Workers insist that unless employers agree to key demands, such as minimum wages, an eight-hour workday, overtime pay, and night duty allowances, any agreement remains incomplete. They also claim these issues had been raised with the Deputy Labour Commissioner three to four months earlier, who had assured action, but no progress was made. No clear organisational or political link So far, no major organisation has publicly claimed responsibility for leading the protest. However, there are inputs suggesting that some office bearers of the Centre of Indian Trade Unions may have supported the agitation from behind the scenes. Officials state that no direct political connection has been established. Nonetheless, the protest spread beyond Noida to Greater Noida, Faridabad, and Ghaziabad, indicating a broader mobilisation. Workers cite low wages and exploitation Workers allege they are paid as little as ₹10,000–₹12,000 per month, which they say is insufficient amid rising inflation. They claim they are made to work up to 12 hours a day without overtime pay and face additional forms of exploitation. Despite the reported agreement on Sunday, dissatisfaction persisted among sections of workers, some of whom either rejected the terms or continued protesting in what authorities describe as a planned manner. Government response and measures The Noida Police have launched a detailed investigation into the violence. A high-level committee has been formed to examine workers’ demands and has already reached Noida. CM Yogi Adityanath has directed that workers must receive fair wages and adequate safety measures. He emphasised maintaining round-the-clock communication in industrial areas and called for strict action against those attempting to disrupt law and order. Appeal for calm and workplace reforms The administration has urged workers to ignore rumours and maintain peace. Noida District Magistrate Medha Rupam stated that key decisions have been taken following meetings with companies. These include the formation of workplace committees to prevent sexual harassment, chaired by women, installation of complaint boxes, ensuring respectful treatment of employees, mandatory salary payments by the 10th of each month, and provision of salary slips. Authorities continue efforts to stabilise the situation while addressing both the alleged conspiracy and the workers’ grievances.

stories.title: Court questions if Shankaracharya case is false:Ashutosh Maharaj and disciples gave different dates of misconduct; order issued in 11 points
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has granted bail to Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, while raising serious questions about the case filed against him. The court pointed out inconsistencies in the statements, noting that the batuk boys mentioned January 18 as the date of the incident, while complainant Ashutosh Maharaj cited January 24. The court also questioned why the children were not placed under proper care and why they approached Ashutosh Maharaj first, despite not knowing him earlier. It observed that, usually, children report such incidents to their family members first. Taking note of these issues, the court said the matter requires careful examination to determine whether the case is genuine or false, while granting bail to the Shankaracharya. Court asked Ashutosh Maharaj - Why did you come after 6 days 1. The case was registered on the order of POCSO court. The case was registered on the petition of that person (Ashutosh Maharaj), who claims to be the alleged guardian of the disciples. 2. The disciples mentioned the incident of January 18, while Ashutosh Maharaj mentioned the incident of January 24. The court asked that when the incident happened on January 18, why did you come after 6 days? When asked, Ashutosh Maharaj replied that he was busy in yagna and worship. The court said - This is no answer, you should have come immediately. 3. If the victim child Batuk was in touch with Ashutosh Maharaj, then why was he not given proper custody until January 25th. This is a violation of the POCSO Act, because in cases involving children, the victim should be immediately handed over to police custody. So that their medical examination can be conducted properly. The victim of misconduct will first tell their family about the pain 4. The most shocking fact is that when an incident happens with a child, they first tell their family or parents. Whereas the Batuks did not know Ashutosh Maharaj beforehand, as Ashutosh Maharaj had said that the Batuks came running to him, and in such a case the Batuks told an unknown person, i.e., Ashutosh Maharaj. The court said that this is against human behavior. A victim of misconduct will first tell their family about the pain. 5. Ashutosh Maharaj stated the incident occurred at Mahakumbh and Magh Mela, whereas the victim Batuks stated it happened in Narsinghpur, Madhya Pradesh and Badrinath, Uttarakhand. Thus, there is a contradiction. 6. A discrepancy came to light in the birth date of one of the boys. One boy became a major, i.e., an adult, on August 1, 2026. Whereas when the incident occurred, he was a minor. The certificates that came forward showed differences. The boys were not students of Shankaracharya's ashram, the claim proved false 7. Ashutosh Maharaj had claimed that both the victim boys were students of Shankaracharya's ashram. The investigation revealed that both were studying at a Sanskrit school in Hardoi. Whereas Ashutosh Maharaj had claimed that misconduct was happening at Shankaracharya's ashram. 8. In the medical report, doctors wrote that there is no external injury on the private part. However, sexual assault harassment (misconduct) cannot be ruled out either. Doctors said that FSL examination should be conducted. The court said to the doctors that you also asked for the FSL report and also claimed that misconduct cannot be ruled out... what does this mean. The doctors did not give a conclusive report that misconduct has occurred. 9. When allegations of misconduct were made against Shankaracharya, why was Shankaracharya's medical examination not done, whereas in POCSO cases, medical examination of both the victim child and the accused is mandatory. Is this a false case 10. The FIR was filed when a commotion occurred on Mauni Amavasya. A dispute arose between the Prayagraj administration and the accused, i.e., the Shankaracharya. Where were the victim children, their families, or the alleged guardians before this? The matter did not come to light earlier. 11. The court said - In such a situation, these incidents and the FIR need to be examined carefully. That is, it needs to be examined point-by-point whether this is a false case or not. Big relief for Shankaracharya from High Court decision The anticipatory bail of Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati was granted by the Allahabad High Court on Wednesday. The court said that Shankaracharya will not be arrested until the chargesheet is filed. This decision was pronounced by the bench of Justice Jitendra Kumar Sinha of the High Court at 3:45 PM in the afternoon. The Allahabad High Court has also imposed conditions while granting bail to Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand. The most important condition is that both parties (Shankaracharya and Ashutosh) will not make statements in the media and will not give interviews. There is also a ban on Shankaracharya going abroad. Permission will have to be taken from the High Court for this. If the bail conditions are violated, the other party can file a bail cancellation petition. While pronouncing this decision, Shankaracharya's lawyers said - Your Honor, also say something about this that someone starts roaming around with children, someone makes statements during the journey. This should also be stopped. On this, the court said that this should not be violated. Shankaracharya has got great relief from the High Court's decision. Ashutosh Maharaj will go to Supreme Court for Shankaracharya's arrest Ashutosh Maharaj's spokesperson Reena N. Singh said - The High Court has granted bail to Avimukteshwaranand. Despite this, our fight for justice will continue. We are dissatisfied with this order. We will knock on the doors of the Supreme Court for justice. We are committed to protecting dharma. We will go to the Supreme Court for Shankaracharya's arrest. Chargesheet has to be filed within 90 days If the accused is in jail, the police must file the chargesheet within 90 days in any case. Otherwise, the court demands an explanation. However, if the accused is not arrested, the police can take some time in the name of investigation. But, the police will have to explain the reason for this. Now know what a chargesheet is A chargesheet is the report that the police submit to the court after completing the investigation. It states what the accused did? What evidence is there against them? Under which laws will the case be made? After this, the court decides whether the case will proceed or not. In simple words, chargesheet directly means that the police have completed their work. Now the court has to make the decision.

stories.title: Noida violence linked to Pakistan-based social media:Commissioner says workers incited through X and WhatsApp groups
stories.summary: Police investigating the recent violence in Noida have identified three key conspirators. Two of them—Rupesh Rai and Manisha Chauhan—have been arrested, while Aditya Anand remains absconding. According to police, all three were present in Noida during the violence and played an active role in instigating workers. Organisations and Digital networks under scanner Three organisations have come under scrutiny, including ‘Mazdoor Bigul Dasta’, allegedly led by Rupesh Rai. The group is suspected of mobilising workers and provoking them into violent protests. Investigators also found two suspicious X (formerly Twitter) handles—‘Meer Ilayasi’ and ‘Ayushi Tiwari’—which were allegedly operated from Pakistan and had been active for the past three months. Sources say Virtual Private Networks (VPNs) were used to conceal their origin. Police have sought backend data for further analysis. WhatsApp groups used to incite violence Police revealed that the accused created WhatsApp groups on April 9 and 10 to mobilise workers. Through these groups, members were allegedly incited to take to the streets, engage in arson, and vandalise property. Using digital platforms, a large number of workers were mobilised. From April 13, around 42,000 employees protesting for higher wages joined the agitation. Two days of violence and damage The protests soon turned violent, with workers pelting stones at factories, vandalising property, and setting vehicles on fire in multiple areas. More than 50 vehicles were reportedly torched during the unrest, which continued for two days. Commissioner details Pakistan link Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh said that data obtained from the platform indicated the two X handles were being operated from Pakistan. She added that misleading information was circulated through electronic means on April 13 with the intent to disturb public order, creating fear and anger among residents across Gautam Buddh Nagar. Arrests and Legal action So far, police have arrested 62 individuals, including alleged conspirators and those involved in arson and rioting. All have been sent to jail. A total of 13 cases have been registered in connection with the violence. Police said further investigation is underway. Background: Workers’ grievances Workers had been protesting over low wages, claiming they were being paid ₹10,000–₹12,000 per month despite working 12-hour shifts, with no overtime compensation. Although an agreement was reportedly reached earlier, some workers remained dissatisfied, while police suspect that certain elements deliberately escalated the situation. Government announces wage hike Following the unrest, the Uttar Pradesh government announced a hike in minimum wages for factory workers by up to ₹3,000. The revised wages will be effective from April 1. A high-level committee held late-night discussions with worker representatives before the decision was approved.

stories.title: Dismissed constable burns elderly man alive:Hatched plot in Hathras to fake his own death; was absconding in a murder case
stories.summary: To avoid going to jail in Hathras, the accused dismissed constable fabricated a false story of his death. He placed his Aadhar card, mobile, and other documents in the pocket of a person, then burned him alive to death. However, while burning him alive, the accused constable also got severely burnt. For two days, he secretly received treatment at Hathras District Hospital, but when his condition worsened, he was referred to Saifai Medical College. Meanwhile, upon finding the body and seeing the partially burnt Aadhar card, the police initially presumed the constable to be dead. But suspicion arose when a beggar, who was seen at the railway station, suddenly disappeared. The police investigated in the constable's village. During this time, information was received about a severely burnt person admitted to the district hospital under the constable's name. The police became alert. Upon investigation, it was revealed that the constable was alive and the deceased was a beggar seen in the area around the railway station. According to the police, the constable committed the crime on March 12. After learning about his conspiracy, the police were waiting for him to recover. He was arrested on Wednesday after being discharged from Saifai Medical College. The accused constable has been identified as Ramveer Singh (55) from Baghauni village in Mainpuri. He was dismissed from the UP Police in 2013. He had 13 cases registered against him, including murder, during his duty. Now know the full story GRP in-charge Suyash Singh said- Ramveer Singh was a UP Police constable but was dismissed due to his criminal tendencies. After his dismissal, he was absconding. Police were looking for him. To avoid arrest and jail, he hatched a conspiracy. He was looking for a person who had no acquaintances. On the Hathras platform, he saw a beggar of his own build. After seeing the beggar, he made a dangerous plan. In fact, on March 12, when the Hathras platform became deserted at night, he executed his plan by pouring kerosene oil on the sleeping beggar and burning him alive. To mislead the police, he left his half-burnt Aadhaar card and burnt mobile phone there. However, while burning the beggar alive, the dismissed constable also got severely burnt. For two days, the constable kept buying and taking medicine from various medical stores, but when the burning sensation became unbearable, he got admitted to Hathras District Hospital. However, considering his condition, doctors referred him to Saifai Medical College on March 14 itself. Police suspected the disappearance of the platform beggar Meanwhile, the police started further proceedings, assuming the unclaimed burnt body found near the Hathras platform was Ramveer Singh. However, during the same time, GRP police became suspicious when a beggar, who was usually seen on the platform, also went missing. According to local residents, that beggar usually never left the platform. As soon as this was known, the police's suspicion deepened. The policemen started an investigation based on suspicion. They contacted Ramveer Singh's village in Mainpuri. Meanwhile, GRP station officer Suyash Singh received information that a person named Ramveer Singh had arrived at the district hospital in a burnt condition and had been referred to Saifai Medical College. Secret revealed in dismissed constable's village, waited one month for arrest When the police also investigated the village of the dismissed constable, it was revealed that a family member was admitted to the medical college, and the family members were engaged in his care. When the police furthered the investigation, it became clear that the dismissed constable Ramveer Singh was alive and admitted to the medical college due to burns. The police investigation also clarified that the body found on the platform belonged to a beggar. After this, the police performed his last rites. Meanwhile, the police were quietly keeping an eye on the dismissed constable admitted to Saifai Medical College. A month later, when he was discharged from the medical college, he was arrested and brought to Hathras. GRP Inspector Suyash Singh said - During interrogation, the accused dismissed constable confessed to his crime. He wanted to burn the beggar and declare himself dead. If the police had believed his story, he would have settled somewhere else to escape the charges and avoid arrest. Caught due to these three reasons 1- GRP came to know in the village that Ramveer is not dead. His family members are undergoing treatment at Saifai Medical College. 2- The beggar used to live at the railway station itself. He did not go anywhere. He was also missing. Therefore, the police's suspicion increased further. 3- The dismissed constable had made a patient slip with his real name and address at Hathras District Hospital and Saifai Medical College. Because of this, the police also found it easy. Wanted in Firozabad, Aligarh, Moradabad, Hardoi, Mainpuri and Badaun GRP said - A total of 13 criminal cases were registered against Ramveer Singh between 2012 and 2013 in Firozabad, Moradabad, Aligarh, Mainpuri, Badaun and Kanpur Dehat. A case of murder was registered at Civil Lines police station in Badaun in 2012, and a case of attempted murder was registered at Matsena police station in Firozabad in 2013. The Gangster Act was also invoked against him from Matsena police station in 2013. He was absconding. Death of the only son, 5 daughters living with their mother Police said - Ramveer Singh's family lives in Mainpuri. He had a total of 6 children, out of whom the only son has died. 5 daughters are left in the family who live with their mother.

stories.title: UP set for harsher heat, less rain ahead:Temperature to increase by 3 to 4 degrees; Purvanchal hotter than Bundelkhand
stories.summary: The heat in UP is bothering people. People are troubled by the scorching sun. According to meteorologists, the heatwave in Purvanchal will bother people for a longer duration this season. However, the people of Bundelkhand, who suffer from heat every season, are likely to get some relief. It is possible that the heat here might be somewhat less intense. Experts say that the monsoon might arrive on time in UP, but there is a possibility of it weakening in July itself. This could lead to less rainfall. This is not good news for farmers. How will the heat be in UP? How will the monsoon rains be? To know this, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh of the Regional Meteorological Centre, Lucknow. Question. How hot will it be in the last 15 days of April? Answer. In the initial days of the month, rain and strong winds provided relief to people. Now the sun has started to get intense. From April 15 to 21, the temperature can rise by 3 to 4 degrees. After this, the temperature will remain stable for 2-3 days. There will be no heatwave (loo). After this, the temperature will gradually increase. Question. Will it be hotter in May and June? Answer. Yes, this is true to some extent. Compared to 2025, there is a possibility of more heat this time in May and June. In 25 to 28 districts of Purvanchal, the daytime temperature is expected to remain above 40 degrees. In June, the heat will be at its peak. The temperature is estimated to average 42 to 44C. Upon reaching around 45C, severe heatwave-like conditions can develop, and nights will also remain warm. There was severe heat in 2025. The mercury went up to 46.2 degrees. This temperature was recorded in Badaun on May 17. Additionally, the temperature in more than 25 districts crossed 45 degrees. Question. How many days will the heatwave last this summer? Answer. Look... there are 3 categories of heatwave- Normal Heatwave- 3-4 days Strong Heatwave- 5-7 days Severe Heatwave- 7-10 days or more. This time, heatwave in Uttar Pradesh's Purvanchal, Ganga's plain regions like Prayagraj, Varanasi, Ghazipur, Ballia, and Central UP districts like Kannauj, Kanpur, Unnao, Fatehpur, could last for more than 10 days. However, Bundelkhand is likely to get some relief this season. Here, the heatwave might last only 5-7 days. Meanwhile, in West UP, a normal heatwave, meaning 3-4 days, is expected. Question. When can monsoon enter UP? Answer. El Nio is active. Due to this, warm winds originating from the Pacific Ocean are likely to shift towards South America. In normal conditions, they remain towards Australia, Indonesia. Now, the shifting of these winds will affect UP. Between June 20-25, the monsoon first enters eastern UP and then western parts a few days later. The same is expected to happen this season. Pre-monsoon rains and strong winds may occur in May and June. However, the monsoon is likely to weaken in July. Know about El Nio and La Nia Question. How much less rainfall is expected? Answer. In 2025, the monsoon rainfall in UP was unbalanced, as West UP received 12% more rainfall, while Purvanchal received 17% less rainfall. Overall, about 6% less rainfall was recorded across UP. This season, there is a possibility of 6 to 8% less rainfall. Question. What will be the impact of a weak monsoon on agriculture? Answer. Due to unseasonal rains in April, farmers' wheat and mustard crops have already been damaged. Now, a weak monsoon will have the biggest impact on the paddy crop. If the monsoon is weak, transplanting will be delayed. Other Kharif crops may also be affected. These include maize, pulses, and oilseeds. Farmers may have to rely on tube wells and diesel pumps. It is feared that a shortage of water could also lead to fodder problems for livestock. Now, weather pictures from 4 cities on April 15- Scorching sun came out. The temperature remained 39 degrees Celsius.

stories.title: Kidney transplant accused Dr. Ali surrenders in Kanpur Court:OT technician with ₹25,000 bounty sent to 14-day judicial custody
stories.summary: An operation theatre (OT) technician, Mudassar Ali alias “Dr Ali,” who was absconding in connection with a kidney transplant scandal, surrendered before a court in Kanpur on Thursday. Ali, who was wanted by the police and had a reward of ₹25,000 on his arrest, appeared before the ACJM-6 court and surrendered. The court subsequently sent him to 14 days of judicial custody. According to police, Ali was actively involved in conducting kidney transplants despite being only an OT technician. He is accused of carrying out more than 30 such procedures in Kanpur. Police search across multiple states Police teams had been searching for Ali across several locations, including Noida, Ghaziabad, and parts of Uttarakhand. Despite extensive efforts, he had managed to evade arrest until his surrender in court. Multiple arrests already made In connection with the kidney scandal, police had earlier arrested 10 accused. Ali is the 11th accused to be sent to jail in the case. See 2 pictures Dr. Mudassir Ali is a resident of Dwarka in Delhi. Inside the operation theatre, he played a key role. He would make the surgical incision in the abdomen, remove the kidney, and transplant it into the recipient patient. Dr. Ali never came to Kanpur alone. He was accompanied by another doctor and two assistants. After the operation, two members of the team would head towards Lucknow, while the other two would go towards Ghaziabad. Rajesh Kumar, a resident of Ghaziabad, stated that five kidney transplants have been carried out since January, and Dr. Ali was involved in all of them.

stories.title: Vrindavan boat tragedy:Manager’s body surfaces on 7th day after swelling; divers search 30 km area
stories.summary: The body of missing Pankaj Malhotra has been recovered on the seventh day after the boat accident in the Yamuna river in Vrindavan. His body was found about 2.5 kilometres downstream from the accident site, near Devrha Ghat and beneath the Panigaon bridge. The body had surfaced due to swelling, and divers along with army personnel, pulled it out. With this, the death toll in the incident has risen to 16. Earlier, on Monday at around 8 am, the body of a woman was found at Bengali Ghat, about 12 kilometres from the accident site, while a youth's body was recovered near the Deora Baba Ashram. The woman was identified as Monika Tandon from Ludhiana. She had come with her mother-in-law, Savita. She had been married just six months ago, and her husband lives abroad. Monika was also planning to go abroad soon. On the day of the accident, she was sitting in the boat with her neighbour Dinky, whose body had been found on April 12. The youth was identified as 22-year-old Yash Bhalla, also from Ludhiana. He had come to Vrindavan for the first time and was associated with the Banke Bihari group. He used to play the dholak during religious singing events. In a video recorded before the boat capsized, Yash can be seen playing the dholak. His elder brother is an accountant, his mother Sunita is a homemaker, and his father sells clothes on a street cart. According to officials, the bodies had floated to the surface of the river. After the post-mortem, both bodies were handed over to their families. The accident took place on Friday, October 10, at around 3 pm when the boat capsized. Since then, the search for Pankaj Malhotra had become a major challenge for the police and administration. Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), and local divers had been continuously carrying out a search operation in the Yamuna River. Around 250 personnel were involved in the operation. Read the full case in detail below Pankaj had come to Vrindavan on April 10 Rural SP Suresh Chandra Rawat said that Pankaj Malhotra was a manager in a steel company in Himachal. He had come alone to Vrindavan on April 10. He was boating in the Yamuna with a group when the boat overturned and he drowned. A rescue operation had been ongoing to find him. On the seventh day after the accident, his body was found near Devrha Baba Ghat. His family has been informed, and the body will be handed over after the post-mortem. Brother said Pankaj used to visit Mathura every year Aniket said Pankaj Malhotra was his cousin. “We are deeply saddened by his death. We had been waiting here for several days, hoping his body would be found. Today, we finally got him. He used to come to Mathura every year with his family. He was married and had two children, a three-year-old daughter and a nine-year-old son. He had two sisters and was the eldest among them. Five to six members of his extended family have also died in this accident.” How did the accident happen? A youth who survived said the boat was about 50 feet from the bank in the middle of the Yamuna River. The wind was blowing at around 40 km per hour. The boat suddenly started shaking, and the boatman lost control. Tourists asked him to stop as they were nearing a bridge, but he did not listen. The boat narrowly avoided hitting the bridge twice, but on the third attempt, it collided and capsized. Timeline: From accident to rescue operation On April 10 at around 3 pm, a boat carrying 38 devotees capsized near Kesi Ghat, about 2 kilometres from the Banke Bihari temple. On the same day, 22 people were rescued, while 10 bodies were recovered. Teams from the army, NDRF, SDRF, PAC and local divers began search operations. At around 12:30 am, the submerged steamer was pulled out using a crane. Rescue teams had hoped to find bodies inside the steamer, but none were found. The search team was then expanded to 250 members. On April 11, one body — Manik Tandon — was recovered, taking the toll to 11. On the same day, contractor Narayan and boatman Pankaj were arrested. On April 12, two more bodies — Rishabh and Dinky — were found. On April 13, a woman’s body was found at Bengali Ghat and a man’s body near Deora Baba Ashram. On April 14, the bodies of Yash Bhalla and Monika Tandon were recovered, taking the toll to 15. On April 16, the body of Pankaj Malhotra was recovered. Four people were made to get off before the accident Rajinder Kaur said there were 37 people on the steamer. The boat stopped midway, and when passengers asked why, the boatman told them to shift to another boat. Women refused, but four elderly people moved to the other boat. She said the boat was not overloaded, as she had travelled in it before. Bridge came towards us, rope got stuck Rajinder Kaur said while the steamer was stationary, the bridge appeared to be moving towards them. The operator said he would cross before the bridge arrived, but it approached quickly and hit the boat. The boat got stuck in a rope attached to the bridge and overturned. The bridge structure then fell over the boat. I was standing and recording video She said she was standing and recording when the boat overturned, and she held onto it. When the bridge fell over, she let go and went underwater. People trapped beneath the boat could not escape. Boat hit my head five times She said

stories.title: 38-year-old man dies after ambulance runs out of oxygen:Fuel also exhausted during transfer from Rampur to Moradabad
stories.summary: A 38-year-old man died after an ambulance carrying him ran out of both oxygen and fuel while he was being shifted from Rampur to Moradabad. The victim had sustained critical injuries after being hit by a tractor. After receiving primary treatment at a district hospital, doctors referred him to Meerut. However, his family decided to take him to Moradabad in a privately hired ambulance. According to family members, the patient was on oxygen support, but the oxygen supply ran out mid-way. Soon after, the ambulance also ran out of fuel, forcing it to stop on the road. The man died shortly thereafter. Accident and Medical referral The incident occurred late Wednesday night in Ahmadnagar Jibai village under Shahzadnagar police station limits in Rampur. The deceased, Kuldeep Singh (38), a farmer, was heading to his field on a motorcycle around 10 pm amid the wheat harvesting season when a speeding tractor hit him, leaving him critically injured. Family members rushed him to the district hospital, where doctors provided emergency treatment and referred him to Meerut due to his serious condition. Oxygen depletion and Ambulance breakdown Kuldeep’s nephew, Harvinder Singh, said the family had barely covered half the distance to Moradabad when the oxygen cylinder in the ambulance got depleted. “We asked the driver to speed up, but shortly after that, the ambulance ran out of fuel as well. Due to lack of oxygen, Kuldeep died,” he said. Family vandalises ambulance, driver flees Angered by the death, the family vandalised the ambulance, while the driver fled the scene. Police were informed and later sent the body for postmortem. The ambulance has been seized at Majhola police station in Moradabad, and further action is underway. Mandatory standards for ambulances As per regulations, ambulances must comply with strict operational standards. These include valid registration and permits, trained drivers and paramedical staff, and a functional oxygen supply at all times. They must also be equipped with a stretcher, first-aid kit, and basic life support (BLS) systems, and remain operational 24×7 with proper fuel and technical readiness. Possible legal action in such cases For critical patients, advanced life support (ALS) facilities are also required. Any negligence in maintaining these standards can invite strict action. Legal provisions may include charges under IPC Section 304A (causing death by negligence), and Sections 279/336/337/338 (endangering life). Authorities may also suspend or cancel the ambulance’s permit, arrest those responsible, and provide compensation to the victim’s family.

stories.title: Yogi vows strict action against mafias in Bengal:Says, 'They will be made to fall in line'; urges people not to fear
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath addressed a rally in Asansol, West Bengal, saying people should not fear “TMC goons, mafias, or clerics.” Yogi, who is one of the star campaigners, while campaigning for the saffron party on Thursday, asserted that if the BJP comes to power in the state, such elements would “fall in line” and even be seen “sweeping the streets.” “Do not be afraid of what TMC’s goons say. Do not be intimidated by Mafias or concerned about what clerics say. Let the BJP form the government, and all of them will start flattering you”, he said. Claims of better law and order in Uttar Pradesh Adityanath highlighted the law-and-order situation in Uttar Pradesh, claiming that no one is allowed to offer Namaz on roads and that festivals are celebrated peacefully. “There is no hooliganism. Women are safe. Only the BJP and a double-engine government can guarantee this,” he said. Remarks on Religion and Politics CM also accused West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee of being “averse to Ram Naam and Durga Puja,” adding that similar attitudes existed earlier in Uttar Pradesh before the BJP came to power. He said the construction of the Ram temple in Ayodhya was made possible after the BJP double-engine government came to power, asserting that neither Congress, the Samajwadi Party, nor the TMC could stop it. “Only Prime Minister Narendra Modi can guarantee no riots, no curfew. We will not allow cow slaughter or division among Hindus,” he added. Multiple rallies across Bengal Adityanath held three public meetings in West Bengal on Thursday as part of the Assembly election campaign. He first addressed a rally in Asansol, followed by events in Birbhum and Bolpur, seeking support for BJP and NDA candidates. Key points from the speech 1. BJP government as solution to ‘Mafia rule’ Adityanath alleged that central funds sent by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for public welfare are “siphoned off by TMC goons.” He said Uttar Pradesh faced similar issues nine years ago, with frequent riots, unsafe conditions for women, and widespread crime. “The only solution to anarchy, fear, riots, and mafia rule is a BJP double-engine government,” he said. 2. ‘No curfew, no riots in UP now’ He claimed that strict action against mafias inUP, including property seizures and use of bulldozers, has ended organized crime. “Today, there is no curfew, no riots in UP—everything is fine. Earlier, people had to agitate for Ram Janmabhoomi, and devotees were fired upon,” he said. 3. Opposition accused of ruining Bengal Adityanath said West Bengal was once India’s cultural capital but alleged that Congress, Left parties, and TMC have turned it into a “crime capital.” “There was development, farmers were happy, and youth had jobs. Now it has become a center of anarchy, corruption, and fear. Mafias dominate resources, and jobs have disappeared,” he claimed. Inauguration of security buildings in Gorakhpur Earlier in the day, Adityanath inaugurated new security buildings in Gorakhpur, constructed at a cost of ₹9.18 crore to enhance security in the Gorakhnath temple area. The facilities will house offices of senior police officials, a control room, storage, and maintenance units. Strengthening policing infrastructure 1. Accommodation for 100 personnel Adityanath said the building can accommodate up to 100 police personnel and officers, with all necessary facilities. He added that in 55 districts, the tallest buildings will now belong to the police. 2. Security as foundation of good governance “Security is the first condition of good governance,” he said, emphasizing the need for proper training and infrastructure for police personnel. He noted that when his government came to power in 2017, more than half the police posts were vacant. “In nine years, we have recruited over 2.19 lakh personnel,” he added.

stories.title: Mercury crosses 44°C in UP for first time this season:Lions and deer cooled with sprays; rhino gets mud pool
stories.summary: Severe heat has started in UP. On Wednesday, for the first time this season, the maximum temperature crossed 44 °C. Not only this, mercury was recorded at 40 degrees or more in 16 districts. The effect of increasing heat is now visible on zoo animals as well. To provide relief from the heat, a mud pond has been built for rhinoceroses in Kanpur. Water sprays are being used on deer and lions. Expert Dr. Nasir said that rhinoceroses keep themselves cool by rolling in the mud. Wet soil sticks to their bodies, which provides relief to the rhinos from the heat. Talking about the last 24 hours, Banda was the hottest, where the day temperature was recorded at 44.8C. Apart from this, mercury was recorded at 43C in Prayagraj, 42.8C in Varanasi, 41.4C in Jhansi, and 41.3C in Sultanpur. Hot winds are making it feel like a heatwave during the day. Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- There are no chances of rain for the next 10 days. Westerly winds are now weakening. Due to this, the mercury will jump by 3 to 6C in the next 4-5 days. In the coming days, temperatures in most districts will reach up to 45 degrees. The impact of heat will intensify. There is also a possibility of heatwave. stories.title: Massive fire in 200 huts in Ghaziabad, cylinders explode:Smoke visible from 10 km away; 22 fire tenders deployed
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in around 500 slum huts in Kanawani village under the Indirapuram police station area of Ghaziabad at around 12:00 noon on Thursday. The fire was so intense that massive flames were visible from nearly 10 km away, triggering panic in the area as residents rushed out of their homes. Local residents immediately informed the fire department. Soon after receiving the alert, about eight fire trucks reached the spot. Considering the seriousness of the situation, additional fire brigade vehicles were also called from Noida. Firefighters are continuously trying to bring the blaze under control. It is being reported that the huts contained large quantities of plastic, wood, and other highly flammable materials, which caused the fire to spread rapidly and made firefighting operations difficult. People in nearby residential areas faced breathing difficulties because of heavy smoke, and many residents stepped out of their homes as a precaution. According to eyewitnesses, fire engulfed several huts within a short time. However, no casualties have been reported so far. The cause of the fire is still unknown. Fire department teams and the local administration are present at the spot and are closely monitoring the situation. Pictures of the incident Eyewitnesses said around 150–200 huts were gutted in the Ghaziabad fire, with losses running into lakhs as the blaze reportedly started during cooking and spread rapidly due to cylinder blasts. About 22 fire tenders were deployed, bringing nearly 90 per cent of the fire under control while preventing it from spreading to nearby residential areas. Residents said entire households were reduced to ashes, affecting around 200–250 people. Authorities have deployed ambulances, alerted hospitals and said a survey will be conducted if anyone is reported missing, while the cause of the fire remains under investigation.

stories.title: Bulldozer action on Eidgah and Imambara in Sambhal:Crowd dispersed; heavy police and PAC deployed
stories.summary: Bulldozer action began at 8:00 am on Thursday on an Eidgah and an Imambara in Sambhal. The Imambara has already been demolished, and the Eidgah is now being razed using four bulldozers. Police personnel from five police stations and one company of Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) have been deployed at the site. Meanwhile, villagers gathered at the spot, but officials removed them due to fear of possible protest. According to the administration, the Eidgah was built on about 7 bighas of grazing land, while the Imambara had been constructed on land meant for a manure pit. Following complaints from villagers, Lekhpal Sparsh Gupta filed an appeal in the Tehsildar court on 18 January. On 31 January, a notice was published in newspapers as per court orders, asking any occupants to come forward. However, no one responded. On Thursday morning around 7:30 am, SDM Nidhi Patel and Naib Tehsildar Deepak Kumar Jurail reached the site with a team. Some people were seen trying to demolish the Imambara using chisels and hammers, but the administration removed them. The incident took place in Bicholi village under the Kotwali Sambhal police station area. DM and SP reach the spot Around 12 noon, Rajendra Pensiya and Krishna Kumar Vishnoi also reached the site. They reviewed the report on the demolition of the structures from police and administrative teams and issued necessary instructions. Imambara wall collapses on JCB in Sambhal, operator injured JCB operator Saurabh Sirswal of the Nagar Palika Parishad Sambhal suffered an injury to his right hand when an Imambara wall suddenly collapsed onto the machine during demolition. The glass of the JCB broke, and the machine was also damaged in the incident. Following the accident, the machine developed a fault and was sent back from the site. Temples built on govt land should also be demolished Villager Zubaida said, Demolition action should be stopped. She stated that the Imambara and Eidgah were used by everyone in the area, and even wedding processions of poor families used to stay there. She questioned that if the issue is construction on government land, then temples built on government land should also face action, but currently, action is being taken only against mosques. She added that if the law is equal for everyone, then action should also be taken against temples built on government land. stories.title: Yogi warns of strict action against police attacks:Says over 2 lakh vacancies filled in 8 years; inaugurates security buildings
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is in Gorakhpur today. He said that the first condition of good governance is security. Efforts are made at the government level for this. There used to be a belief that for security, just recruit police. But if police personnel are not trained, then they are also ordinary people. Therefore, after the recruitment process, their training should happen. After that, when they perform their duty, the infrastructure facilities during that time should also be of that standard, this was not paid attention to. The result of this was that the police personnel were not able to fulfill their responsibilities. Yogi said- We have increased police facilities When we came in 2017, at that time more than half the posts in Uttar Pradesh Police were vacant. In 9 years, we have done recruitment of more than 2 lakh 19 thousand. When we came to government in 2017, the training capacity of police was not more than 3 thousand at a time. Currently, as a result of the development of infrastructure facilities, we are training more than 60 thousand police personnel. The state is the same, but now facilities have increased more than 200 times. Earlier, whether it was police station, outpost, police lines or PAC battalion, there were no residential facilities for police personnel anywhere. The result was that they lived on rent or somehow spent their life. Residential facilities for 200 police personnel were provided in every police line. What the model of a police station will be, you can see Gorakhnath police station. Buildings for fire tenders are being built rapidly. When infrastructure facilities developed, their work speed also increased. The result was that a better security model was created. Earlier, the CM inaugurated the security buildings. These have been constructed for the security of the Gorakhnath Temple area. The construction of both buildings cost Rs 9 crore 18 lakh. Both buildings are adjacent to each other. Both buildings have been constructed as stilt plus 4 floors. The Additional Superintendent of Police, Deputy Superintendent of Police office and control room will be located here. Along with this, a police store room and maintenance workshop have also been built in it.

stories.title: 2 children burnt alive, 250 families homeless in Lucknow fire:Women allege huts were deliberately set ablaze
stories.summary: Two children were burnt alive in a massive fire that broke out on Wednesday in a cluster of huts in Lucknow. Nearly 250 families living in the slum area were left homeless after the blaze destroyed their homes. DCP Diksha Sharma said efforts are underway to identify the victims’ families. On Thursday morning, only ashes and burnt household belongings could be seen at the site. Several families were searching through the debris for whatever they could recover, while police asked people to move away from the area. The District Magistrate arranged shelter for many affected families in night shelters, while some spent the night on a nearby vacant plot. Women from the settlement alleged that residents of nearby houses had earlier threatened them to vacate the huts, warning of consequences if they refused. They claimed the huts were deliberately set on fire after they did not leave. They also said their lifelong savings were reduced to ashes, adding that some belongings could have been saved if the fire brigade had arrived earlier. Police deployment has been increased in the Vikasnagar area amid fears of tension. Security personnel with helmets and batons are stationed at the site. Key details of the incident The fire broke out around 5:30 pm on Wednesday in Vikasnagar, one of the posh areas of the city. During the blaze, more than 30 LPG cylinders exploded, and over 250 huts were destroyed. Smoke from the fire was visible from nearly 10 km away. As a precaution, residents of 20 nearby houses were evacuated. Around 20 fire brigade vehicles worked for nearly five hours to control the fire. Electricity supply in the area was temporarily cut during the operation. Rajnath Singh, the Member of Parliament from Lucknow, spoke to District Magistrate Vishakh G to review the situation, while Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak also visited the spot to assess the situation. stories.title: Over 250 huts gutted in fire as 30 cylinders explode:Flames visible up to 10 kilometres; man says, '4 children burnt alive'
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in Lucknow on Wednesday evening at 5:30 PM. This fire in the Vikasnagar area caused more than 30 cylinders to explode. Over 250 huts and small housing units were reduced to ashes. Flames were visible from about 10 kilometers away. After the fire broke out, around 20 nearby houses were evacuated. 20 fire brigade vehicles brought the fire under control after about 3 hours. During this time, electricity in the area was cut off. When it became dark, rescue operations were carried out using generator-powered lights. A young man claims that his 4 children died in the fire. All belongings of other people were reduced to ashes. Those whose huts burned kept crying and wailing. Some people allege that the fire was set deliberately. CM Yogi took cognizance of the fire incident and immediately directed officials to reach the spot. Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak also reached the spot and ordered officials to expedite rescue operations. First see the pictures of the massive fire People said - Everything I had turned to ashes Local resident Aman Gupta said that the fire broke out at 5:30. After the fire, there was mourning and chaos in the settlement. A woman, Shamsunisha, said while crying - The entire family was at home when the fire broke out. Now there is no trace of the family. Our house has completely burned to ashes. Pooja said - Wedding preparations were going on at home. My brother-in-law's son's wedding procession was about to leave. All the wedding items burned in the fire. People somehow saved their lives. Meanwhile, a woman fainted while searching for family members. People present at the spot took her to the hospital. A victim Rahman said while crying - My 4 children have been burnt. I have my mother, no father. My children were playing at home. I saw that a fire had broken out. As soon as I reached there, I saw my children had been burnt. My 4 children died in the fire. Prema said that she has small children. All the children's clothes were burnt in the fire. It is not known how the fire started. All the household items turned to ash. The grain was also completely burnt. Now there is nothing left to eat. Several cows were also burned in the fire incident. Animal Welfare Officer Abhinav Verma also reached the spot. He informed that the injured stray animals from the accident have been sent to the Municipal Corporation's cow shelter. Two cows are being treated and 6 have been rescued. People's anger visible after the fire After the fire, anger was visible among the people. Angry people created a ruckus outside the plot owner's house. Women alleged that they were threatened to vacate the slum. People accused the plot owner of setting the fire. Police dragged out the youth to control the situation. Even after this, people continued to create a ruckus for a long time. However, the land where the fire broke out is said to belong to LDA. According to local people, there is a dispute over the land. The matter of compensation between farmers and the authority is pending. A large number of huts were built here. Most people worked as laborers. Many people also worked as rag pickers. The number of people residing here from Assam is said to be higher. DG Fire said- Large number of gas cylinders found DG Fire Sujit Pandey said- As soon as information about the fire was received, fire engines were immediately sent to the spot from nearby fire stations including BKT and Indira Nagar. More than 20 fire engines worked together to extinguish the fire and prevented it from spreading to nearby areas in time. The relief is that there is no information about any loss of life so far. He said that a large number of gas cylinders have been recovered in this incident, which could be a major reason for the rapid spread of the fire. Currently, the entire matter is being investigated and the situation is being continuously monitored. After the fire, the NDRF team reached the spot to control the deteriorating situation. Traffic jam from Munshi Puliya to Engineering College As soon as information about the fire in Vikas Nagar was received, ambulances and fire brigades started reaching the spot. This caused severe traffic jam in the area. The road from Munshi Puliya to Engineering College intersection remained jammed for about 3 hours. Vehicles remained stuck on the flyover for hours as well. Rajnath told DM - Speed up relief and rescue work Defense Minister Rajnath Singh took cognizance of the matter and spoke to the District Magistrate over the phone. He gave instructions to speed up relief work. He asked to ensure all possible assistance for the affected people and to arrange proper treatment for the injured. According to BJP Lucknow Metropolitan President Anand Dwivedi, the Defense Minister has expressed deep concern over the incident and has given instructions to the administration to provide immediate help. Meanwhile, DM Vishakh G said that people affected by the fire have been shifted to rain basera (night shelter). Brajesh Pathak said - Government is with the affected families Taking cognizance of the fire in the Vikas Nagar area, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak immediately reached the spot. He said that a high-level investigation will be conducted into this incident. The government stands with the affected families. The Deputy CM called health department teams on the spot and gave instructions to provide better treatment to the people injured in the incident. He instructed officials to speed up relief work. The Deputy CM discussed rescue operations in this incident with the District Magistrate, Police Commissioner, Chief Development Officer, Municipal Commissioner, NDRF and other officials at the incident site itself. Akhilesh said - Victims should get immediate treatment and help Former Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav has also reacted to this incident and demanded swift action from the government. He said - Immediate arrangements for food and water should be made for the victims. The injured should get immediate treatment and alternative accommodation arrangements should be ensured for the affected families. Akhilesh demanded a thorough investigation of this fire incident and said that keeping in mind the side of the poor, every aspect should be investigated and the situation regarding those who are missing should also be clarified.

stories.title: Chain pulled to stop Punjab Mail for Uma Bharti:Train halted for 5 minutes in Jhansi; former CM claims it departed ahead of schedule
stories.summary: Former Chief Minister Uma Bharti had to stop the Punjab Mail by chain pulling at Jhansi on Sunday. When Uma Bharti reached the platform, the Punjab Mail going to New Delhi had already departed. The train had left half the platform. Uma's supporters immediately stopped the train. She had to board the First AC coach A-1 of the train. But by the time the train stopped, coach A-1 had reached the yard. Therefore, she boarded coach B-1. Due to the chain pulling, the train's brake air had been released. The train stood for 5 minutes, half on the platform and half in the yard. After Uma Bharti boarded the train, the train was sent forward. Uma Bharti said- The train had departed ahead of schedule. This entire incident is a result of railway mismanagement. What happened to me today is happening to passengers every day. Such difficulties frequently occur at stations like Mathura, Jhansi, and Lalitpur. Women run around on platforms with luggage and children. The elderly and differently-abled face the most trouble.Uma Bharti had to board Third AC. Now know the complete matterUma Bharti's claim - Reached the station at 2:18 PMFormer CM Uma Bharti claimed that she arrived at Jhansi Railway Station on Sunday afternoon at 2:18 PM. The train was at 2:23 PM.Uma Bharti said - I was going by escalator, but the officers asked me to go by e-cart. After walking some distance, a train passed in front of the e-cart, so we had to stand there for five minutes. Then a hand trolley came out. Due to this, the train was missed.Wrote a letter to Rail Minister on X - Lack of sensitivity at the stationUma Bharti has written a letter to Rail Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on social media X after the incident. Uma Bharti said, I have previously written about the insensitivity towards passengers at Mathura Railway Station. Today again, an incident happened with me while boarding at Jhansi Railway Station in which there is no criminal, but the lack of practical sensitivity in the construction of modern facilities at stations has become the cause.Officers asked to go by e-cart. After this, Uma Bharti went to the platform by e-cart.CCTV should be retrievedUma Bharti wrote - CCTV footage of Jhansi Railway Station should be retrieved. I had reached Jhansi Railway Station before the train arrived and this train came before the scheduled time and departed before the scheduled time. I was being taken in a battery cart from platform number 1 towards number 4. Meanwhile, a train passed on the same track for a long time and we stood waiting.Then when we moved a little ahead, a handcart was stuck in the track. My security personnel helped in removing it. Then when I reached platform number 4 and the train Punjab Mail in which I had to board was leaving. Who pulled the chain, I have no idea, and I was made to board the train. Will tell about Mathura and Jhansi incidents togetherUma further wrote- Everything was according to time, there was no mistake by anyone. Three-four minutes of the train went bad for me. The first reason for this was the train arriving before time and leaving 2 minutes before time.Mistake of Officials Operating the TrainUma Bharti said, leave me aside, but common people, differently-abled persons, elderly, women and men carrying a lot of luggage and women with children in their laps become victims of mismanagement. I do not consider it the fault of Jhansi Railway officials at all, nor do I consider it my fault. This entire system was created by the officials operating the train inside the railway. I will tell you again to pay attention to these mismanagements.Railway's Claim - Train Departed on TimeAccording to the National Train Enquiry System, the train arrived at platform 4 at 2:09 PM, 6 minutes before its scheduled time of 2:15 PM. After that, it was supposed to depart at 2:23 PM after an 8-minute stop, and the train departed at its scheduled time. Later, when it was stopped by chain pulling, it departed again at 2:28 PM.Divisional Railway Manager Aniruddh Kumar informed-The chain pulling of the Mumbai-Firozpur Punjab Mail was not done by Uma Bharti. Some passengers who had gotten down on the Jhansi station platform to get food and water, when they saw that the train was starting to move, their fellow passengers pulled the chain. It doesn't happen in the railway system that a train leaves the platform before the scheduled time. Yes, it is true that trains do arrive at the station before the scheduled time. Still, we are investigating the matter whether the train was run before time or not.

Who ordered firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya?:Former IAS says most decisions are political; also replies to Akhilesh Yadav
stories.summary: A senior official linked to the Ram Temple project has spoken about the Ayodhya demolition issue and the claims of firing on karsevaks. He said most such decisions are political, not taken by top officials alone. Nripendra Misra, chairman of the Ram Temple Construction Committee and a former IAS officer, spoke in Ayodhya on Saturday. He said decisions like these are not made at the chief secretary level. He added that around 90 percent of such decisions are political, while only 10 percent include inputs from officers like the Home Secretary, Chief Secretary and Director General of Police. His remarks come amid ongoing political debate on the issue. Two months ago, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav raised the matter in Parliament during a discussion on MNREGA. Akhilesh said MNREGA had been renamed “VBG Ramji”. He pointed towards BJP MP Arun Govil and asked where “Ramji” was. He said people have seen him since childhood and questioned why he was seated at the back in the Lok Sabha. He added that he should be brought forward and given seat number 2." During this, ruling party MPs said - those who fired on Karsevaks are talking. Hearing this, Akhilesh flared up. He said - those who ordered the firing are building the Ram Temple. If you don't know something, go and ask, find out. Don't come here with incomplete information. When the firing took place, I was the Secretary During the press conference, Nripendra Misra was asked about Akhilesh Yadav questioning him on the firing on Kar Sevaks in Ayodhya in 1990. At that time, you were the Principal Secretary. To this, Nripendra Misra said, yes, I was the Principal Secretary in Mulayam Singh Yadav's government. But such decisions are not made at the level of the Chief Secretary. About 90 percent of such decisions are political, and in 10 percent of decisions, suggestions received from the Home Secretary, Chief Secretary, and Director General of Police are included. He (Akhilesh) is the son of a respected leader of the country. Therefore, he must have all the information. Nripendra Misra explained the difference between Mulayam and Kalyan's tenures Nripendra Misra also mentioned his tenure under different governments, which included the tenure of former Chief Minister, the late Mulayam Singh Yadav. He also explained the difference in the distinct approaches adopted by these two leaders during times of crisis. Nripendra Misra said, "I have worked as Chief Secretary for both former Chief Ministers, Mulayam Singh Yadav and Kalyan Singh. You might also know that when a report was presented to Kalyan Singh in 1992 stating that law and order had completely deteriorated in Ayodhya, he gave a written order that there would be no firing of any kind in this holy city." Police fired bullets in Ayodhya on October 30 and November 2 During Mulayam Singh Yadav's tenure, on October 30 and November 2, 1990, police fired on Kar Sevaks, at which time a large number of devotees of Lord Ram had gathered in Ayodhya as part of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad's 'Kar Seva'. According to reports, more than 28 people died in the police firing on unarmed Kar Sevaks. Former Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav later said, This action was taken on his orders, and he justified it, stating it was necessary for the security of the disputed structure and to maintain national unity. In contrast, during the demolition of the disputed structure on December 6, 1992, the then Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Kalyan Singh, had instructed that despite the extremely tense situation, no firing should be opened on the karsevaks. It is said that Kalyan Singh had stated that karsevaks would not be fired upon for the sake of a building. Later, on the evening of December 6, 1992, after the demolition of the disputed structure, he resigned from the post of Chief Minister.

stories.title: Severe heat to hit Uttar Pradesh, mercury to cross 40°C:Strong sunshine and dusty winds expected, no rain likely for next 2 weeks
stories.summary: Summer has started to show its strong impact across Uttar Pradesh. Since Sunday morning, the sky has remained clear with bright sunshine and steady winds. The Meteorological Department has said that temperatures will cross 40°C during the day today. Dusty winds are expected to blow at a speed of 25 to 35 km/h, and in some areas, people may feel heatwave-like conditions. The department said that the effect of the Western Disturbance has now ended, leading to a rise in heat. No new weather system is expected to become active in the next 15 days. Because of this, there is no chance of rain, and the heat is likely to increase sharply. The maximum temperature may rise by up to 8°C, while the minimum temperature could go up by 6°C. In the last 24 hours, Prayagraj and Jhansi recorded the highest temperatures at 37.6°C. Varanasi and Jalaun were close behind at 37.4°C. Strong winds were seen in many districts, including Lucknow. Due to this, nights felt slightly cooler despite the rising daytime heat. Atul Kumar Singh, Senior Scientist at the Regional Meteorological Center, Lucknow, said- The weather will remain clear in the state for the next two weeks. There are no chances of rain. The wind direction will change. Humidity in the atmosphere will decrease due to winds coming from the east. The heat will further increase. The average temperature of night and day may increase by 6 to 8 degrees Celsius. Today's weather pictures- How will the weather be for the next 5 days? Farmers get relief as weather clears Agricultural experts say that farmers have got relief as the weather has cleared. This is because the harvested wheat crops had gotten wet. With strong sunlight, the crops will dry quickly. This will allow farmers to thresh as soon as possible. The chances of the crop grains turning black will be reduced. What was the reason for the sudden storm and rain? The sudden storm and rain were due to a Western Disturbance. This is normal for this season. Every year, during this season, there is rain with storms. However, this year, Western Disturbances are occurring very frequently. Because of this, the weather has been continuously stormy and rainy. Farmers suffered losses, wheat crop in crisis Untimely rains caused heavy losses to farmers. The wheat crop was destroyed. Regarding this, CM Yogi had instructed officials to go into the field. He had said that officials should survey the damage within 24 hours and compensation should be given to the affected farmers as soon as possible. No kind of negligence will be tolerated. Providing help to farmers is the government's priority.

stories.title: 4 videos show final moments before Vrindavan boat accident:Punjab youth seen singing ‘Nazar Saawre Lag Na Jaye’; death toll rises to 13
stories.summary: Four videos of devotees from Punjab, taken before the boat accident in the Yamuna River in Vrindavan, Mathura, have surfaced. In them, the scene just before the accident is clearly visible, with devotees seen singing bhajans. It can be clearly seen in the video that none of the devotees was wearing life jackets for safety. Everyone was chanting 'Radhe-Radhe' and performing bhajan-kirtan. Bhajans were being sung to the rhythm of dholak and manjira. A young man is singing a bhajan while playing the manjira - ‘Nazar Sanware Lag Na Jaye Kahin...’ Death toll rises to 13 The rescue operation continued on Sunday for the third day. A team of about 250 people, including the army, NDRF-SDRF, is involved in the operation. The search area has now been increased from 14 km to 20 km. So far, 13 devotees from Punjab have died in this accident. 22 people have been rescued. 3 are still missing. This morning, two more bodies were found. They were identified as Dinky from Dugri (Ludhiana), Punjab, and Rishabh Sharma from Jagraon. According to the administration, the bodies had bloated and floated to the surface of the river. Using ropes, the bodies were pulled into a boat and brought out. Family members identified both. Dinky was a final year BA student. Rishabh had passed 12th grade and used to assist his father in his work. What is visible in all four videos Find out how the accident happened A young man who survived the accident said- The boat was in the middle of the Yamuna river, about 50 feet from the bank. The wind was blowing at a speed of about 40 km per hour. The boat suddenly started to wobble. The boatman lost control. The tourists said that the bridge was approaching, stop the boat, but he did not listen. Twice the boat narrowly avoided hitting the bridge, but on the third time, it collided and sank.

stories.title: Punjab Banke Bihari Club linked to 13 deaths:Friends sang devotional songs, then organised Vrindavan trips; charged ₹4500 per devotee
stories.summary: 13 devotees died in the boat accident in Vrindavan. All of them were taken on a religious trip by the Banke Bihari Club of Jagraon, Ludhiana. This club was formed about 9 years ago by two real brothers and their friend. In the same accident, one of these two brothers also died. They started with 'sankirtan' (devotional singing) in temples at the age of 16-17. Then the three of them together formed this club. It was not registered. After this, people gradually joined the club. The club performs 'sankirtan' from house to house. 5 years ago, they started organizing trips to Vrindavan. This time, on April 9, they took 130 devotees to Vrindavan in 2 buses. Each devotee was charged 4,500 rupees. The accident happened on April 10, in which 13 devotees died. Read when the Banke Bihari Club was formed and how people joined it The story from forming the club to organizing trips
