stories.title: Yogi says UP bulldozer will act in Bengal:Claims only BJP can tackle rioters; Mamata accused of Muslim vote bank politics
stories.summary: CM Yogi said in West Bengal on Sunday - TMC people want half the population to speak Urdu. Tell them to go where Urdu is spoken. Only Bangla will be spoken in Bengal. UP's bulldozer will treat the goons in Bengal. The bulldozer doesn't just build roads, it also treats mafias. It crushes the ribs of those who play with the honor of daughters. The CM called TMC leaders traders of Muslim vote bank. He said- In UP, namaz is no longer read on the streets. There is no sound of shouting from mosques. There is a strict law for love jihad. Cow slaughter cannot happen. Every daughter, every businessman is safe. Every hand has work, every field has water. Even Congress and SP could not stop UP's development.Yogi said - The hooliganism that exists in Bengal today was the same in UP 9 years ago. There were riots on every festival and celebration. Curfews would be imposed for months. Businesses would remain shut. Parallel to the government, goons and mafia used to rule. In 2017, a double engine government came to UP. Now in UP, there is no appeasement, there is satisfaction.Yogi said-There are no riots in UP now. No curfew, no riots, everything is fine in UP. All the mafia that were there have gone on a journey to hell. Now there is no mafia. There are no goons. Now every citizen is safe there. Only BJP can cure goons and mafia.Yogi said these things while campaigning for the assembly elections. He held a total of 3 rallies. First he reached Sonamukhi in Bankura district. After this, he held public meetings in Nandakumar and Kanthi South in Purba Medinipur.Yogi campaigned for the assembly elections in West Bengal.5 Major Points from Yogi's Speech1. BJP government will treat the riotersYogi said- Bengal has now started moving towards change. Today it is painful to see the plight of Bengal. First Congress, then the Left parties and now TMC have ruined it. Mamata Banerjee's government has made Bengal bankrupt. TMC has turned Bengal's land of nationalism into a land of appeasement. It has been turned into a land of loot, plunder and anarchy.He said - As soon as Bengal's name comes up, one remembers the two great men who gave us the National Anthem and National Song. In Ayodhya, a movement for Ram Janmabhoomi continued for several hundred years. A large number of kar sevaks had also gone from Bengal. People used to say that the temple would not be built, but when the double engine government came, the temple was built.2. Bengal's farmers are troubled, potatoes are selling at one rupee per kiloYogi said - We are surprised to see what kind of havoc has occurred in Bengal. Worker Suman Padri was shot dead. The homes of workers like Swarup and Palas Ghosh were destroyed. Someone's hand was cut off.Farmers were harassed. Bengal's farmer is feeling exploited. They are not getting proper prices. In UP, potatoes are available at 15-16 rupees per kilo, but in Bengal their price is 1 to 1.5 rupees.Yogi addressed a public meeting in Sonamukhi, Bankura district in Bengal for the assembly election campaign.3. There are many possibilities in Bengal, bring BJP to powerYogi said - Youth are getting jobs in UP. There are new possibilities for the poor. 15 crore people are getting free ration. 10 crore people are getting treatment worth 5 lakh through Ayushman Bharat. 65 lakh poor people have received PM housing.9 lakh youth have been given government jobs. Employment arrangements have been made in industries for 3 crore youth. This work can also be done in Bengal. There are many possibilities in Bengal. You just have to bring BJP to power.4. Mamata's Fear - Lest Muslim Votes Slip AwayYogi said - Recently a Dalit Hindu was murdered in Bangladesh. BJP protested, but Mamata Didi remained silent. She was afraid that if she spoke, her Muslim vote bank might slip away. These vote bank traders want to change Bengal's demography.You have time. Don't let them off the hook. These people work to create obstacles during Navratri celebrations. Now we should not accept these things. This is the best time, we must come together to restore Bengal's former glory.Yogi said - As soon as Bengal's name comes, one remembers the two great men who gave us the national anthem and national song 5. Said in Bengal - Bengal will not remain silent During the speech, Yogi also spoke in Bengali. He said - 'Banglar chup thakbe na' meaning Bengal will not remain silent now. Now khela (game) will end, development will begin. For this, BJP's double engine is necessary.

stories.title: 'Father never allowed his daughter to meet anyone':Relatives claim he avoided taking her to hospital, due to alleged black magic practice
stories.summary: A father lived in the house with his daughter's corpse for 4 months in Meerut. To prevent the smell, he would spray perfume. Finally, the decomposed skeleton of daughter Priyanka was found. Neighbours and relatives suspect that Priyanka's father, Udaybhanu, used to visit babas (godmen) for her treatment. According to neighbours, the father was never seen taking his daughter to the hospital. It is feared that due to faith healing rituals, her condition worsened, leading to her death. To hide the death, Udaybhanu kept sitting with his daughter's corpse hidden in the house. Relatives say the father did not want to get his daughter married. He would not talk to anyone. If someone approached him to discuss this matter, he would evade the conversation. From what we have learned about this case, only a psycho could do such a thing. Dainik Bhaskar team reached that house in Teli Mohalla and tried to understand the entire incident. First, know about the family and the incident- Hid daughter's death for 4 months, wife had also committed suicide In Sadar Teli Mohalla, Udaybhanu Biswas, retired from the Education Department, lived in his house with his 35-year-old daughter Priyanka. In this same house, Udaybhanu Biswas's wife had committed suicide by hanging. Udaybhanu's relatives also have houses around his house. After his wife's death, father and daughter were left alone in this house. For four months, no neighbour had seen daughter, Priyanka. Udaybhanu would often lock the house and go out. When he came once or twice in between, he told neighbors that his daughter was unwell. She is admitted to the hospital. He didn't say anything more than this. But on Friday night (10 April), his relatives living in the neighbourhood became suspicious. They caught Udaybhanu after spotting him sitting at a tea shop in Thaparnagar. They pressured him and asked where his daughter was. Later, when the police arrived and opened the gate of the house to look inside, they found the daughter's skeleton lying on the bed inside. Many empty perfume bottles were found nearby, and a pile of garbage had also accumulated inside the house. During police interrogation, Udaybhanu said that his daughter had died from jaundice. This is her corpse. He loves his daughter so much that he cannot leave her. Now read what people on the ground told... Father-daughter used to go somewhere daily by e-rickshaw Neighbor Kulbhushan Jain said that my shop is right opposite. Every day while opening the shop, I would see the father-daughter going somewhere by e-rickshaw. They would return in the evening. This was their routine. Since they didn't interact much with anyone, we never asked. Otherwise, we never saw them going to a doctor. The daughter would leave the house first and catch an e-rickshaw from the road. The father, Udaybhanu, would follow, and then both would go somewhere. They would return straight in the evening. In this same house, Udaybhanu's wife had committed suicide by hanging. Kept daughter away from phone, didn't give money for expenses There are some other shops right outside Udaybhanu's house. People from the market said that daughter Priyanka seemed somewhat mentally disturbed. Because she would often come out of the house onto the street. Coming onto the street, she would sometimes ask one person or another, through gestures, for some food items. She would say get me cheese or Kurkure, packets of chips. She never gave money. Just took the packet and went back inside the house. We also thought he was mentally weak, so we never asked him or his father for money, even for ₹5-10. We just thought that Udaybhanu had such a strange nature that he neither gave his daughter money for expenses nor gave her a phone. Even though he himself was retired from government service and was receiving a pension. People also said that apart from this house, Udaybhanu had also bought a flat ahead. Which even relatives don't know about. Relatives said- Talked to Priyanka one year ago Upon learning about the incident, Priyanka's cousin, Alpana, also reached the spot. Alpana said that whenever she came here, she would often meet Priyanka and Udaybhanu. I saw Priyanka for the last time about a year ago. She was very sweet-natured. She was quite educated. She had done MCA and MA. She used to study a lot. She didn't work anywhere; she stayed at home. We don't even know why Uncle wasn't getting her married. We told him once or twice to get his daughter married, but he avoided the topic. We also didn't say much more. She had also met at a wedding recently, and we had talked then. We don't think it's suicide, but she had jaundice. We don't know where her treatment was going on. Uncle used to meet at the temple during Durga Puja, and we would talk there. To me, it seems like a case of mental disturbance. Had limited interaction, even with neighbours and relatives Relative Rupa Biswas says, 'Udaybhanu is my uncle's father-in-law. We come and go in front of his house, but we never felt that a corpse was rotting inside the house. Uncle kept saying that Priyanka has jaundice'. She has been admitted to a hospital in Dehradun. We didn't know what was inside the house. Uncle didn't let anyone enter the house. After aunty's suicide, he had reduced talking to everyone. Neither Priyanka nor her father, Udaybhanu, used to talk much with anyone. When Priyanka's mother was alive, she used to meet neighbors and relatives. There used to be visits to their place on birthdays, weddings, or festivals. But Priyanka and Udaybhanu did not talk much with anyone. Both kept to themselves. They had reduced mixing with relatives. Mother also committed suicide due to depression Relatives said that Udaybhanu's wife, Sharmishtha, was also in depression. She never openly told relatives about her problems. But in conversations, she would say that Udaybhanu was involved in tantra-mantra (occult practices). He wouldn't go to a doctor for treatment. He wasn't letting their daughter get married either. Perhaps due to this depression, the wife also committed suicide inside the house. Behaviour changed after wife's suicide Relatives said that the behavior of both Priyanka and her father, Udaybhanu, completely changed after the wife's death. Both father and daughter would remain locked alone inside the house. Even when they went out, they wouldn't talk much to anyone. They had also reduced communication with us. After Aunty's death, relatives never went inside their house. Neither father nor daughter would talk to anyone on their own. Both would leave the house daily. They would go somewhere, but we don't know where they used to go. Then they would return in the evening. Father did this out of sympathy Akanksha is a staff nurse at the medical college. Akanksha said that I had come to Sadar for shopping on Friday. There was a huge crowd here. It was found that a father had beaten his daughter and locked her inside the house. The corpse is rotting inside the mortuary. The police did not let us go inside. But hearing about this incident is very frightening and also feels bad. Priyanka's age was also young. The father would not have wanted his daughter to be separated from him. That's why, out of sympathy, he probably kept his daughter's corpse. His mental condition must also be bad. Kept stopping the stench of the corpse with perfume If we look at the geographical location of Udayabhanu's house, there is a gated lane adjacent to the main road. Udayabhanu's house is the first one on the right side inside the lane. After this, further inside the lane are the houses of Udayabhanu's other brothers and relatives. This is the main route for coming and going. People had to pass by Udaybhanu's house. But in the last 4 months, no one smelled any foul odour from the house. Nor did anyone suspect there was a corpse. Employees come to use the washroom next door. They also did not suspect a corpse. Children come to the neighboring house for tuition. They never smelled any foul odour either, which would indicate that a corpse was decomposing in the house. Udaybhanu kept suppressing all the foul smell by applying perfume. Now read what the police say CO Cantt Navina Shukla says- A skeleton of a young woman has been found in a house that has been closed for many days. During interrogation, her father stated that his daughter died due to illness. In panic, he kept this truth hidden from everyone. The body has been sent for post-mortem. The entire matter is being investigated.

stories.title: Death toll rises to 13 in Vrindavan boat tragedy:BA student and youth bodies recovered, 4 pre-accident videos surface
stories.summary: In Vrindavan, Mathura, the death toll in the boat accident has risen to 13 devotees, while 22 people have been rescued and 3 others are still missing. On Sunday, the rescue operation entered its third day, with around 250 personnel from the Army, NDRF, and SDRF engaged in the search. The search area has now been expanded from 14 km to 20 km. Two more bodies recovered Earlier today, two more bodies were recovered. They were identified as Dinky from Dugri in Ludhiana, Punjab, and Rishabh Sharma from Jagraon. According to officials, the bodies had swollen and floated to the surface of the river. They were pulled out using ropes into a boat. The victims were later identified by their families. Dinky was a final-year BA student, while Rishabh had completed Class 12 and helped his father in work. Four videos recorded before the accident have also surfaced. In these, devotees are seen playing dholak and manjira, immersed in devotion, chanting “Radhe-Radhe” and singing bhajans such as “Nazar Sanwre Lag Na Jaye Kahin”. Earlier recovery and victim details On the second day of the search operation (Saturday), the body of Manik Tandon from Punjab was recovered near Devaraha Baba Ghat. He was engaged and was scheduled to be married in September. His father broke down after seeing his body. How the accident happened The boat carrying 38 devotees overturned on Friday around 3 pm near Kesi Ghat, about 2 km from Shri Banke Bihari Temple. Police have arrested boat operator Pappu Nishad and pontoon bridge contractor Narayan Sharma. Pappu had boarded passengers from Juggal Ghat. A survivor said the boat was about 50 feet from the bank in the Yamuna river when strong winds of around 40 kmph caused it to wobble. Despite warnings from passengers, the boatman did not stop. The boat narrowly escaped hitting the bridge twice, but collided on the third attempt and capsized. Massive search operation continues On Sunday, search operations continued with Army, NDRF, SDRF, and local teams working in coordination. The affected area has been divided into seven sectors, and the search radius has been increased to 20 km. Officials confirmed that 13 deaths have been reported so far, while 3 people remain missing. Bodies surfaced in the river due to swelling and were retrieved using ropes. Officials said the river current and depth (around 25 feet at the accident site) have made the rescue difficult. A large number of personnel and equipment have been deployed to locate the missing devotees. Background of victims and travel group Most devotees were part of a group from Ludhiana’s Jagraon area, who had travelled to Vrindavan on a four-day religious trip. The group had arrived on Friday after travelling in two buses. Authorities have also arrested the boat operator and pontoon contractor, while investigation continues into safety lapses, including overloading and lack of life jackets. stories.title: Preparations for UP BJP reshuffle intensify, Vinod Tawde reaches Lucknow:Meets Brajesh Pathak; plans to interact with Keshav Maurya in evening
stories.summary: Political activity in Uttar Pradesh has intensified over the formation of the BJP’s new organisational team. The party’s National General Secretary Vinod Tawde reached Lucknow on Sunday and began a series of one-on-one meetings with senior leaders at the party office. He has already met Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak. Tawde is likely to meet former state president Bhupendra Chaudhary in the afternoon and Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya later in the evening. He is also holding separate discussions with the party’s state general secretaries. He will remain in Lucknow on Monday as well. Sources say Tawde is gathering feedback from workers and MLAs on ground realities and will submit a report to the party high command. Based on this, the new UP BJP team and key political appointments are expected to be finalised. Earlier, BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary had met Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath after returning from Delhi on Saturday. Brajesh Pathak said that organizational processes keep running in BJP; this is nothing new Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, who reached the State BJP office, said that Organizational processes keep running continuously in the BJP. This is nothing new. We all work on the instructions of the leadership. He said- We are working to take PM Modi's welfare schemes for the poor to every person. Under CM Yogi's leadership, UP's law and order is being praised in every household. In 2027, we will form the government with a massive majority. 'Why is Akhilesh playing hide and seek on the women's reservation?' The Deputy CM also attacked Akhilesh Yadav. He said that he feels that just as property is transferred on the basis of a will, power is also transferred in the same way. But, this is not the case. Whoever the public blesses, runs the state. If you dare to speak on a woman's reservation, then speak openly. Why are you playing hide and seek? Brajesh Pathak said - Under CM Yogi's leadership, UP's law and order is being praised in every household. Preparation for organizational changes after 3 years According to party sources, after the appointment of BJP's National President Nitin Nabin, the party is now moving forward to prepare new leadership teams in the states as well. As part of this strategy, changes are being prepared in the UP BJP organization after about 3 years. Sources say that in the new team, some office bearers who have been holding positions for a long time may be removed, while several new faces are likely to get a place in the organization. Pankaj Chaudhary and Dharampal Singh have already held discussions with the party's national leaders in Delhi regarding the formation of the state organization. After consensus has been reached on several names, the focus is now on maintaining caste and regional balance in the organization. It is being reported that due to the greater influence of Purvanchal in the government and organization, Western UP, Awadh, Bundelkhand, and Kashi regions may now be given more representation in the organization. Decision may also be taken on appointments to commissions Meanwhile, the process of appointing chairpersons to various commissions, boards, and corporations, including the Minority Commission and Kinnar Development Board in the state, may begin from next week. Actually, last year, the matter of discontent regarding appointments to the Women's Commission had reached Delhi. Keeping this in view, the party leadership has sent Vinod Tawde as an observer this time, so that a final decision can be taken only after discussions with all parties. New members are elected every 3 years The current organizational team of UP BJP was formed by Bhupendra Chaudhary on March 25, 2023. At that time, he was the state president. The rule is that members should be elected every 3 years afresh. Therefore, state president Pankaj Chaudhary has to form his team anew.

stories.title: Cancer super specialty hospital to be built in Varanasi:Preparations have accelerated to set up 100-bed health centre in the city
stories.summary: Varanasi draws patients not only from nearby districts but also from other states, leading to long waiting times at major institutions like BHU. In a significant relief for cancer patients, preparations have accelerated to set up a 100-bed cancer care hospital in the city. The proposed facility will be equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructure. The Arajline development block has been identified for the project, and the search for suitable land is underway. The Kalyan Singh Cancer Institute in Lucknow has been designated as the nodal agency for its development. The move follows a recent decision by the Yogi government to establish modern cancer super-specialty hospitals in every division of the state. Chemotherapy and radiotherapy facilities will also be available Currently, a large number of cancer patients are coming to BHU and Pt. Madan Mohan Malaviya Cancer Institute, located in Sundarpur face long waiting times. The construction of the new hospital will provide significant relief to cancer patients. Here, along with consultation, all tests will also be conducted. Patients will not need to go elsewhere for chemotherapy and radiotherapy. After the hospital is built, a complete team of cancer specialists will also be appointed here. In conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Additional Director (Health) of Varanasi Division, Dr. N.D. Sharma, said that the work of identifying the land has been almost completed. The construction of this hospital will provide considerable relief to cancer patients coming from several districts and neighboring states. More than 35 thousand patients annually The Cancer Institute, located in Varanasi, receives an average of more than 35 thousand new cancer patients every year. Patients from Varanasi district, along with Jaunpur, Mirzapur, Azamgarh, Ghazipur, Chandauli, as well as Bihar and Jharkhand, reach here. Almost the same number of patients come to the Oncology Department of BHU as well. In such a situation, there is a long waiting period for cancer patients here.

stories.title: Heat intensifies in Gorakhpur as day progresses:Dusty winds increase trouble, signs of heatwave in coming days
stories.summary: The effect of the heat started showing as soon as the strong sun came out on Sunday morning in Gorakhpur. Upon going outside, a burning sensation is felt on the face and in the eyes. Over the past few days, as the day progressed, the sun became more intense, and by afternoon, the condition became distressing. The dusty winds blowing along with the strong sun are becoming a major problem for people. Wind is blowing in the city at a speed of 35 to 40 kilometers per hour, due to which dust is flying everywhere. People walking on the road, especially two-wheeler riders, appeared more troubled. Complaints of difficulty in breathing and burning sensations in the eyes are also increasing due to dust. See 3 pictures... Today's temperature and weather conditions According to the Meteorological Department, today the maximum temperature is expected to be around 36 degrees Celsius and the minimum 22 degrees Celsius. The weather will remain dry and hot throughout the day. There is no possibility of rain in the coming days, so there is no hope of relief from the heat either. Light clouds may be visible here and there, but there will be no effect. The Meteorological Department has not issued any warning for now, but has mentioned that temperatures will rise rapidly in the coming days. It is estimated that the temperature may reach 40 to 42 degrees. Along with this, the possibility of hot winds has also been indicated. In such a situation, going out during the afternoon may become even more difficult. Air quality has also deteriorated Due to dusty winds, the Air Quality Index (AQI) has reached between 100 to 120, which is not considered good. Because of this, children, elderly people, and respiratory patients may face more problems. Issues like eye irritation, sore throat, and breathing difficulties are being reported. Weather will remain the same for the next 5 to 7 days There will not be much change in the weather for the next 5 to 7 days. The maximum temperature will remain between 36 to 39 degrees, and the minimum between 21 to 24 degrees. Strong sunshine and dusty winds will continue. The possibility of rain is very low. Temperature will cross 40 by the end of April As the month progresses, the heat will intensify further. After Wednesday, the temperature may cross 40 degrees, and conditions similar to heat waves may develop. In such circumstances, people are being advised to avoid sunlight during the day, cover their heads when going out, and drink plenty of water.

stories.title: Mirzapur advocate murder case accused shot in encounter:Shot in both legs; lawyer was murdered during morning walk
stories.summary: In Mirzapur, police arrested the ₹50,000-rewarded accused Rajendra Sonkar in an encounter on Saturday night for the murder of senior lawyer Rajiv Singh. Sonkar was shot in both legs during the exchange of fire and was later carried by police personnel to a vehicle before being admitted to the divisional hospital. SP Aparna Rajak Kaushik said the police team was checking vehicles at Baraudha intersection when the accused, arriving on a bike, tried to flee on spotting them. During the chase, he opened fire at the police, prompting retaliatory action in which he was injured. Earlier that morning, at around 7:15 am, 45-year-old lawyer Rajiv Singh was shot dead near his house while out for a morning walk. The accused fired at him from point-blank range, hitting him in the chest. He died on the spot. The attacker fled with an accomplice after the incident. The entire incident was captured on CCTV. Police had formed five teams and announced a ₹50,000 reward for Sonkar’s arrest. He was caught within 15 hours, while the search for his accomplice is still underway. See pictures of the encounter spot- Incident recorded on CCTV; attacker's bike didn't start for quite some time Lawyer's wife is village head, family lives in the city Originally a resident of Devri village in the Vindhyachal police station area, Rajeev Singh alias Rinku was living in Katra Kotwali. He had purchased land here in 2011 and built a house. He was living here because of his children's education. He used to commute to court from here. In the village, his wife, Pratibha Singh (40), is the Pradhan (village head). He himself had been Pradhan twice. Due to this, he had to frequently visit the village as well. He has 2 sons: Om (18) and Sarthak (12). Accused has also contested Pradhan elections The SP had informed that the main accused, Rajendra Sonkar, was a resident of the lawyer's village, Devri. He had contested the Pradhan elections. He had an ongoing electoral rivalry with Rajeev's wife, Pratibha Singh. Rajendra lives on rent in Katwaru's Pura, that is, near the lawyer's house. He already knew at what time Rajeev left home for his morning walk every day. He committed the crime after plotting the entire conspiracy. The investigation revealed that the accused had a case under the Arms Act registered against him in 2020. In that case, Rajiv Singh was representing Rajendra Sonkar. Family members stated that, being from the same village, Rajiv often helped Rajendra financially as well. The police informed that Rajendra Sonkar has been to jail three times before. He is also addicted to drugs. Accused considered Rajendra like a brother The deceased lawyer's father, Jata Shankar Singh, said that he considered Rajendra like a brother. He also used to plead his cases. Whenever there was any dispute, he would settle the matter through reconciliation. The reason for the murder is old enmity. He said that Rajiv Singh was the village head of Devri twice. When it became a women's seat, his wife, Pratibha Singh, is the village head. Gun was pointed at the lawyer 7 months ago, too Neighbors had informed that Rajendra Sonkar had attacked Rajiv Singh about 7 months ago by stopping him on the road. He had taken out a pistol from his bike's carrier, pointed it at Rajiv Singh, and assaulted him. Rajiv Singh had also filed a complaint in this matter at Katra Kotwali, but no action was taken by the police in time. Neighbour Manish Dubey had said that Rajendra Sonkar used to come home often. After a dispute for a few months, his visits stopped. After that, he was often seen loitering near the house in the morning. He has already been accused of murdering a lawyer earlier. He has murdered his grandmother and occupied the residence located in Danghar Mohalla of the city.

stories.title: Kidney transplants carried out in filmy style in Kanpur:Teams flew in, hospital staff sent on leave; inside the racket
stories.summary: Police have busted an illegal kidney transplant racket in Kanpur, exposing a disturbing network exploiting both the poor and the wealthy. The syndicate allegedly lured financially vulnerable people into selling their kidneys, convincing them that one can survive with a single organ. At the same time, deals worth crores were struck with affluent patients, who were provided illegal transplants. The transplant team reportedly flew in from Delhi, conducted surgeries under the cover of darkness, and left immediately after. Shockingly, the procedures were not carried out by qualified surgeons but by OT technicians. No eurologist has been identified in the case so far, even though such transplants are not possible without one, raising serious questions about how the operations were conducted. This entire case is like a movie. It has greed, fraud, and deception. What it doesn't have is a hero. Everyone is a villain. Today in Sunday Big Story, we learn about the complete Kanpur kidney case... Ahuja Hospital: The center point of the story About 2 years ago, Ahuja Hospital was started in the Kalyanpur area of Kanpur. Dr. Preeti Ahuja and Dr. Surjit Singh Ahuja started it. Both are husband and wife and are MBBS, MD. Earlier, they used to see patients in different hospitals in Kanpur, but then they set up their own hospital. They contacted big and renowned doctors of the city and convinced them to sit in their hospital. A total of 27 doctors used to sit in Ahuja Hospital. The hospital had arrangements for 35 beds. There were high-tech ICUs, NICUs, and operation theaters. Overall, a perfect hospital. Dr. Preeti is the Vice President of Kanpur in the Indian Medical Association (IMA). She is a Medical Officer at the State Bank of India. She is the Secretary of the Diabetes Association and a member of the Physician Forum of Specialist Doctors. Preeti holds positions in so many organisations that if any complaint reaches the higher authorities, they will think ten times before taking action. Preeti always maintained good relations with senior officers in the medical field. Broker Shivam built a network, lured everyone with the temptation of earning money Everything was going fine, but a few days later, Shivam Agarwal alias Shivam Kada entered the story. Shivam from Jalaun had run away to Kanpur at the age of 15. He didn't go to school after 8th grade. He did odd jobs in Kanpur, then became an ambulance driver. He built connections with hospitals and doctors. When he met Dr. Preeti, he became exclusively associated with Ahuja Hospital. Shivam Kada's connections kept growing not just in Kanpur, but in different parts of UP. He met Dr. Rohit from Noida. Rohit was an old player in the kidney transplant game. A deal was struck between the two. After this, Shivam got busy finding clients. For this, he made social media his medium. He created channels on Telegram. He became active on gaming apps. These were gaming apps where money was involved. Many people had already lost. During gameplay, through conversations, one could gauge how far the person on the other end would go for money. The work that Shivam was doing in Kanpur, the same work Dr. Afzal was doing in Meerut and Naveen Pandey was doing in Prayagraj-Noida. All of them would search for people who desperately needed money for kidneys and who would be ready to sell their kidneys. Deal made for ₹6 lakhs, sold for ₹90 lakh There are 2 victims in the kidney case. One is Ayush from Bihar, the second is Parul from Muzaffarnagar. Ayush needed money, and Parul needed a kidney. Between these two was an entire illegal system that would go to any extent for profiteering. Ayush and Shivam came in contact through Telegram. Both had discussions. When money was discussed, the deal was finalised at ₹6 lakh. Ayush was to receive ₹3 lakh before the operation and ₹3 lakh after the operation. On the other hand, Dr. Afzal from Meerut had prepared Parul from Muzaffarnagar for a kidney transplant. This deal was finalised for around ₹90 lakh. Ayush's conversation with Afzal started on Telegram. Afzal assured Ayush that the operation would be done before his MBA exam in May. In between, Ayush changed his mind, but Afzal and others convinced him again to sell his kidney. Preeti and Surjeet took charge of the management The date of March 29th was chosen for the kidney transplant. The location, as always, was Ahuja Hospital in Kanpur. It was also decided that after removing the kidney, Ayush would be admitted to Medi Life Hospital and Parul to Preeti Hospital. This had always been the practice. Dr. Narendra Singh alias Nandu, owner of Preeti Hospital, and Dr. Ram Prakash Kushwaha and Dr. Rajesh Kumar, owners of Medi Life, were already set up. They received more than ₹1-1 lakh each for admitting these patients. Ahuja Hospital kept ₹2 lakh 75 thousand for itself for one operation. The operations management was handled by Dr. Rohit from Noida. He is currently absconding. Dr. Rohit had formed an entire team. As soon as things were finalised, he would prepare the team. In his team, the kidney transplant work was done by Mudassar Ali from Dwarka, Delhi. Mudassar is not a urologist who specialises in this work. He is an OT technician. To assist Mudassar, two other OT technicians, Rajesh Kumar and Kuldeep Singh Raghav, also came from Ghaziabad. According to the plan, on March 28, Dr. Afzal reached Kanpur from Meerut with Parul. On the other side, Ayush was also admitted to the hospital. For March 29, Dr. Rohit booked flight tickets for Mudassar Ali, Rajesh, and Kuldeep. The entire team always left Delhi at night. The responsibility of picking up and dropping off at the airport was Saifi Parvez's. He used to stay with Afzal from Meerut. When the team arrived, he would receive everyone along with some other drivers. On the day of operation, the staff had a holiday The operation was scheduled for March 29 at Ahuja Hospital. Three days before that, the number of patients started decreasing. Dr. Preeti and Dr. Surjit would decide that on the day of the kidney transplant, no serious patient should remain in the hospital. More than half of the hospital staff would be given leave. The kidney transplant work would take place between 3 to 4 AM. At that time, only a few patients and their relatives in the hospital would be sleeping. There was no fear of investigation either. The operation took place on the night of March 29. The team that had come from Noida-Delhi returned by flight. Parul was shifted to Preeti Hospital on the morning of March 30, and Ayush was shifted to Medi Life Hospital. Their treatment began here. On this same day, the police received some information about the illegal kidney transplant case. It was also confirmed by intelligence inputs. After this, DCP West, Crime Branch, and SOG, all three together, raided Ahuja Hospital, Preeti Hospital, and Medi Life Hospital. The entire story unfolded from here. Kidney syndicate extends to South Africa Initially it seemed like just one case, but as the investigation progressed, a large syndicate came to light. Police arrested Dr. Preeti Ahuja, Dr. Surjit Ahuja, Preeti Hospital owner Narendra Singh, Medi Life Hospital's Ram Prakash Maurya and Rajesh Kumar, and ambulance driver Shivam Agarwal. After the arrest, during interrogation, many secrets were revealed. Several videos were found on Shivam Agarwal alias Shivam Kada's phone. In one video, Meerut's Dr. Afzal was lying with bundles of 500-rupee notes. This was ₹15 lakh. In another video, Shivam Agarwal, who has only studied up to 8th grade, is seen examining an African girl named Arabica. This shows that this syndicate has spread not just within the country, but to South Africa as well. It was found that approximately ₹2 crore were taken from Arabica in the name of a kidney transplant. No surgeon has been caught yet The biggest point in the entire case is that among the arrests made so far, there is no urologist, that is, kidney doctor. The police had recovered CCTV footage from Ahuja Hospital on the night of March 29-30. After the operation, 3 people were seen returning by car. One of these cars went towards Ghaziabad, which had Mudassar Ali, Kuldeep Raghav, and Rajesh Kumar. The second car went towards Meerut. It had Dr. Rohit, Afzal, Vaibhav, and Amit Sawar. The third car has become a puzzle in this case, as it went towards Lucknow. It is being reported that this car had one surgeon and two doctors from a private hospital. All three were also visible in the operating theatre's CCTV camera. But who they are, which hospital in Lucknow they were connected with, no information about this has reached the police so far. The police have also conducted raids at some places in Lucknow in search of them. More than 50 brokers and doctors involved in the racket A recording found on Shivam's phone revealed that he had facilitated 40 to 50 kidney transplants. In one video, standing outside Punjab's Maninder Ahuja Hospital, he was saying that these people took ₹43 lakh from me, but haven't done the kidney transplant yet. Now all of them have been caught. All our money has sunk. We have no option left except to commit suicide. In the initial 4 days, 9 accused were caught. After interrogation, many more names came to light. Kanpur Police has formed 10 teams to investigate the case. These teams are conducting raids in Lucknow, Noida, Delhi, Ghaziabad and Kanpur. Police have not been able to catch Dr. Rohit, Dr. Afzal, Dr. Mudassar Ali, Dr. Amit, Dr. Vaibhav, and Naveen Pandey yet. After they are caught, more layers of the case will come to light.

stories.title: Man loses 9 family members in Vrindavan accident:Boat overturned during kirtan, no life jackets provided, survivors blame crane work
stories.summary: "I watched my own family drowning and could do nothing. I lost 9 members of my family in the accident, including my son and wife. In just a few minutes, a journey filled with happiness turned into mourning. Our world was destroyed." Saying this, Vijay Kumar, who lost his loved ones in the boat accident in Vrindavan and was himself on that boat, breaks down crying. This accident occurred on April 10. 13 people died in it, and the search for 3 continues. Vijay described the scene of the last 7 minutes of the accident. Vijay said that many people had gathered on the boat because of the kirtan (devotional singing). Vijay said that when our boat reached near the newly constructed bridge, the crane pulled the iron dam installed there. Just then, a strong wind came, and the boat went towards the pillar. During this, the rope got entangled, and the boat capsized after hitting the pillar. Vijay said that as soon as all the people fell into the water, they started screaming. I, my son, and some other people who knew how to swim, kept struggling in the water. Son Madhur kept fighting to save his mother, but while trying to save her, he drowned. We brought him out, but could not save him. Read the full report The story of the last 7 minutes in Vijay's words Trip organizer Yashu said that they don't even provide life jackets there...

stories.title: Minister Khanna, BSP’s single seat in danger:SIR disrupts 114 seats; BJP-SP's calculations disrupted
stories.summary: 2.04 crore voters' names were cut from the final SIR list released on April 10 in UP. In the 2022 assembly elections, there were 114 seats where the victory-defeat margin was less than 10 thousand. After SIR, these seats have seen a reduction of 16 thousand to 1.18 lakh voters. In such a situation, these seats have come into the danger zone. The reason is that if the reduced voters were core voters of the party that won by a narrow margin last time, then the result there in 2027 could completely reverse. Out of these 114 seats, the BJP had won 63, SP 41, and other parties had won 10 seats. How much will the electoral game of 2027 change after SIR? Will the equations change on seats with low margins? Which party will suffer more loss? Read the special report In 2022, 15 seats had a margin of less than a thousand Looking at the 2022 assembly elections, there were 15 seats where the winning margin was less than a thousand. Of these, 10 seats had a margin of less than 500 votes. Out of these 15 seats, the BJP and its allied parties won 9. Meanwhile, 6 seats went to the SP alliance. Now, on these seats, votes have decreased by 21 to 72 thousand. Senior journalist Hemant Tiwari says, ‘Looking at the current situation, these seats have come into the danger zone for the BJP. Comparing the results of the last two elections shows that the win-loss margin in 2022 was much less compared to 2017’. This is why the BJP's winning margin on more than 60 seats was less than 10 thousand. BJP's held seats saw the biggest vote decline In 2022, there were 99 seats where the margin of victory was less than 10 thousand. Of these, the BJP got 55, SP got 35, RLD got 3, Nishad and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party got 2-2 each, and the BSP and Congress got 1-1 seat each. Political observers believe that these seats have also come into the danger zone. During the SIR itself, CM Yogi had warned about these seats in coordination meetings with the party, government and Sangh. In western UP and Bundelkhand, 22 seats had witnessed victory-defeat margins of less than 10 thousand votes. Out of these, BJP had won 13 seats. Meanwhile, SP, along with RLD, had registered victory on 9 seats. The West has a larger Muslim and Jat population, but the equations are not the same as in 2022. RLD has broken its alliance with SP and joined the BJP. In such a situation, SP may suffer losses on seats with narrow margins. Votes decreased by 10 times more than the winning margin in Minister Suresh Khanna's seat In the 2022 Assembly elections in Central UP, there were 50 seats with a margin of less than 10 thousand. There was a direct contest between SP and BJP here. Out of these, BJP captured 30 seats while the SP won 20. OBC voters like Lodhi, Maurya, and Kurmi-Yadav dominate this belt. After SIR, the equations of both parties have been disrupted here. Votes have decreased by up to 10 times compared to the winning-losing margin here. This includes Finance Minister Suresh Khanna's Shahjahanpur seat as well. In 2022, he won by 9313 votes, while more than 1 lakh votes were reduced in the seat. The special thing is that this seat has more than 30% Muslim voters. In such a situation, BJP's equation in the seat appears to be deteriorating. Challenge for Congress and BSP in Purvanchal In Purvanchal, the victory-defeat margin was less than 10 thousand on 27 seats. In 2022, SP had contested elections in alliance with Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP). This alliance proved stronger than the BJP in this region. BJP won 12 seats, while SP won 9. SBSP and Nishad Party won 2-2 seats each, while BSP and Congress won 1-1 seat each. Now Subaspa is with the BJP. This belt has a larger population of the backward classes. BJP has an alliance with SBSP and Nishad Party, which represent these backward classes. After SIR, the seats of Congress MLA Virendra Chaudhary from Farenda and BSP's sole MLA Umashankar Singh from Rasra appear to be in jeopardy. The reason is that Congress's Virendra won by 1246 votes while BSP's Umashankar Singh won by 6583 votes. Whereas in SIR, Farenda saw a decrease of about 29 thousand votes, and the Rasra seat saw a decrease of 37 thousand votes. Meanwhile, BJP had won the Duddhi seat, but MLA Ram Dular Gond was convicted in a rape case. In the by-election, this seat was won by SP's Vijay Singh Gond, but he too has passed away due to illness. Currently, this seat is vacant. Senior journalist Anand Rai says, ‘Duplicates, transfers and names of deceased have been removed from the final list issued after SIR. It could not be ascertained which caste group has migrated the most’. There is a common perception that Yadavs and Muslims are SP voters. Similarly, Dalits are considered BSP voters while upper castes and extremely backward castes are considered BJP voters.

stories.title: Thief's neck stuck between shutter and wall:Hung for 6 hours, rescued by cutting shutter in Ghaziabad
stories.summary: A thief got stuck between the wall and shutter of a clinic in Ghaziabad. The thief was entering through the roof to steal from the clinic. While climbing down, he got trapped between the shutter and concrete wall. His neck got stuck between the shutter and wall. He remained stuck in that condition for about 6 hours. When the doctor arrived at the clinic on Saturday afternoon, he came to know about the situation. He immediately informed the police. The police who reached the spot informed the fire brigade. The fire brigade team arrived and conducted the rescue. The thief was safely brought out by cutting the shutter. The case is from Indirapuram police station area. First see 2 pictures.... Now know the complete matter Body came out, neck got stuck The name of the caught thief is Abhishek. He is originally a resident of Bihar. According to police, on Saturday morning around 7 o'clock he was entering a clinic located in Abhay Khand to commit theft. There was a little space at the upper part of the shutter. Abhishek climbed onto the roof. He started entering through this space. His torso somehow got inside the clinic, but his neck got stuck between the shutter and the wall. He tried hard to get out. He kept struggling, but couldn't get free. He remained trapped in that condition. Around 12 noon, the doctor reached the clinic. He saw that a thief was stuck near the shutter. He immediately informed the police. Police reached the spot. A fire brigade team was also called along. Thief was rescued by cutting the shutter Seeing the seriousness of the incident, the fire service team immediately started the rescue operation. The team carefully cut the shutter with the help of special equipment. After this, the youth's neck was safely extracted. During the entire rescue, the team exercised complete caution so that he would not suffer any additional injury. After the rescue, the thief was safely brought out. CFO Rahul Pal said On Saturday around 1 pm, Vaishali Fire Station received information that a youth was trapped between the shutter and wall of a clinic. On receiving the information, the fire brigade team reached the spot. Half of the youth's body was stuck inside and half outside. The team broke the shutter and safely brought the youth out and handed him over to the police.

stories.title: High-profile Kanpur rave busted:140 youths, IIT students among those intoxicated
stories.summary: Police raided a high-profile rave party late Friday night in the city and found around 140 youths, including students from reputed institutes such as IIT, in an intoxicated state. Many of those present were from Kanpur, while others had come from Delhi, Haryana and Rajasthan. The party was being held at Stella Naomi Club in NRI City under the name ‘Sonic Shift’. Police said several drugs were recovered from the spot, including LSD, cocaine, marijuana, charas and hashish. The organiser and the alleged drug supplier have been arrested and sent to jail. Police said the party was organised through invitations sent on Instagram. Acting on a tip-off about drug use, the Special Operations Group (SOG) launched a covert operation under “Operation White Powder”, which is being led by trainee IPS officer Sumit Sudhakar Ramteke. Undercover entry, late-night raid According to Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal, two police personnel entered the party after purchasing passes worth ₹1,000. Around 2:30 am, when most attendees were under the influence of drugs and alcohol, the undercover team alerted backup units. A raid was then carried out. As police entered, panic broke out inside the club and many tried to flee. However, the main gate was shut, preventing escape. Police detained those present and later released most of them after issuing warnings. Organiser, supplier arrested The organiser was identified as Mohammad Fardeen alias Gumti, a resident of Jajmau, while the alleged drug supplier, Mohit Jaiswal, lives near Sant Nagar Chowraha. Police said Jaiswal had brought LSD from Pushkar in Rajasthan to sell at the party. Investigators said drugs were being distributed among partygoers, and large LED screens and projectors were installed to enhance the psychedelic effects. Drugs and cash recovered Police recovered small quantities of multiple narcotics, including LSD, marijuana, charas, cocaine and hashish. They also seized smoking equipment and ₹49,000 in cash from the venue. Officials said further raids are being conducted at other clubs in the city as part of the ongoing crackdown on narcotics. What is LSD? LSD (Lysergic Acid Diethylamide) is a powerful hallucinogenic drug that affects the brain and alters perception. After consumption, users may see or hear things that are not real, a condition often described as a “trip”. Its effects usually begin within 15 to 30 minutes and can last for several hours. During this period, colours, lights and sounds appear more intense, and users may feel strongly drawn to music and visual effects.

stories.title: Trader suffers heart attack during anti-encroachment drive, dies:Action by Lucknow Municipal Corporation outside shops; panic after demolition
stories.summary: A businessman died suddenly during an anti-encroachment drive by the Lucknow Municipal Corporation in Rajajipuram’s E Block on Saturday, triggering tension in the area. According to reports, the civic team had reached the locality to remove illegal encroachments. As the drive began, the businessman present at the spot protested. During the argument, his health suddenly worsened and he collapsed. Eyewitnesses said he was rushed towards a nearby hospital, but he had stopped breathing by then. The municipal team had demolished a shop in the same area during the operation. Soon after the incident, a large number of traders gathered in the market, leading to a tense situation. Additional Municipal Commissioner Arun Kumar Gupta said the drive continued peacefully till around 3:30 pm and no untoward incident occurred during the action. He added that the traders’ association of Rajajipuram E Block had itself requested the corporation to remove encroachments. Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Kumar also denied any link between the civic action and the trader’s death, calling such claims rumours. However, the deceased’s family has alleged that he suffered a heart attack due to stress caused by the demolition drive. Police have sent the body for post-mortem, and an investigation is underway. The situation in the area remains tense. Further updates are awaited.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. Centre approves 2% DA hike for central govt employees, pensioners The Union Cabinet on Saturday, April 18, approved a 2% hike in Dearness Allowance (DA) for central government employees and pensioners, raising it from 58% to 60% of basic pay. The revision, effective from January 2026, will also apply to pensioners through a corresponding increase in Dearness Relief (DR), leading to higher monthly payouts. 2. Yogi asks Mamata to vacate West Bengal throne, targets TMC rule Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath urged Mamata Banerjee to step down, claiming BJP will form government in West Bengal. He accused TMC of backing infiltrators and vowed to end “love jihad”, as “Bulldozer Baba” slogans echoed at a Mathabhanga rally. 3. Aparna Yadav protests over women’s bill setback, burns SP-Congress flags In Lucknow, BJP leader Aparna Yadav staged a late-night protest over the Women’s Reservation Bill setback, burning SP and Congress flags. She accused the opposition of blocking women’s rights, calling them “pretentious” and warning that “Nari Shakti” will respond strongly. 4. Iran reimposes restrictions on Hormuz over US blockade on ports Iran's IRGC has issued a statement claiming that control of the Strait of Hormuz has now “returned to its previous state” due to the US’s continuing blockade of Iranian ports. In a statement cited by Iran’s IRIB broadcaster, the IRGC command said the US has “continued acts of piracy and maritime theft under the guise of a so-called blockade”. 5. Stay on FIR against Rahul Gandhi: Allahabad High Court flags no-notice lapse, halts action Stay on FIR order against Rahul Gandhi: Allahabad High Court revisits directive, flags lack of prior notice as legally untenable; Justice Subhash Vidyarthi halts action in alleged dual citizenship case, orders fresh hearing on April 20, petitioner plans move to Supreme Court against rollback decision. 6. Tehsildar accuses Firozabad DM of corruption, harassment; seeks CM’s intervention In Firozabad, Tehsildar Rakhi Sharma accused the District Magistrate of harassment and demanding costly gadgets, alleging her salary was withheld for eight months. She claimed sustained pressure over complaints and has sought intervention from Yogi Adityanath for justice. 7. NDA women MPs protest over Women's Reservation Bill defeat NDA leaders are protesting nationwide over the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill not passing in the Lok Sabha. Delhi CM Rekha Gupta marched towards Rahul Gandhi’s residence with women MPs. Workers burnt Rahul Gandhi’s effigy. Police used water cannons to disperse the crowd. 8. Bomb threat to Jhansi judge, court security tightened ahead of April 30 A special judge in Jhansi received a bomb threat via letter alleging bias against a community. Police registered a case and launched a probe, while security was intensified at the court and the judge’s residence ahead of the warned April 30 attack. 9. Kanpur gas crisis deepens, residents queue for hours in heat Residents in Kanpur face severe cooking gas shortage, waiting hours under scorching sun with umbrellas. Many return empty-handed amid delayed supply. Locals allege black marketing and poor communication, as bookings remain pending despite repeated visits to distribution centres. 10. Himanta accuses Mamata of selling land to Bangladeshis for votes Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Saturday alleged that West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee had “sold land” to illegal Bangladeshi migrants for electoral gains. Addressing a rally in Kalimpong, Sarma claimed that the state had deteriorated under her leadership and called for her removal from power.

stories.title: Varanasi ₹40 lakh jewellery theft busted:Two ₹25,000-reward thieves arrested after scanning 250+ CCTV clips
stories.summary: The Varanasi Police Commissionerate has arrested two accused involved in a major house theft and recovered jewellery worth around ₹40 lakh, officials said. The incident took place in Gayatri Nagar under the Lanka Police Station Varanasi area. The victim’s family had gone to their native village on March 31, 2026. When they returned on April 4, they found the lock of their house broken and ancestral jewellery along with other valuables missing. Police registered a case and launched an investigation soon after receiving the complaint. Case cracked using CCTV footage During the probe, police scanned more than 250 CCTV camera recordings from the area. Based on this extensive surveillance, the suspects were identified. Investigators found that the accused used to roam in residential areas posing as street vendors. They would target locked houses and carry out thefts when they found an opportunity. Accused carried ₹25,000 reward each On April 17, 2026, police arrested both accused — Mohammad Sharik Jamal Ansari (38) and Reyaz Akram (27) — from Kashipuram Colony in the Seer Govardhanpur area. According to police, a reward of ₹25,000 each had been announced for their arrest. An official from the Bhelupur ACP office said that stolen jewellery worth about ₹40 lakh has been recovered from their possession. The recovered items include gold and silver necklaces, bangles, rings, earrings, and anklets.

stories.title: UP STF nabs main accused in Noida labour violence:NIT BTech graduate caught in Tamil Nadu, non-bailable warrant issued by court
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) has arrested Aditya Anand, the main accused in the Noida labour unrest case, from Tamil Nadu. He had been on the run for several days, while six teams of Noida Police were trying to trace him. Police said Anand, along with two others — Rupesh Rai and Manisha — allegedly instigated workers and played a key role in triggering the unrest. The three had created multiple WhatsApp groups on April 9 and 10 to mobilise workers, officials said. A case had been registered against Anand at the Phase-2 police station in Gautam Buddha Nagar district. A local court had also issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against him. According to investigators, the unrest was not spontaneous but planned in advance. During the probe, police also found indications of a possible international link. Officials said two social media handles on X (formerly Twitter) — @Proudindiannavi and @Mir_Ilyas_INC — were allegedly being operated from Pakistan and were active during the period of unrest. Further investigation in the case is underway. Noida violence accused held in Tamil Nadu after multi-state search Aditya Anand, who carried a ₹1 lakh reward, has been arrested from a railway station in Tiruchirappalli after a multi-state search operation. Police teams used technical surveillance and conducted raids in several states before tracking him down. Anand is a BTech graduate from National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur. He was present in Noida during the labour unrest. Police allege he created multiple WhatsApp groups through QR codes to mobilise workers and delivered provocative speeches to incite violence. Online network used to fuel unrest Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh said misleading and inflammatory content was circulated through social media accounts to disturb law and order in Gautam Buddh Nagar. These accounts were operated using VPNs to hide identities. Investigators said the network had been active for nearly three months. Some IP addresses have links to Pakistan. Authorities are now examining back-end data to trace the full extent of the alleged digital conspiracy. Key role in organising protests Probe agencies said Anand, along with Rupesh Rai and Manisha, played a key role in mobilising workers. The trio was active in Noida on March 31 and April 1. Between April 9 and 10, they allegedly created several WhatsApp groups and called on workers to protest, damage property and turn violent. On April 13, violence broke out across parts of Noida, with mobs pelting stones and setting vehicles on fire. So far, 63 accused have been arrested. Protests turned violent across industrial areas The unrest began on April 9, when factory workers protested over wage demands. With no resolution, workers took to the streets on April 13. Clashes broke out when police intervened. The protest, which began in Phase-2, spread to nearly 10 industrial sectors. In Sector 57, more than 30 factories and offices were vandalised. Companies in Sectors 40 and 60 were surrounded, while a factory gate in Sector 85 was broken. Roads were blocked in multiple sectors and near the DND Flyover. Security forces, including PAC and RAF, were deployed to control the situation. Further attempts at unrest were reported on April 14. Police crackdown and government action Police and paramilitary forces conducted flag marches, while CCTV and drones were used for surveillance. Around 200 workers were detained and cases were filed against about 60 people. Several factories were shut, while others shifted to work-from-home. The Government of Uttar Pradesh has formed a high-level committee to probe the incident. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said strict action would be taken against those behind the unrest. The state government also announced a wage hike of up to ₹3,000 for factory workers, effective from April 1.

stories.title: Stay on FIR order against Rahul Gandhi:Allahabad HC reviews its direction; says action without prior notice not legally appropriate
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court’s Lucknow bench has stayed its own earlier order directing registration of an FIR against Rahul Gandhi in a case related to alleged dual citizenship. The update was published on the court’s website on Saturday. The court said a hearing was held on April 17, where it asked the petitioner and lawyers for the Centre and state whether a notice should be issued to Rahul Gandhi. The lawyers said a notice was not necessary, following which the court initially ordered registration of an FIR. However, before the order was formally issued, Justice Subhash Vidyarthi reviewed the matter again. He noted a 2014 judgment of the High Court, which states that in cases seeking FIR registration, if a plea is dismissed, only a revision petition is maintainable — and the proposed accused must be given notice. Based on this, the court said it would not be appropriate to proceed without issuing notice to Rahul Gandhi. The next hearing has been scheduled for April 20. The petition was filed by S. Vignesh Shishir, a resident of Karnataka. He has made allegations against Rahul Gandhi under the Indian Justice Code, Official Secrets Act, Foreigners Act, and Passport Act. Following the development, the petitioner said he would approach the Chief Justice of India against the decision to withdraw the FIR order. Order to register FIR was given on April 17 The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court on Friday ordered the registration of an FIR against Rahul Gandhi in a case related to alleged dual citizenship. Justice Subhash Vidyarthi directed that the FIR be registered and the matter be handed over to the CBI. The petition was filed by Vignesh Shishir, a BJP worker from Karnataka. Earlier, on January 28, 2026, the MP-MLA court had dismissed his plea, stating that no new or concrete evidence regarding citizenship had been presented. While overturning the lower court’s order, the High Court observed that the magistrate did not need to comment on the truthfulness of the allegations at that stage. Centre submits ‘top secret’ files During the hearing, the court asked the Foreigners Division of the Home Ministry to submit all relevant documents. The Ministry presented the case-related files before the court. The petitioner claimed he had submitted documents indicating that Rahul Gandhi was listed as a voter in the United Kingdom and had records linked to participation in elections there. Case moved from Raebareli to Lucknow The complaint was initially filed in the MP-MLA court in Raebareli. On the petitioner’s request, the High Court transferred the case to Lucknow on December 17, 2025. After the Lucknow court dismissed the plea in January 2026, the petitioner approached the High Court, which first ordered the FIR and later stayed its own order. Similar plea dismissed earlier In 2019, the Supreme Court of India had dismissed a similar petition on Rahul Gandhi’s citizenship. Then Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi said that mentioning someone as a British citizen in company records does not automatically make them a British citizen. The bench had ruled that the petition had no merit and rejected the plea seeking action from the Home Ministry and disqualification of Rahul Gandhi from elections. Three cases against Rahul in Uttar Pradesh Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is currently facing three separate cases in Uttar Pradesh. Lost MP seat in Modi surname case Rahul Gandhi lost his Lok Sabha membership on March 24, 2023, after being convicted by a Gujarat court in the Modi surname defamation case. However, on August 4, 2023, the Supreme Court of India stayed his conviction. Following this, the Lok Sabha Secretariat restored his membership on August 7, 2023.

Codeine cough syrup mastermind’s father denied bail:Booked under PIT NDPS like NSA, action based on SIT report
stories.summary: Bhola Jaiswal, father of alleged codeine cough syrup mastermind Shubham Jaiswal, will not be eligible for bail for one year after being booked under the PIT NDPS Act. The action, considered equivalent to the National Security Act (NSA) in its preventive detention effect, was approved by the state government following a proposal from Sonbhadra police. Superintendent of Police Abhishek Verma said the move was based on findings of a Special Investigation Team (SIT), which identified Bhola Jaiswal as a habitual offender in the illegal codeine cough syrup trade. The approval was granted after a recommendation was sent to the government through Sonbhadra District Magistrate B.N.A. Singh. The order came into effect on April 15. Arrested while attempting to flee Bhola Jaiswal, a resident of Kayastha Tola in Prahlad Ghat, Varanasi, and owner of Shaili Traders, was arrested by Sonbhadra police on December 1, 2025, from Kolkata airport while allegedly trying to leave the country. He is currently lodged in Sonbhadra jail. With the PIT NDPS Act invoked, he will neither be able to apply for bail nor be granted bail for one year. Properties worth ₹36 crore attached Police said properties worth ₹36 crore linked to Bhola Jaiswal have already been attached. Officials added that the process is underway to convert these assets into government property under legal provisions. Smuggling through fake billing: SIT findings According to the SIT probe, Bhola Jaiswal was involved in smuggling codeine-based cough syrup using forged or manipulated bills through his firm, Shaili Traders. The investigation concluded that he was a repeat offender, prompting authorities to initiate preventive detention under PIT NDPS. SP Verma said a detailed dossier was prepared by the SIT and forwarded to the government, which granted approval for the stringent action.

stories.title: Akshaya Tritiya buzz in Gorakhpur:Gold and silver sales may rise by 20%, over 350 vehicles booked
stories.summary: Gorakhpur is seeing strong demand ahead of Akshaya Tritiya, with brisk bookings for gold, silver, cars and bikes. Traders expect jewellery sales to rise by about 20% compared to last year. Jewellers say customers have been booking in advance, helped by relatively lower gold prices. Sanjay Agarwal, Director of Parampara Gems and Jewels, said the market has been active for the past week and sales are likely to grow by around 20% this year. Auto sector sees strong bookings Automobile dealers also report high demand. Around 8–9 car dealerships in the city expect combined sales of over 200 cars on the day. Abhishek Agarwal, MD of Orbit Automobile, said his showroom alone will deliver more than 60 vehicles. Among cars, the Maruti Suzuki Invicto is expected to be the most expensive delivery, while the Maruti Suzuki Vitara is likely to see the highest number of deliveries. Bike demand rises, youth show interest Bike sales are also set to surge. Dealers estimate that more than 400 bikes could be sold across the city. Popular models include the Jawa Bobber, which has strong demand among young buyers, along with the Yamaha MT-15 and Yamaha R15. With around 25 bike agencies in the city, each is expected to sell 15–20 units on average. Many deliveries have already been scheduled for the festival day. Weddings add to festive demand The wedding season is also driving sales. More than 100 weddings are expected to take place in the city on Akshaya Tritiya. About 75% of marriage halls have already been booked, while some families are planning ceremonies at home. Overall, traders and dealers say the festival, along with the start of the wedding season, is boosting consumer spending across sectors.

stories.title: Kanpur gas shortage leaves residents waiting in long queues:Women wait with umbrellas in scorching heat; allege gas black marketing
stories.summary: Residents in Kanpur are facing a severe shortage of cooking gas, with long queues reported across several areas. Many people are standing in line for hours under the scorching sun, yet returning empty-handed due to irregular supply. The administration claims that home delivery services are in place, but residents say the system is not working effectively on the ground. According to them, they first have to queue up to book a cylinder and then wait again separately to receive it. People wait under sun, supply fails to arrive A large number of residents gathered at Bhagwat Indane Gas Service near JK Temple on Friday, hoping to collect their cylinders. Many were seen sitting outside with umbrellas, waiting for the delivery vehicle. However, the gas supply did not arrive for a long time, triggering anger among those waiting. People said they have been visiting the agency repeatedly but are still unable to get cylinders. Residents have urged the administration to fix the system quickly and ensure regular supply to ease their difficulties. ‘Booked in march, still no cylinder,’ say residents Sagar Goyal said he had booked a cylinder on March 25 and received the DAC number on March 26. “I stood in line the whole day, and my turn came around 4 pm. We were told the cylinder would be given on April 18. But now they say it won’t come today,” he said. He alleged that cylinders are being sold illegally in the black market. “Gas vehicles are going to other parts of the city, but not here. Now we are being told to come again on Monday,” he added. People queue from early morning, allege poor communication Another resident, Tribhuvan, said people have been coming to the agency for the past three days. “We were given April 18 as the delivery date. I have been standing here since 8 am, while some people started queuing from 6 am,” he said. He added that the agency should have informed people earlier if the supply was not coming. “If they knew the vehicle wouldn’t arrive today, they should have told us in advance,” he said.

stories.title: Bomb threat to Jhansi judge, security tightened:Letter warns of April 30 attack, alleges bias against community
stories.summary: In Jhansi, Special Judge (SC/ST Act) Aditya Chaturvedi received a bomb threat through a letter sent by post. The letter alleges that the judge has “wrongly punished members of a community” in several cases and warns of a bomb attack inside the court premises by April 30. The letter was received on April 16. The sender’s name was mentioned as Mohammad Saleem Mansuri. On April 17, a district court official informed the City SP in writing. Police registered a case the same night and began an investigation. Security has been increased at the court premises, as well as at the judge’s residence. Letter sent from post office inside court campus Police said preliminary findings indicate that the letter was posted from a post office located within the court premises. The envelope carried the stamp of that post office. Officials have also identified the time at which the letter was sent. CCTV footage from nearby areas is being examined to trace the sender. Police said efforts are underway to identify the accused at the earliest. Initial suspicion points to a possible mischief attempt. Judge’s security increased Assistant Superintendent of Police Ariba Noman said the threat appears to be an attempt to intimidate the judge. She said the matter is being taken seriously, a case has been registered, and an investigation is in progress. Security arrangements at the court and for the judge have been strengthened.

stories.title: Aparna Yadav protests over Woman's Reservation bill setback:Says, 'Oppn's face pretentious, Nari Shakti will crush them'; SP-Congress flag burnt in Lucknow
stories.summary: BJP leader and UP Women's Commission Vice President Aparna Yadav staged a protest late Friday night in front of the Assembly in Lucknow. Along with commission officials and supporters, she burned SP and Congress flags in the middle of the road and raised slogans over the Women's Reservation Bill being dropped in the Lok Sabha. Aparna said- We were going to celebrate in the morning. But, tonight proved to be dark. These people are like Duryodhana and Dushasana. That's why we are burning their flags. We are protesting because the Nari Shakti Adhiniyam Bill was not passed. The darkness will fade, the sun will rise, the lotus will bloom. She said that the opposition has said that this bill is for show, so we respond to them that all their faces are also for show. All opposition parties have been doing the same work. They never want daughters and daughters-in-law from common households to come out and reach the House. They only want to promote their own families. Nari Shakti will never forgive these people. Ugly face of opposition exposed Aparna said that if this bill had been passed, there would have been celebrations in the morning. For this, we were going to different districts of the state for different programs. We were fully confident that the bill would definitely be passed. We thank the Prime Minister again and again for exposing the ugly face of the opposition. She said that the PM made a lot of effort to get the Women's Empowerment Act passed. But, what has happened today is not right. This is a night that brings disgrace. In our country, where the slogan of Bharat Mata Ki Jai is raised. Women's power will not forgive them. They will crush them. Women protested in front of SP office Women also protested around 10 PM outside the Samajwadi Party office. Angered by the non-passage of the women's reservation bill, they raised slogans of "Akhilesh Yadav-Rahul Gandhi Murdabad". A member of the UP Women's Commission said that women's dreams were shattered due to the bill not being passed. Akhilesh is responsible for this. Meanwhile, Akhilesh Yadav wrote on X - BJP should have at least sent 12 women to the protest. Bill needed to be passed with two-thirds majority Actually, the government could not pass the 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill related to the Women's Reservation Bill in the Lok Sabha. It had a provision to increase the 543 seats of Parliament to 850. Voting took place after 21 hours of discussion on the bill in the Lok Sabha. 528 MPs present cast their votes. 298 votes in favor, 230 votes against. A two-thirds majority was needed to pass the bill. Know about Aparna Yadav

stories.title: Assistant Professor re-examination begins today amid tight security:Centres in six UP cities, including Varanasi; life imprisonment for those who cheat or aid cheating
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission is conducting a re-examination for Assistant Professor-51 starting today, April 18. This is being organized under strict surveillance. For this examination, which will be held over 2 days, a total of 48 examination centers have been set up in 6 cities, including Varanasi. The examination is being held in Varanasi, Prayagraj, Agra, Meerut, Lucknow, and Gorakhpur. In Varanasi, 8 examination centers have been established for this purpose. The Commission's Chairman and former DGP Dr. Prashant Kumar, has imposed special strictness regarding this examination. He has stated that if anyone is caught cheating or facilitating cheating in the examination, or attempting any kind of breach, they will be directly sentenced to life imprisonment. Monitoring being done from control room set up in the commission All rooms of the examination centers and all important sections have been equipped with CCTV. Its monitoring has been connected to the district control room and the commission's command and control room. Candidates arriving at the examination center will be allowed entry only after proper frisking. Prohibitory orders have been imposed around all examination centers. The District Magistrate, Senior Police Officers, and their monitoring teams have been instructed to continuously visit the examination centers. The district administration has deployed adequate force at the examination centers. Various security agencies are maintaining a vigilant watch to strictly monitor suspicious and anti-social elements. Use of any kind of electronic devices, mobile phones, etc., by candidates at examination centers will be prohibited. Vimal Kumar Vishwakarma, observer for Varanasi One member each has been designated as observer for each district and sent to the districts. Vimal Kumar Vishwakarma has been appointed as observer for Varanasi. He reached the district and also took into account the arrangements. Similarly, Dr. Krishna Chandra Verma in Gorakhpur, Dr. Harendra Kumar Rai in Prayagraj, Kirti Gautam in Agra, Prof. Radhakrishnan in Meerut, and Yogendra Nath Singh in Lucknow have been designated as observers. Don't pay attention to rumors: Chairman Commission Chairman Prashant Kumar has appealed to all examinees to reach the examination centers on time and strictly comply with the instructions written in the admit card. In accordance with government directives, all necessary arrangements have been ensured at the examination centers in their interest. Candidates should not fall prey to any rumors or misleading information. They should verify information on the Commission's website www.upessc.up.gov.in and 'X' handle @upesscprayagraj. Same examination being conducted again after one year Actually, the Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission had conducted a written examination on April 16 and 17, 2025, under Number-51 for 910 Assistant Professor posts in aided degree colleges. More than 82 thousand candidates had applied for the recruitment. However, immediately after the examination, complaints of large-scale fraud, cheating, and illegal extortion started surfacing. Candidates also continued to stage sit-in protests regarding this. Considering the seriousness of the case, the STF conducted a confidential investigation under the CM's direction. A major revelation was made in the investigation. After this, the STF arrested three members of the gang - Mahboob Ali, Baijnath Pal, and Vinay Pal, who were cheating candidates by preparing fake question papers.
