stories.title: 12 SP leaders seek tickets for their sons and daughters:Several meet Akhilesh Yadav, begin campaigning with children in their respective constituencies
stories.summary: 12 SP leaders are lobbying for Assembly tickets for their sons and daughters in the 2027 elections. Among them is Rakesh Verma, son of senior SP leader Beni Prasad Verma. For the Katehari seat, considered an SP stronghold, MP Lalji Verma is pushing for his daughter’s candidature. Meanwhile, ailing leader Ramgovind now wants his son to contest from the Bansdih seat. Tufani Saroj is also in the race. After establishing his daughter Priya Saroj in politics, he is now seeking a ticket for his son as well. These leaders have met Akhilesh Yadav over the past few months. Many have already begun campaigning with their sons and daughters in their respective areas to strengthen their claim ahead of the party’s survey process. Who are these leaders? Do two or more members of their families already belong to some house or the other? Let's find out in this report... Know about the concerns of 12 leaders regarding their political heirs Fareed wants to secure a seat for his son Fareed Mahfooz Kidwai, MLA from Ramnagar seat in Barabanki, has been a minister in the Akhilesh Yadav government (2012-2017). During this period, he handled the responsibility of several departments, including technical education, forest, and sports. Now, he wants to make his son Faizan Kidwai contest elections to carry forward his political legacy. For this, he has also started campaigning in the name of Faizan in the area. Faizan is also a Bollywood actor. Awadhesh demanding a ticket again for his son Ayodhya MP Awadhesh Prasad is demanding a ticket for his son Ajit Prasad from the Milkipur seat. In the Milkipur by-election held in February 2025, SP candidate Ajit Prasad was defeated by BJP's Chandrabhanu Paswan by 61,710 votes. This defeat was considered significant because in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Awadhesh Prasad had won the Ayodhya (Faizabad) seat by taking a lead from this very area. Despite the defeat in the by-election, Awadhesh Prasad is adamant about handing over his political legacy to Ajit Prasad. He has already become active in the area for the 2027 Assembly elections. Awadhesh Prasad has been an MLA from Milkipur 9 times. Rakesh's lobbying for daughter's ticket Rakesh Verma, son of Beni Prasad Verma, who was a prominent SP leader in Barabanki, has been an MLA from the Kursi seat. He has also been a Minister of State in the Akhilesh government. After taking over his father's legacy, he now wants to bring his daughter, Shreya Verma, into politics. He had made such an attempt in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections as well. Shreya had contested from Gonda and received 4.28 lakh votes. However, she lost by 46 thousand votes. Now, Rakesh Verma wants her to contest the MLA election from the Kursi seat in the 2027 elections as well. Lalji Verma wants to make his doctor daughter an MLA Lalji Verma is the SP MP from Ambedkar Nagar. In the 2022 elections, he won from the Katehari assembly constituency and became an MLA. Akhilesh Yadav gave him a Lok Sabha ticket in 2024. He won the election and became an MP. In the by-election, his wife Shobhavati Verma contested on an SP ticket and won. This time, Lalji Verma wants to see his daughter Chhaya Verma in the assembly. Chhaya Verma is a doctor (ophthalmologist) by profession. 8-time MLA Ram Govind wants to hand over legacy to his son Ram Govind Chaudhary, who has been an MLA 8 times from Bansdih in Ballia, now wants to hand over his political legacy to his son Ranjit. He lost from the Bansdih seat in the 2022 Assembly elections. Ketki Singh had defeated him. Ram Govind Chaudhary was the Leader of Opposition in the Assembly from 2017 to 2022. He has been unwell for a long time, so he is now demanding a ticket for his son. He has also lobbied for this with Akhilesh Yadav. Preparing to launch son into politics after Priya Saroj Tufani Saroj has been an MP from Machhlishahr. Currently, he is an MLA from Kerakat. His daughter Priya Saroj is an MP from Machhlishahr. She is carrying forward his political legacy. Her marriage is fixed with cricketer Rinku Singh. Now, Tufani Saroj is preparing to launch his son Dhananjay into politics as well. Dhananjay is an advocate by profession and practices in court. Claim for ticket for son Rajendra Yadav has been an MLA twice from the Bakhshi Ka Talab (BKT) seat in Lucknow. Now, he is fully standing behind Shivendra to take his legacy forward. In the 2022 assembly elections, Shivendra Yadav was considered almost a confirmed candidate from SP. His name was also in discussion. At the last moment, for strategic reasons, the party cut his ticket and fielded Gomti Yadav. SP had won Gomti Yadav from here in 2012. However, in 2022, he lost to the BJP's Yogesh Shukla. Shivendra has been continuously active in the area. SP has faced defeat in Bakhshi Ka Talab in the last two elections (2017 and 2022). Ambika wants ticket for son Ambika Chaudhary is counted among the senior leaders of SP. Ambika Chaudhary was among the trusted leaders of Mulayam Singh Yadav. He has been a minister of important departments like Revenue and Backward Class Welfare in the SP government. During the family feud between Akhilesh and Shivpal Yadav, Ambika Chaudhary joined BSP in 2017. He also contested elections from the Phephna assembly seat on the BSP ticket, but lost. In August 2021, he rejoined the SP. This foundation was laid through his son, Anand Chaudhary. Anand Chaudhary had won the election for Ballia District Panchayat President with SP's support. Ambika Chaudhary is now preparing to hand over his legacy to Anand Chaudhary. There is talk that he wants a ticket for Anand from a prominent seat in Ballia (possibly Phephna or Ballia Sadar) in the 2027 Assembly elections. Preparing to vacate seat for son Alam Badi surprises everyone by reaching the Assembly on a scooter, even at the age of 90. Continuously winning from the Nizamabad seat of Azamgarh is proof of his grassroots hold. Now, he is preparing to field his son, Mujteba Alam alias Babu, in the electoral arena. In fact, Alam Badi has made the Nizamabad seat an impregnable fortress of SP. Considering his advancing age and health reasons, he wants to hand over the legacy to his son, Mujtaba Alam. Mujtaba Alam is already active in the area. An atmosphere is being created for him at the organisational level. However, Alam Badi has not yet spoken to the high command. Attempt to bring son to the assembly Durga Prasad Yadav has been an MLA from the Azamgarh Sadar seat for 9 consecutive terms. His closeness to Akhilesh Yadav is well known. He helped his son Vijay Yadav reach the position of Azamgarh District Panchayat President. Now, Vijay is fully active in politics. There is talk that Durga Prasad Yadav may leave his traditional 'Azamgarh Sadar' seat for his son Vijay Yadav. With advancing age and the changed political environment, he wants Vijay to secure his seat while he is still around. Sambhal's SP MLA will field his son in elections Sambhal's prominent leader and SP MLA, Nawab Iqbal Mahmood, wants to bring forward his son, Suhail Iqbal Mahmood, for the 2027 elections. Nawab Iqbal has been an MLA 7 times. Nawab Iqbal Mahmood indicated at an event held in October 2025 on Mulayam Singh Yadav's death anniversary that he now wants to take a break from politics and hand over his legacy to his son Suhail. During this, he sought suggestions from workers and spoke about fielding Suhail in the 2027 electoral arena. To which supporters gave a positive response. Meanwhile, Suhail Iqbal has been actively involved in managing his father's election campaigns and resolving regional issues for a long time. Suhail came into discussion recently when his name surfaced in the investigation related to the Sambhal violence that occurred in November 2024. He had to appear before the SIT and record his statement in this matter. However, Nawab Iqbal Mahmood has continued to call it a 'political conspiracy'. Will give his safe seat to his son Amroha's prominent leader and former Cabinet Minister, Mahboob Ali, is now preparing his son Parvez Ali for the Assembly elections. Parvez Ali has been an MLC from the Moradabad-Bijnor constituency from 2016 to 2022. Mahboob Ali has been continuously serving as MLA from the Amroha seat since 2002. He has been a minister of important departments like Secondary Education and Silk Industry in the SP government. After playing a long innings in politics, Mahboob Ali now wants Parvez Ali to reach the assembly by being elected directly from among the people. It is believed that he may either leave his safe seat for 2027 or is lobbying for some favourable seat nearby for Parvez. Those cases where sons are lobbying for themselves Preparing to carry forward political legacy In the politics of Sant Kabir Nagar, the name of the late Bhalchandra Yadav is taken with great respect. Bhalchandra Yadav was a Member of Parliament from Khalilabad (now Sant Kabir Nagar) twice. He had a strong grip on the backward class and farmer politics of the region. Bhalchandra passed away in 2019. His son Subodh Yadav is preparing the political ground by gathering old supporters in 2027. In the 2022 elections, Subodh Yadav contested from the Khalilabad seat on an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) ticket. However, now he is trying to make a comeback in mainstream politics through his 'original home', that is, SP. Attempt to carry forward family politics Ahmad Hameed, heir to Baghpat's historic 'Nawab family', is now trying to carry forward the political legacy of his late father, Kaukab Hameed. Ahmad's father, Kaukab Hameed Khan, was an MLA 5 times and also served as a minister in the state government. His influence was not only in the Muslim community but also among Jats and other communities. Ahmad Hameed has contested assembly elections twice so far. In 2017, he contested on a BSP ticket and came second. In 2022, he contested on an RLD ticket but lost the election by a very narrow margin. Recently, Ahmad Hameed met SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. It is believed that he is strengthening his claim for an SP ticket for 2027. Apart from this, there are many such MLAs or MPs whose fathers have been MPs or MLAs...

stories.title: Mercury rises sharply in UP with temperatures reaching 45°C mark:16 cities cross 40°C; hot winds persist, weather likely to change in 3 days
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is experiencing severe heat in April itself. The mercury has reached close to 45 degrees. Since Friday (April 17) morning, most districts in the state have been experiencing strong sunlight with hot winds resulting in heatwave like conditions. On Thursday (April 16), the temperature in Banda was recorded at 44.4 degrees. Last year, on April 22, the mercury in Prayagraj was recorded at 44.3 degrees. This means that this time, the maximum temperature has exceeded last year's level, 6 days earlier. Temperatures in 16 districts recorded at 40°C The maximum temperature in 16 districts was recorded at 40 degrees or above. Prayagraj, Varanasi, and 50 other cities experienced severe heat. Children going to school were seen covering their faces with cloth and carrying umbrellas. In this regard, Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Singh said, “The temperature in the state will rise by 2-3 degrees for the next three days. After this, a new Western Disturbance will become active. However, there is no possibility of rain due to this, but there will be a change in the direction of the winds. The sky may become cloudy. There might be slight relief from the heat”. See weather pictures- Now know the condition of the cities Why is it getting so hot? According to meteorologists, due to the absence of any active weather system currently, dry westerly winds are directly reaching the plains. Along with this, an anti-cyclone formed over Karnataka and Maharashtra is now shifting towards Central India. This is the reason for the continuous increase in temperature. How will the weather be for 4 days? See yesterday's weather pictures- These dates will be affected by ‘Nautapa’ This year, the king of planets Sun, will enter Rohini Nakshatra on May 25 at 15:37. After this, the Sun will remain in Rohini Nakshatra for 15 days, until June 8 at 13:33. In such a situation, the effect of ‘Nautapa’ will remain for nine days from the beginning of the Sun's entry into Rohini Nakshatra. According to astrologer Punit Varshney, “This effect will start from May 25 and continue till June 2. During this period, the direct rays of the sun start falling on the Earth, due to which there is intense heat during this period”. Know about El-Nino and La-Nina- El Nino: In this, the sea temperature increases by 3-4 degrees. Its effect occurs twice in 10 years. Due to this, areas with high rainfall receive less, and areas with low rainfall receive more rain. La Nina: In this, the sea water cools rapidly. It affects weather worldwide. Clouds cover the sky and there is good rainfall.

stories.title: Lucknow wedding turns tragic after fire:Bride fails to reach in-laws, groom arrives without procession; four stories of loss
stories.summary: We were preparing for the wedding. The nephew's baraat (groom's procession) was about to leave in an hour. Guests had arrived. Preparations were underway to adorn the groom. He was being applied ubtan (a traditional paste). The women of the house were singing songs. Suddenly, screams erupted. Someone shouted that there was a fire in the settlement. Saying this, Rani of Lucknow's voice choked. Tears welled up in her eyes. She had come to attend her nephew Manish's wedding. At the time when 250 huts caught fire in Vikas Nagar, the baraat was supposed to leave from there an hour later, but the fire burned everything to ashes. However, the family members took the baraat. The wedding took place, but due to the lack of a home, the bride's farewell could not happen. To understand the scene after the fire in Vikas Nagar, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached the ground. Here, they learned about the pain of the affected families. Read the report See 3 pictures of helplessness Fire guts wedding preparations, family devastated The groom’s aunt Rani, said the house was full of celebration, with the wedding procession set to leave in an hour when the fire broke out. As cylinders started exploding, everyone ran to save their lives. The groom’s sherwani, clothes, and the bride’s wedding dress and jewellery were destroyed. The wedding home turned into a scene of mourning, with people of all ages crying. Over 100 guests from different places also fled for safety. The family had bought a new saree with great hopes for the wedding, only that one remains. Rani said her sister, who works as a domestic helper, had borrowed ₹1.5 lakh for her son’s wedding and is now shattered. She appealed to the government for help. While the house was burning, Manish’s wedding procession had left, and his marriage with Madhu took place four hours later in Pani village, Indiranagar. Home destroyed before their eyes, Nandini kept sobbing Nandini was sitting 50 meters away from where the fire broke out. She was sobbing with tears in her eyes. We tried to talk to her. Sitting silently, Nandini said that this scene is very terrifying for her. Our childhood was spent here, this is the first time I've seen such a fire.Everything we had burned in this fire, we only managed to save our lives. When the accident happened, only my parents were at home. My sister and I had gone to work. That's where we got the information that our house was on fire, we rushed back and were stunned by the scene here. Fire destroys savings Nandini said the fire ruined their family's TV, fridge, and all their belongings were burnt. The family had saved ₹2.5 lakh through labor work for her wedding and made some jewelry, but both the cash and jewelry were destroyed in the blaze. She said the money was saved through sweeping and mopping work. All important documents were also burnt, including the papers of a car bought last Dhanteras. She appealed to the government for help, saying nothing is left except the clothes they were wearing. Fire leaves family missing An unconscious Shamsunnisha was being supported by a girl as she cried and beat her chest, saying everything they had was destroyed in the fire. She said they had married their daughter nine months ago, but even two hours after the blaze, there was no trace of her son and daughter-in-law. She added the family had been living there for 17 years and had no idea how the fire suddenly broke out. After her husband’s death, she survived by doing sweeping and mopping work, and her son and daughter-in-law were her only support. Now they are missing, and she says nothing is left. 250 homes destroyed A massive fire broke out in Vikas Nagar, Lucknow, on Wednesday evening. After the fire started, the sound of gas cylinders, refrigerators, and AC compressors exploding echoed all around. More than 40 cylinders exploded due to the fire. Over 250 shanties were burnt to ashes. Flames were visible up to 10 kilometers away. After the fire broke out, 20 fire brigade vehicles brought the fire under control after a struggle of about 7 hours. All the belongings of the people were burnt to ashes. Those whose shanties were burnt kept crying and wailing. Late at night, people were sent to temporary night shelters.

stories.title: Fire guts 250 huts in Lucknow’s Vikasnagar:Children search for toys in debris, women break down after devastation
stories.summary: An evening that began like any other in Vikasnagar turned chaotic on April 15 as a fire tore through a cluster of huts in Lucknow, triggering panic and desperate calls for help. Residents said the crackle of flames quickly drowned out the usual sounds of daily life, before a stunned silence settled over the area. Day after, survivors sift through ashes By morning, the extent of the damage became clear. Children searched the charred remains for toys, while adults looked for documents, cash and other essentials. Entire households were reduced to debris, leaving families with little to salvage. Losses both material and personal Among the survivors, grief was visible. A father broke down after finding his child’s burnt schoolbooks. Nearby, a woman wept over belongings she had saved for years. Officials said around 250 huts were destroyed, displacing several families. Tap on the photo above to watch the video of the aftermath.

stories.title: PM Modi calls Akhilesh 'friend' in Parliament:Shah says 'no need to fear'; sharp exchange fuels political buzz
stories.summary: The central government on Thursday introduced amendment bills related to the Women’s Reservation framework during a special session of Parliament, triggering a series of political exchanges inside the House. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while addressing members, referred to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav as his “friend”. In response, Yadav smiled and folded his hands, drawing attention from members across party lines. Akhilesh–Shah exchange draws attention A debate between Yadav and Union Home Minister Amit Shah added intensity to the proceedings, with both leaders raising points over the implications and timing of the proposed amendments. Meanwhile, Union Minister Smriti Irani also became a subject of discussion during the session, despite not being a member of either House of Parliament at present. Political messaging dominates proceedings The session reflected not only legislative developments but also political signalling, with leaders using the platform to underline their respective positions on women’s representation and electoral strategy. Watch the video of the Parliament debate for full details.

stories.title: Car mows down 3 women sitting on divider in Hapur:Victims were waiting for bus, two critically injured
stories.summary: A speeding car ran over people sitting on a road divider in Hapur on Thursday evening, killing three women and injuring two others. The accident took place in the Hafizpur police station area when the car was travelling from Hapur towards Bulandshahr. Police said the driver lost control near Yadav Dhaba in Murshidpur village, after which the vehicle climbed onto the divider. Victims were waiting for transport Several people were sitting on the divider waiting for a bus or auto when the car hit them. Sitara (52), Sharda (52), and Saroj Sharma (60), all residents of Brijnatpur, died on the spot. Ruby (25) and her six-year-old son Lavish were seriously injured and taken to hospital. Driver detained, vehicle seized The car (UP15 CJ 6315) was being driven by Naresh, a resident of Meerut. He was taken into custody. Police removed the damaged vehicle and restored traffic. Bodies of the deceased have been sent for post-mortem. Officials visit spot, probe underway District Magistrate Abhishek Pandey and Superintendent of Police KG Singh inspected the site. ASP Vineet Bhatnagar said the car hit women sitting on the divider after going out of control. He confirmed three deaths and said further legal action is underway. Family account of incident According to Manoj, son of Sharda, the family was waiting by the roadside to travel to Narena village in Dhaulana. Sharda had accompanied her daughter Ruby. The accident occurred while they were waiting for transport.

stories.summary: Social activists, academics, and former civil servants have urged the government to publicly share draft bills on women's reservation and delimitation for wider consultation. While wholeheartedly supporting women's reservation, the group expressed concern over the "opaque and non-consultative manner" of their introduction in the upcoming special parliamentary session.

stories.title: Sheriff sues Sunny Naqvi for $1 million over 'false story' of being detained by ICE; claims she was with ex-boyfriend
Delimitation must be preceded by census: Sonia Gandhi
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi has questioned the Modi government's planned delimitation, arguing it must follow a census and be politically equitable. She emphasized that states pioneering family planning and smaller states should not be disadvantaged. Gandhi also called for an OBC sub-quota for women in reservation, highlighting the need for broader discussions before proceeding with such consequential amendments.

stories.title: Clear stand on free compulsory pre-primary education, SC tells govt
Soon, access to nicotine gums may get tougher
SC wants govt response to PIL seeking hike in MSP for grains
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has sought responses from the Centre and states on a PIL demanding a higher Minimum Support Price (MSP) for farmers to cover production costs and prevent suicides. Petitioners argue that current MSPs are insufficient, citing the M S Swaminathan Commission's recommendations and the impact of free ration schemes on agricultural markets.

stories.title: Anna Kepner murder: 16-year-old stepbrother charged with killing of Florida teenager
Man transporting cattle jumps into Ramban rivulet to escape assault, goes missing; 4 held
J&K: Last tonga in Srinagar rolls again, 70-year-old keeps past alive
stories.summary: Ghulam Rasool Kumar, a 70-year-old tonga driver, has returned to Srinagar's streets after a hiatus, becoming a nostalgic spectacle for tourists and locals alike. Despite facing disruptions due to a terrorist attack, he continues to offer rides, his horse-drawn cart a poignant reminder of the city's past amidst modern traffic.

stories.title: Wangchuk renews push for talks, says Ladakh 'hangs between trust and mistrust'
stories.summary: Environmentalist Sonam Wangchuk urged the Centre to resume dialogue on Ladakh's key issues, expressing concern over a growing trust deficit. He highlighted that over two months have passed since the last talks, allowing divisive elements to exploit the gap. Wangchuk appealed to the Prime Minister and Home Minister to take timely measures for national interest.

stories.title: Florida man arrested after swinging machete at milk crates; charged with possession of deadly weapon
1,000 Roman objects were found in Lake Switzerland, and they are almost perfectly preserved
J&K: Sighting of terror suspects prompts search ops in Kathua
stories.summary: Two armed terror suspects were reportedly spotted in Jammu and Kashmir's Kathua district, prompting extensive search operations by security forces in multiple border areas. The duo, carrying heavy backpacks, was seen moving towards the forests of Ambanall. Despite a joint cordon-and-search operation, no trace of the suspects was found.

stories.title: Asmongold spends $7K on dental surgery during Twitch suspension, says he could “taste the rot”
stories.summary: Asmongold revealed he spent $7,000 on dental surgery after a Twitch suspension in April 2026, stemming from severely rotting teeth. The streamer described tasting the decay while eating, prompting him to finally address the long-ignored health issue during his break. The treatment significantly improved his daily life and enjoyment of food.

stories.title: Tax fraud by 4 Indian-origin accountants in Texas: Their clients received more funds, US govt lost millions of dollars
Florida man arrested for showing deepfake AI video of people breaking into police car to a cop
Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin extracts oxygen from Moon dust in a breakthrough for long-term human life on Moon
stories.summary: Blue Origin has successfully extracted oxygen from Moon-like soil in lab tests, a significant step for sustained lunar presence. This molten regolith electrolysis technique could drastically cut reliance on Earth supplies. The process, which also yields useful metals for construction, addresses a key challenge for future long-term human missions beyond our planet.

stories.title: Vikram's 'hop' unravels surficial 'layers' near lunar south pole region
Government hints ethanol blending in petrol can be increased by a percent
Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam to boost women-led development: Delhi CM
Indian student missing in US since 2019: FBI's social media post on Mayushi Bhagat sparks confusion
Justin Trudeau and Katy Perry called ‘hypocrites’ for drinking from plastic cups at Coachella
MAGA-friendly Bishop Barron says Trump owes pope an apology: 'No president in my lifetime...'
Don Tzu and art of war (only winning, no losing)
stories.summary: Today we bear witness to said winning, in a way that greatest strategic philosophers of yore: Chanakya, Machiavelli, and obviously Sun Tzu could never have conceived.

stories.title: Partey denies new charges: ex-Arsenal star pleads not guilty; trial delayed to 2027
stories.summary: In a Southwark court, former football star Thomas Partey faced a new set of sexual assault charges, which he firmly rejected. Prosecutors are seeking to merge this latest case with existing rape and assault allegations, potentially delaying the trial until 2027.

stories.title: Pacers set the rhythm at Times Internet Half Marathon
'Sending this from Coachella is WILD': Justin Trudeau trolled for his post on Viktor Orbán's defeat in Hungary election
IMD predicts ‘below normal’ monsoon rainfall over the country amid growing risk of El Niño
Woman falsely told police her ex-boyfriend was carrying bombs onto American Airlines flight to get him arrested
Wife reneges promise of consent divorce, SC invokes Article 142 to grant divorce
stories.summary: The Supreme Court dissolved a marriage and quashed a domestic violence case. A woman broke a divorce settlement after receiving substantial payment. She then filed a criminal case against her husband and his family. The court found her claims about undeclared assets unbelievable. It emphasized that parties must adhere to settlement agreements.

stories.title: Nepal PM Balen accepts Modi invite, unveils anti-VIP reform push at home
stories.summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra “Balen” Shah has accepted Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s invitation to visit India, even as he unveiled an ambitious 100-point governance agenda at home aimed at curbing VIP culture, reducing political interference in campuses and bureaucracy, cutting delays in public services, expanding free healthcare for the poor, improving women’s safety in public transport, and easing academic pressure on young children.

stories.title: Police Seek Witness Footage: Surrey Police probe rape near Epsom church; appeal for videos
stories.summary: Surrey Police are on the lookout for key details following a distressing report from a woman in her twenties who experienced a sexual assault near Epsom Methodist Church early today. The victim had left a nearby nightclub and was allegedly pursued before the incident occurred.

stories.title: On this day: 10 minutes that changed India forever - 107 years of Jallianwala Bagh massacre
stories.summary: On April 13, 1919, Jallianwala Bagh became a scene of brutal massacre as British forces opened fire on unarmed civilians. This horrific event, fueled by oppressive colonial policies, ignited India's freedom struggle. The unhealed scar of this tragedy continues to resonate, a stark reminder of the immense cost of independence and the enduring power of collective memory.

stories.title: 'I have not spoken to any women...': Katie Porter on her connection to Swalwell accuser influencer Cheyenne Hunt
Was the Odyssey real? 3,000-year-old sanctuary of legendary Trojan War hero Odysseus discovered in Greece
stories.summary: A significant archaeological find on Ithaca, Greece, suggests centuries of worship for the legendary Odysseus. Researchers unearthed a sanctuary with inscribed artifacts, ritual offerings, and ceramics dating back to the Mycenaean era. This discovery strengthens the link between the epic hero and tangible history, fueling renewed interest in his enduring tale, especially with a major film adaptation planned.

stories.title: Indian woman killed in road crash in US, family says she could not be saved even after 3 surgeries
Evening news wrap: US warships move to blockade Hormuz; Noida sees violent protests over wage demands & more
The 10K run nobody knew about: The untold story behind DIG BSF Ajeet Kumar Singh's run at Times Internet Half Marathon
Elon Musk reveals he ‘felt like he was dying’ after a COVID vaccine shot; says the virus was just a bad cold
stories.summary: Tech mogul Elon Musk sparked global vaccine debate by sharing his severe reaction to a COVID-19 vaccine dose, contrasting it with a mild virus infection. His remarks followed testimony by a former Pfizer toxicologist raising concerns about vaccine safety. Health authorities, however, continue to affirm the vaccines' safety and efficacy for the general population.

stories.title: Shots fired near ULFA(I) chief Paresh Baruah's house in Assam
Umar Khalid seeks review of SC verdict denying him bail, prays for open-court hearing
Panchayat polls delayed by Rajasthan govt over 'fear of defeat': Pilot
‘Fed biryani to Pakistani terrorists’: Amit Shah attacks Mamata Banerjee at Bengal rally
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday attacked Mamata Banerjee and Congress at a rally in West Bengal, accusing them of feeding “biryani” to Pakistani terrorists instead of acting against them. He said the BJP would crack down on corruption, illegal immigration and violence if voted to power, and claimed people in the state had decided to remove the TMC government.

stories.title: ‘Closure deeply damaging’: Keir Starmer announces UK-France summit on restoring navigation in Strait of Hormuz
How saudi arabia is using wastewater to build a green corridor in the desert
Clavicular loses cool mid-interview over Andrew Tate link, internet brands him “insecure”
stories.summary: Kick streamer Clavicular walked out of a 60 Minutes Australia interview after being questioned about his association with Andrew Tate. Visibly frustrated, he accused the interviewer of making things “political” before abruptly ending the conversation. The incident quickly went viral, with fans calling him “insecure.” This marks his second recent walkout, following a similar clash with Andrew Callaghan, raising concerns about how he handles criticism.

stories.title: Who to be next Bihar CM? BJP likely to declare face for top post on Tuesday
stories.summary: The leadership change will mark a milestone for the BJP, which is set to get its first chief minister in Bihar, the only Hindi heartland state where the top post has so far eluded the party. Even so, party leaders have remained cautious in their public remarks. Dilip Jaiswal, a minister and former Bihar BJP president, said, "It is an emotional moment for us. We hope that Nitish Kumar will continue to offer his guidance to the new government."

stories.title: 'Almost treating me as guilty': Arvind Kejriwal lists 10 reasons for seeking recusal of Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma in excise policy case
Army launches Sikkim's first border village community radio station
'Ready to play full part': France, UK plan joint mission to protect Hormuz shipping route
stories.summary: France and the UK will jointly lead a multinational initiative to restore free and secure navigation in the Strait of Hormuz amid rising US-Iran tensions. This strictly defensive mission aims to safeguard maritime traffic through the strategic waterway, separate from ongoing hostilities, and will be deployed when conditions permit.

stories.title: Chilling space facts that will stay in your mind long after reading
stories.summary: Although many people consider the cosmos to be a peaceful, stunning environment, the truth behind its appearance offers an incomprehensible universe with extreme events. For instance, there are the undead stars (or zombie stars) that consume energy from their star neighbours, and there are enormous galaxies that may contain thousands of Milky Ways. Therefore, the universe operates on a scale of existential chaos that defies human intuition. While the night sky looks peaceful, it is a graveyard of 'Zombie Stars' and a playground for 'Galactic Titans' that challenge the very laws of physics and are impossible to comprehend by human beings.The most terrible thing is that the more we uncover things about deep space, the more we will find hypergiants that dwarf the Sun and end up drifting in the dark, infinite void of outer space. The facts listed below provide a frightening reality about how vast and incredibly terrifying the universe truly is.

stories.title: 'People will respond to bombs with ballots': Amit Shah in Bengal, warns 'jail' for TMC 'goons'
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah intensified his attack on the TMC in West Bengal, urging voters to respond to violence with ballots and promising to bring the BJP to power. He alleged corruption and a "mafia raj," vowing strict action against "syndicate and cut-money promoters" and illegal immigrants, while also highlighting welfare promises.

stories.title: 'Himanta most corrupt in country': Rahul Gandhi backs Pawan Khera as passport row escalates
stories.summary: Khera struck Himanta's nerve after he alleged, in a press conference, the Assam CM's wife held multiple foreign passports, prompting a sharp rebuttal and legal threat from the BJP leader. “We have documents showing that Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma’s wife Riniki Bhuyan Sharma, holds three passports. The first is a UAE Golden Card, the second an Antigua and Barbuda passport, and the third an Egyptian passport. Two of these belong to Islamic countries, yet they continue to claim religious adherence publicly,” Khera alleged.

stories.title: Turning car battery acid into clean energy: A surprising breakthrough in plastic recycling
Big boost for India as GE signs contract with IAF to set up engine repair facility in country for Tejas fleet
Assam government moves Supreme Court against transit bail granted to Pawan Khera
stories.summary: The Assam government has approached the Supreme Court challenging a Telangana High Court order granting transit anticipatory bail to Congress leader Pawan Khera. Khera had sought protection from arrest in a case stemming from his allegations against Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma's wife. The Supreme Court's intervention will now shape the legal proceedings.

stories.title: Supreme Court flags ‘margin of error’ in Bengal SIR, refuses to intervene
stories.summary: The Supreme Court expressed serious concerns regarding West Bengal's electoral roll revision, emphasizing the need for a strong appeals system to correct wrongful deletions. Judicial officers are overwhelmed, leading to potential errors. Despite these worries, the court directed voters to appellate tribunals for resolution, highlighting the importance of voter inclusion.

stories.title: AIADMK-BJP alliance will make Tamil Nadu ‘retrogressive’, warns Udhayanidhi Stalin
Days after major security breach, Delhi Assembly receives bomb threat
stories.summary: The Delhi Legislative Assembly experienced a bomb threat via email, triggering a multi-agency response including police, bomb disposal units, and dog squads. A thorough search yielded no suspicious findings, and the situation is under control. This incident follows a recent security breach where an SUV rammed the assembly gate, leading to the detention of three suspects.

stories.title: 98 km in 85 minutes: Green corridor rush saves young man with failing heart
Hidden for centuries: Archaeologists uncover the 350-hectare ‘missing city’ of Magas beneath Chechen soil
‘Needs to be examined’: Supreme Court seeks Centre, ECI response on biometric voting plea
stories.summary: The Supreme Court is reviewing a proposal to implement fingerprint and iris scans at polling stations to combat voter fraud and impersonation. Notices have been issued to the central government, Election Commission, and states. While acknowledging the need to examine this for future elections, the court clarified it won't be introduced for current state polls.

stories.title: Kuwait Citizenship Law Amendments 2026: Decree expands revocation powers; naturalisation rules tighten
stories.summary: Kuwait has enacted significant changes to its citizenship law, empowering the government to grant and revoke nationality with greater authority. The new decree tightens eligibility criteria, particularly for naturalisation and marriage-based applications, while reinforcing strict rules against dual nationality. These reforms aim to safeguard national identity and address past irregularities, ensuring citizenship is granted strictly by law.

stories.title: 'Mood favouring the BJP': PM Modi after interacting with party workers in West Bengal, takes jab at TMC
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed confidence in the BJP's growing support in West Bengal, citing feedback from party workers in Siliguri. He highlighted public connection with the BJP's development agenda and criticized the TMC government for corruption, appeasement, and neglecting North Bengal.

stories.title: ‘On brink of making history’: PM Modi says women’s reservation bill will strengthen democracy
Hajj 2026: Saudi Arabia halts Makkah entry, suspends Umrah visas and sets strict rules for pilgrims
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has implemented strict entry restrictions into Makkah ahead of Hajj 2026, suspending Umrah visas to manage crowds and ensure safety. Only those with valid Hajj permits or official work/residency documents will be allowed entry from April 13. This move aims to prevent overcrowding and unauthorized participation during the pilgrimage.

stories.title: ‘Deeply flawed’: Sonia Gandhi slams women’s quota bill, calls it ‘assault on Constitution’
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi asserts the Centre's focus on delimitation, not women's reservation, is the "real issue" behind the special Parliament session, deeming it "extremely dangerous" and an "assault" on the Constitution. She argues population control performers shouldn't be disadvantaged and criticizes the government's rushed approach for political gain, calling it "hollow" and "anti-democratic."

stories.title: 'Crucial to ensure transparency': Kerala assembly opposition leader Satheesan urges EC to release poll data
stories.summary: Kerala's opposition chief VD Satheesan passionately called upon the Election Commission to promptly disclose the official polling figures for the elections held on April 9. He raised concerns over the delay in releasing detailed constituency data and postal ballot outcomes, stressing the need for accountability and public confidence.

stories.title: 'Trust deficit in Ladakh': Sonam Wangchuk says no date for next round of talks with government announced
stories.summary: Ladakh activist Sonam Wangchuk warns of deepening divisions due to stalled talks with the Centre, over two months since the last dialogue. He highlights growing disillusionment and the risk of social discord, urging timely action from the Prime Minister and Home Minister. Wangchuk's release had raised hopes for constructive dialogue on demands for statehood and Sixth Schedule status.

stories.title: Hormuz row: Iran takes '100% PhD' dig to mock Trump for 'blockading their blockade'
BJP MP Manoj Tiwari to hold multiple campaign events in West Bengal today
stories.summary: BJP MP Manoj Tiwari will attend five election campaign programs in West Bengal today ahead of the Assembly elections 2026.

stories.title: 'Enemy will become trapped in a deadly vortex': Iran claims 'full control' of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps has asserted full control over the Strait of Hormuz, warning of severe consequences for any military vessels approaching. While civilian traffic is permitted under unspecified regulations, the move follows a US naval blockade order, escalating regional tensions. A recent ceasefire's durability is uncertain after stalled talks.

stories.title: Pakistan: BLA carries out first-ever attack on Coast Guard boat near Iran border, 3 killed
stories.summary: Three Pakistan Coast Guard personnel were killed in a brazen attack by Baloch fighters on a patrol boat near the Iran border. The Balochistan Liberation Army claimed responsibility, calling it a "new phase" of operations. This incident escalates concerns over rising militant activity in the restive Balochistan region, with security forces now on high alert along the coast.

stories.title: 'Weak on crime': Donald Trump slams Pope Leo over 'enough of war' remark on Iran
stories.summary: President Trump sharply criticized Pope Leo XIV, labeling him "weak on crime" and "terrible for foreign policy." Trump accused the pontiff of being soft on Iran's nuclear ambitions and opposing US military actions, while the Pope had called for peace and dialogue amid global conflicts.

stories.title: The Chinese treasure fleet (1525): One of history’s greatest strategic mistakes
Asha Bhosle passes away: Haan, yahi kahenge hum sada, ki dil abhi nahin bhara
Shivraj Singh Chouhan named observer, BJP starts process to form Bihar govt
stories.summary: As Nitish Kumar prepares to resign as Bihar CM on April 14, the BJP has appointed Shivraj Singh Chouhan as its central observer for electing the new leader of its Bihar legislature party. Samrat Choudhary is reportedly the frontrunner for the chief minister's post, with the oath-taking ceremony expected on April 15.

stories.title: "Sorry not sorry": Internet meltdown intensifies as Sykkuno fake apology post spreads during ongoing controversy
stories.summary: Sykkuno went viral after a fake “sorry not sorry” Instagram screenshot spread online, leading many to believe he had responded to serious allegations. The post was later proven fabricated, but the damage was done as fans reacted strongly. With no official statement from him, speculation continues to grow, highlighting how quickly misinformation spreads when audiences are searching for answers during ongoing controversy.

stories.title: Asha Bhosle passes away: 'With Umrao Jaan, she gave Lucknow a permanence'
stories.summary: Asha Bhosle's voice transcended mere singing, embodying a profound presence that immortalized moments. For 'Umrao Jaan,' she didn't just perform; she underwent a reckoning, channeling the essence of a bygone era of restraint and unspoken longing.

stories.title: Before women's quota bill session, PM Modi steps up direct outreach
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is engaging with prominent women achievers to garner support for the women's quota bill, slated for parliamentary discussion on April 16. The legislation, aiming for implementation from the 2029 elections, reserves one-third of seats for women in Lok Sabha and assemblies. This direct outreach seeks to build public backing amidst opposition concerns regarding the delimitation process.

stories.title: US blocks 'all maritime traffic' to Iran ports after Islamabad talks fail, allows Hormuz passage
stories.summary: The US military will blockade all Iranian Gulf ports starting Monday at 1400 GMT, while allowing non-Iranian bound vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz. This action follows failed talks with Tehran over its nuclear ambitions, with President Trump accusing Iran of backtracking on assurances and engaging in "WORLD EXTORTION."

stories.title: Cabaret to global pop, Asha lived 'crossover' before it was buzzword
stories.summary: Asha Bhosle transcended eras, absorbing global music trends and blending them with Indian classical training. She fearlessly explored genres like jazz, rock, and pop, collaborating with international artists and becoming a cultural icon. Her innovative spirit led to groundbreaking projects, earning her a Grammy nomination and cementing her legacy as a truly versatile vocalist.

stories.title: West Bengal polls: Chandra Bose joins TMC, attacks BJP
stories.summary: Subhas Chandra Bose's grandnephew, Chandra Bose, has joined the TMC after quitting the BJP, criticizing the latter's "blatantly communal and anti-Constitution" policies. He accused the BJP of using the religion card for electoral gains, a tactic he likened to British colonial rule. Bose declared it's time to drive out the BJP, just as India did the British.

stories.title: 4 days after Bengal roll freeze, tribunals to start hearings today
stories.summary: Kolkata's 19 appellate tribunals will commence hearing elector inclusion/exclusion appeals on Monday, following the freezing of the electoral roll for Bengal's second-phase assembly polls. These tribunals, established after a Supreme Court order, will address grievances for over 27 lakh names excluded from supplementary lists.

stories.title: Hate crimes targeting Sikh Americans in US rose 3,700% in a decade: FBI report
'1,000 crore BJP deal' video real, admits Kabir; TMC questions PM Modi
stories.summary: Suspended Trinamool MLA Humayun Kabir admitted a controversial video showing him seeking Rs 1,000 crore from BJP and making remarks about Muslims is authentic, though selectively edited. He claims the full 51-minute recording will prove his innocence.

stories.title: West Bengal polls: NIA detains Congress nominee, 3 others over Malda unrest
stories.summary: The NIA has detained Congress candidate Sayem Choudhury and gram panchayat member Golam Rabbani for questioning. The detention is linked to the April 1 violence in Mothabari. Seven judicial officers were confined for eight hours at the Kaliachak-II block office. Choudhury and Rabbani were reportedly present at the scene. The NIA is investigating the incident after a Supreme Court order.

stories.title: Who is Péter Magyar? Lawyer set to become Hungarian prime minister
Many of you will be arrested: West Bengal CM Mamata warns TMC workers
stories.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee warned Trinamool workers of impending arrests by the Election Commission ahead of assembly polls, urging them to remain vigilant. She also vowed to resist the BJP's alleged plans for delimitation and NRC implementation, which she claims aim to divide Bengal and create detention camps.

stories.title: Astronomers detect mega-laser beam signal from 8 billion light-years away
US cop caught swiping on dating app during high-speed chase with armed suspect
China's 'fictitious names' mischievous, says India
stories.summary: India has strongly rejected China's latest attempt to rename 23 places in Arunachal Pradesh, calling it a "mischievous attempt" to assign fictitious names. The Ministry of External Affairs stated that such actions detract from efforts to stabilize India-China ties and reinforce China's baseless claims over the Indian state.

stories.title: With 10.9% net voter deletions, Bengal 5th among 12 states, UTs
stories.summary: West Bengal, despite facing significant opposition to voter list revisions, ranked fifth in net deletions and third in absolute numbers of absent, shifted, and dead electors removed. The state was second only to Uttar Pradesh in dropping deceased voters. While additions were lowest among major states, West Bengal led in deletions through adjudication.

stories.title: This Egyptian discovery could rewrite humans origin history; scientists say we have been looking in the wrong place
Amarnath yatra from July 3 to August 28, registration begins on April 15
stories.summary: The annual Amarnath Yatra will commence on July 3 and conclude on August 28, spanning 57 days. Pilgrims aged 13 to 70 can register from April 15, with enhanced accident insurance of Rs 10 lakh. Registrations will be available at 554 bank branches nationwide.

stories.title: J&K: 3 Kashmir varsities end MOUs with US NGO after ‘security concerns’
stories.summary: Three universities in Kashmir have terminated academic agreements with the US-based Kashmir Care Foundation (KCF). The University of Kashmir, IUST, and SKUAST-K cited internal reviews and "adverse reports" as reasons for cancellation. Officials indicated growing caution over foreign collaborations, particularly in sensitive fields, though no money was exchanged.

stories.title: US will ‘probably’ need to use special forces to get Iran’s uranium, says Nikki Haley
First batch of BrahMos made in Lucknow delivered to Army; national security is collective duty of every citizen, not just forces: Rajnath
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh announced India's strides towards defence self-reliance, with BrahMos missile manufacturing commencing in Lucknow and the first batch delivered to the Army. He highlighted record domestic defence production of Rs 1.5 lakh crore and exports reaching Rs 38,424 crore for FY 2025-26. Singh emphasized national security as a collective citizen duty, urging active participation beyond defence forces.

stories.title: ‘Don’t care if Brandon’s wife is Indian’: Internet reacts to US congressman calling out Indians at 7-Eleven
Mazagon Dock acquires controlling stake in Colombo dockyard for $26.8 m, move will help counter China's control of Lanka port
stories.summary: India's Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Ltd (MDL) has acquired a 51% stake in Sri Lanka's Colombo Dockyard PLC for approximately Rs 249.5 crore. This strategic move aims to counter China's maritime influence in the region and strengthens India-Sri Lanka maritime cooperation. The acquisition is expected to boost CDPLC's revenue and profits.

stories.title: Stalin attacks Centre over ‘women’s quota’ pitch; ramps up poll promises in Tamil Nadu
Agnimitra Paul vs Tapas Banerjee: Asansol turns key battleground ahead of Bengal assembly polls
After 60-year wait, Ghazipur villagers inaugurate crowdfunded bridge over Magai River
Tamil Nadu polls: Vijay rejects ‘four-cornered’ contest, says fight is between TVK and DMK
'We are not slaves': EPS hits back at Udhayanidhi Stalin, says DMK 'can't accept AIADMK’s strength'
How are China and Iran cornering US without firing a shot amid tensions in Gulf
​India has played a balanced diplomatic role amid West Asia crisis: Rajnath Singh
Ex-girlfriend of Trump ally speaks out after ICE deported her: 'It was not enough for him...'
West Bengal polls: Mamata Banerjee alleges BJP 'threatening' TMC candidates to manage majority
stories.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of threatening TMC candidates and ministers to secure support if they fall short of a majority. She also alleged a BJP plan to trifurcate West Bengal by merging parts with Bihar or Odisha, causing hardship for Bengali residents.

stories.title: TMC supports 'tukde-tukde gang' to cut Siliguri Corridor: PM Modi in Bengal rally
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi alleged a 'tukde-tukde gang' threatened to sever the Siliguri Corridor, accusing the TMC of supporting them. He criticized the TMC's appeasement politics, claiming it caused suffering and stalled development, including vital infrastructure projects. Modi promised a special package for North Bengal and urged voters to support the BJP for security and jobs.

stories.title: Karnataka Congress leaders seek cabinet reshuffle; first-time MLAs push for representation
stories.summary: Senior and first-time Karnataka Congress MLAs are in New Delhi pushing for a cabinet reshuffle. They aim to secure ministerial berths for experienced leaders and new legislators. The delegation plans to meet party high command to press their demands. This move comes amid ongoing discussions about leadership changes within the state government.

stories.title: Bengal polls: Netaji’s grandnephew Chandra Bose joins TMC, targets BJP’s ‘divisive politics’
Swami Vivekananda's first life-sized statue unveiled in United States
Andhra techie dies in California waterfall accident during trip with friends
stories.summary: A tech professional from Andhra Pradesh, Singireddy Sai Sriharikrishna, tragically died in an accident at a California waterfall while on a trip with friends. His family, residing in Vizianagaram district, is awaiting the early repatriation of his body. The incident has prompted a request from a TDP MLA to the Andhra Pradesh NRI Empowerment Minister.

stories.title: From welfare to dependency? How Tamil Nadu fell into the freebie trap
‘Sikkim Sundari’: Indian Army launches first border village radio station
stories.summary: The Indian Army's Trishakti Corps has launched Sikkim's first border village community radio station, "Sikkim Sundari," to enhance communication and information access in remote high-altitude areas. The station will broadcast local news, weather, government schemes, and promote culture, while also fostering youth development.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Legendary singer Asha Bhosle passes away; US-Iran talks in Pakistan collapse & more
'Broke my glasses': Anti-India US reporter says she was assaulted at Minneapolis ICE protest
'Baseless narratives cannot alter reality': India rejects China's renaming of places in Arunachal Pradesh
stories.summary: India has strongly refuted China's latest attempt to rename places in Arunachal Pradesh. New Delhi described the move as a mischievous effort to assert false claims. Such actions by China cannot alter the reality that Arunachal Pradesh is an integral part of India. These attempts undermine efforts to stabilize bilateral ties between the two nations.

stories.title: China sets up new county near PoK, Afghan border to curb Uyghur infiltration
'To divide West Bengal': Mamata claims Centre trying to 'trifurcate' state through delimitation
stories.summary: West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee accused the Centre of a plot to trifurcate the state through delimitation, potentially merging parts with Bihar and Odisha. She also alleged a Rs 1,000-crore BJP deal to unseat her government and criticized central forces' conduct during searches. Banerjee further claimed the BJP plans to bribe voters and manipulate polls, urging vigilance.

stories.title: $1bn, a bride or a breakup: Uganda general’s bizarre ultimatum to Turkey
stories.summary: Uganda's army chief, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has ignited a diplomatic firestorm by demanding $1 billion and Turkey's most beautiful woman as a wife, threatening to sever ties if his demands aren't met within 30 days. He also accused Ankara of profiting from Somalia while Uganda shoulders the security burden. This follows similar controversial remarks made by the general in the past.

stories.title: Bihar: Power play brews between JD(U) and BJP for CM post as Nitish packs bags at 1 Anne Marg
stories.summary: Bihar's political landscape is heating up as Chief Minister Nitish Kumar is set to resign for a Rajya Sabha seat, with the BJP expected to nominate the new CM. JD(U) workers are advocating for Nitish's son, Nishant, to take over, while the RJD alleges a conspiracy driven by BJP pressure.

stories.title: EAM Jaishankar thanks UAE president for protecting Indian diaspora amid West Asia conflict
‘Misleading the country’: Jairam Ramesh slams Modi government over caste census delay
stories.summary: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh accused the Modi government of delaying a caste census, citing contradictory statements and policy shifts. He highlighted the government's past refusals, Prime Minister Modi's criticism of caste census demands, and a recent announcement of its inclusion.

stories.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Thousands of violations reported as brief Easter truce breaks down
Asha Bhosle passes away. Send in your tribute
'One of the most iconic and versatile voices’: PM Modi condoles death of Asha Bhosle
stories.summary: Legendary singer Asha Bhosle passed away at 92 in Mumbai due to multiple organ failure. Her son confirmed her demise, with her residence open for tributes and last rites scheduled for Monday with state honors. Bhosle, a celebrated icon, had a career spanning decades, beginning in 1943.

stories.title: 'We need young jansevak': JD(U) workers pitch Nishant Kumar as ‘future CM’ in Bihar after Nitish’s exit
stories.summary: Posters in Patna advocating for Nishant Kumar as Bihar's future Chief Minister have ignited political discussions following Nitish Kumar's move to the Rajya Sabha. While speculation mounts about Nishant's potential role, JD(U) leaders assert Nitish Kumar remains the guiding force. This transition signals a significant shift in Bihar's political dynamics.

stories.title: 57-day Amarnath pilgrimage from July 3; registrations from April 15
Saudi Arabia launches 5 rail routes to cut cargo time and costs, linking Gulf ports faster
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has launched five new rail logistics routes to accelerate cargo movement and reduce transport costs, connecting Gulf ports with key economic hubs. This initiative aims to enhance supply chain efficiency, ease highway congestion, and position the Kingdom as a vital link in global trade under Vision 2030.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu assembly polls: Udhayanidhi Stalin launches campaign in Mannargudi
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu leaders are actively campaigning for the upcoming Assembly elections. Udhayanidhi Stalin launched his campaign in Mannargudi, criticizing rivals and emphasizing regional identity. Chief Minister M K Stalin campaigned in Paramakudi, alleging the BJP is using the AIADMK as a mask. Welfare promises for women, housing, and education were reiterated. The elections are scheduled for April 23.

stories.title: China to resume flights, ease trade curbs with Taiwan amid outreach push
stories.summary: China is set to resume direct flights to more Taiwanese cities. Imports of Taiwanese aquaculture products will also restart. These moves follow talks between Chinese and Taiwanese leaders. Beijing aims to establish a communication mechanism with Taiwan's Kuomintang party. Trade restrictions are being eased. Infrastructure proposals are also being advanced.

stories.title: BJP issues whip, orders full attendance of MPs for April 16–18 special Parliament session
stories.summary: BJP has issued a strict three-line whip for a mandatory three-day Parliament session starting April 16, requiring all MPs and Union ministers to attend. The special session is expected to focus on the Women's Reservation Amendment Bill, with the government proposing to use 2011 census data for implementation timelines.

stories.title: Qatar resumes full maritime traffic, all vessels allowed from Sunday
stories.summary: Qatar has fully reopened its maritime traffic for all vessels, restoring normal sea operations after precautionary restrictions. The Ministry of Transport confirmed the decision, citing improved regional stability. This move allows commercial and private vessels to resume operations within designated hours, with a strong emphasis on safety compliance and a warning against price gouging in marine services.

stories.title: Swami Vivekananda Monument installed in downtown Seattle
stories.summary: Seattle has made history by becoming the first U.S. city government to host a life-size statue of Swami Vivekananda. Unveiled at Westlake Square, the bronze monument, a gift from India, signifies Seattle's inclusive spirit and strengthens cultural ties. Dignitaries and community leaders attended the ceremony, celebrating this unique Indo-American cultural exchange.

stories.title: UAE: BAPS Hindu Mandir to reopen from April 14 in Abu Dhabi after temporary closure
Assam earthquake: Magnitude 4.3 tremor hits Cachar district
stories.summary: A magnitude 4.3 earthquake jolted Assam on Sunday morning at 09:21:58 IST. The tremor, originating at a depth of 5 km in Cachar district, had its epicentre at latitude 24.659°N and longitude 92.763°E. No immediate damage or casualties have been reported.

stories.title: US-Iran talks pause without breakthrough: 5 reasons why negotiations failed in Pakistan
stories.summary: US-Iran nuclear talks in Islamabad concluded without a deal after 21 hours, with deep divisions over nuclear commitments, sanctions relief, and regional control preventing a breakthrough. Both sides indicated future discussions, but significant disagreements over enrichment, frozen assets, and maritime security remain.

stories.title: 'To preserve security of people': Lebanon PM postpones US visit amid Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam has postponed his US and UN visit due to "current internal circumstances" and security concerns. This comes amid rising tensions, with Iran warning Beirut against sidelining Hezbollah in talks with Israel. Israeli strikes continue, complicating regional stability efforts despite a ceasefire push.

stories.title: ‘Without details, no meaningful talks’: Kharge pens letter to PM Modi on delimitation
'Provided great assistance to get us out': Indian fishermen stranded in Iran return home
stories.summary: Indian fishermen, stranded in Iran due to escalating Middle East conflict, expressed profound gratitude for their safe return facilitated by coordinated diplomatic efforts. Union Minister Piyush Goyal received the first batch of 345 fishermen at Chennai Airport, highlighting Prime Minister Modi's directive for their evacuation from Iran via Armenia.

stories.title: Bengal assembly elections: Over 3.6 crore voters eligible for first phase polls on April 23, says EC
stories.summary: Over 3.6 crore electors across 16 districts are set to vote in the first phase of the West Bengal assembly elections on April 23. The electoral rolls include 1.84 crore men, 1.75 crore women, and 465 third gender voters. Murshidabad leads with the highest voter count, while Kalimpong has the lowest.

stories.title: Knife attack suspect shot dead by police after injuring 3 in New York
stories.summary: A knife-wielding man, identified as Anthony Griffen, fatally shot by NYPD officers at Grand Central subway station after injuring three people. Griffen, who claimed to be "Lucifer," advanced on officers with a large knife. Authorities confirmed no link to terrorism, and the victims are in stable condition.

stories.title: Iran hits out at US after Islamabad talks fail, cites ‘breach of promises’
stories.summary: High-stakes talks between Iran and the US in Islamabad concluded without an agreement, with Tehran accusing Washington of "breaches of promise" and "excessive demands." Key issues like the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear program remained unresolved. Despite the setback, Iran indicated potential for future negotiations, thanking Pakistan for its mediation efforts.

stories.title: What led to Iran-US ceasefire talks collapse after 21-hour marathon in Islamabad
stories.summary: High-stakes US-Iran talks in Islamabad concluded without a ceasefire or broader diplomatic framework after 21 hours. Key differences, particularly Iran's nuclear program, remain unresolved. Despite the setback, both nations signaled a willingness to continue discussions, with Iran urging the US to drop 'excessive demands' and recognize its rights.

stories.title: Haiti stampede: 30 killed at historic Citadelle Laferrière
stories.summary: A deadly stampede at Haiti's Citadelle Laferrière on Saturday claimed at least 30 lives as crowds gathered for an annual celebration. Overcrowding and rainfall contributed to the tragedy at the historic fortress, with many young people among the victims. Officials are responding to the scene, and the death toll may increase.

stories.title: Pro-Palestine rally: Over 500 arrested in London for protesting
stories.summary: London police arrested over 500 individuals during a pro-Palestinian demonstration. The arrests were made for showing support for Palestine Action, a group proscribed in the UK. This action follows a High Court ruling that questioned the ban's legality. Organizers criticized the police action, citing the court's decision. The ban on Palestine Action has led to numerous arrests since its inception.

stories.title: Union minister Piyush Goyal welcomes second batch of evacuated Indian fishermen at Chennai Airport
stories.summary: Speaking to reporters at the airport on Saturday, Goyal said the evacuation was carried out following directions from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with coordinated efforts by the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and Indian missions abroad to relocate the stranded fishermen from Iran to Armenia before bringing them back to India.

stories.title: Trump's peace board faces a cash crunch
stories.summary: Donald Trump's Board of Peace has secured only a fraction of the $17 billion pledged for Gaza's reconstruction and governance. Despite billions pledged by Gulf Arab states, only three countries have contributed funds, totaling under $1 billion. The ongoing war with Iran has further complicated these funding difficulties.

stories.title: Indians hunger for untested Chinese weight-loss peptides
stories.summary: Influencers and online communities are driving a surge in unapproved weight-loss peptides imported from China. This trend is fueled by the high cost of doctor-prescribed medications and the desire to overcome weight-loss plateaus, as the body can adapt to even potent GLP-1 drugs, leading to weight regain.

stories.title: Pak military contingent lands in Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Pakistan has dispatched a significant military contingent, including approximately 13,000 soldiers and 10-18 jets, to Saudi Arabia. This deployment, part of a strategic defence pact, aims to bolster joint military coordination and operational readiness. The move underscores the mutual defence agreement where an attack on one nation is considered an attack on the other, enhancing regional security.

stories.title: Musk accused of 'ambush' ahead of $100bn OpenAI trial
Sykkuno scandal deepens as multiple women come forward with shocking allegations
stories.summary: Allegations against Sykkuno have triggered a major online backlash, with multiple women sharing personal experiences that paint a troubling picture. From past relationships to uncomfortable encounters, several voices claim patterns of dishonesty and manipulation. While supporters remain divided, the streamer has not yet publicly responded. As the story gains traction, the controversy continues to grow, raising questions about accountability, influence, and trust within the streaming community.

stories.title: UK pauses Chagos handover deal after Trump criticism
stories.summary: Britain has shelved plans to return the Chagos Islands to Mauritius following strong criticism from US President Trump. The deal, which included leasing Diego Garcia for a century, will not proceed without US support. A former top official indicated the UK government was forced to abandon the plan due to Trump's opposition.

stories.title: Under Trump's Nasa, moon rocket from Boeing faces uncertain future
stories.summary: NASA's Artemis II mission successfully sent astronauts around the moon using Boeing's rocket. However, the Trump administration is now seeking cheaper alternatives from competitors like SpaceX for future lunar endeavors. This move puts pressure on NASA's leadership to deliver on ambitious moon landing goals by 2028, despite the established but costly nature of current programs.

stories.title: 'It's OK to howl at Moon': Why Nasa streamed Artemis flight on Twitch
stories.summary: NASA flight director Zebulon Scoville championed public engagement for the Artemis Moon missions, implementing an optical communications system for higher-resolution streaming. The Artemis II crewed flight saw extensive live programming across NASA platforms and social media, attracting millions of viewers. Astronauts' vivid descriptions and genuine emotion captivated audiences, marking a shift towards a more engaging public narrative for space exploration.

stories.title: US-Iran direct talks begin in Pakistan amid disputes, distrust
stories.summary: Direct US-Iran talks commenced in Pakistan Saturday, following a fragile ceasefire. US Vice President JD Vance met with Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf to discuss advancing the peace, amidst ongoing Israeli attacks. Regional powers, including China, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and Qatar, are present to facilitate discussions on critical issues like compensation for war damages.

stories.title: Net deletions due to SIR 5.2cr (10%) in 12 states/UTs; 2 crore included in Phase 2
stories.summary: Over 2 crore new voters joined electoral rolls across 12 states and UTs during intensive revision, while nearly 5.2 crore names were deleted. This purification process, aimed at ensuring accurate voter lists and preventing bogus voting, resulted in 45.8 crore electors remaining. Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Uttar Pradesh saw the highest purification percentages.

stories.title: PM Modi writes to parties, seeks support on women's quota bills
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi has urged all party floor leaders to support the unanimous passage of women's reservation bills next week, aiming for implementation by the 2029 elections. The government seeks to enact the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, which will reserve one-third of Lok Sabha and assembly seats for women.

stories.title: Big share of funds for kids' jabs not spent: RTI data
stories.summary: Despite significant annual allocations for India's National Immunisation Programme, a substantial portion of funds remains unspent, raising concerns about implementation efficiency. While vaccine coverage has improved, RTI data reveals consistent spending shortfalls, highlighting a need for better fund utilization and accountability in this crucial public health initiative.

stories.title: Assam turnout nears record 86%, highest rise in Muslim-majority districts
stories.summary: Assam witnessed a record-breaking voter turnout of nearly 86% in the 2026 assembly polls, the highest in the state's history. The Muslim belt saw the most significant increase in participation. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma expressed confidence in an NDA victory, citing strong support from the Sanatani community.

stories.title: Avenge Mamata's insult to Murmu, Shah calls upon tribal community
stories.summary: Union Minister Amit Shah urged Bengal's tribal communities to vote against TMC, alleging Mamata Banerjee insulted President Droupadi Murmu. Speaking in tribal-dominated districts, Shah promised a "son of soil" CM and inclusion of Kurmali and Rajbanshi in the Eighth Schedule, while also criticizing TMC for corruption and alleged land grabs by infiltrators.

stories.title: 'Going to have big problems': Donald Trump warns China on reports of weapons shipments to Iran
stories.summary: Donald Trump asserted US military dominance over Iran, claiming to have dismantled its capabilities and warning China against supplying weapons. Despite ongoing peace talks mediated by Pakistan, Trump declared victory regardless of a deal, emphasizing America's win and control over key shipping routes.

stories.title: SIR: Dead woman on voters list but husband, son off in Bengal
stories.summary: A 77-year-old woman, Mina Jalal, passed away before her name was cleared by the EC for voter registration, an irony as she had voted previously. Her husband and son were excluded from the voter list after adjudication, while other family members qualified. The family, residing in Kolkata for decades, faces harassment and lack of transparency from the EC.

stories.title: 'SIR is a big scam to bring BJP to office'
stories.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee has accused the Election Commission's Special Summary Revision (SIR) of being a "big scam" orchestrated to help the BJP win. She alleged indiscriminate voter deletion, disproportionately affecting Hindus, and claimed over 250 deaths occurred during the exercise.

stories.title: West Bengal polls: Didi alleges bid to cancel her nomination in Bhowanipore
stories.summary: West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee alleged attempts to cancel her Bhowanipore nomination through "false affidavits" filed by "traitors." Two objections, including a name mismatch and allegations of old criminal cases, were rejected. A third issue regarding ballot logistics was also resolved, ensuring her name remained on the first EVM.

stories.title: 'Big khela' coming to Bengal, declares PM Modi
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi intensified the BJP's Bengal campaign, challenging the TMC's "khela hobe" slogan and framing the polls as a fight for Bengal's identity. He promised to implement the Uniform Civil Code to end appeasement politics and vowed accountability for those who have "played far too long."

stories.title: Vijay's film not leaked from our system: CBFC
stories.summary: The Central Board of Film Certification has refuted claims of the Tamil film 'Jana Nayagan' leaking from its system, stating its certification process is secure. The board clarified that films are handed over to producers via a secure KDM mechanism. The alleged leak, which surfaced online, has sparked outrage and calls for stricter anti-piracy measures within the industry.

stories.title: Sam Altman’s alleged Molotov cocktail attacker identified as Daniel Alejandro Moreno-Gama
Delegates from 22 countries laud India's poll process
stories.summary: International delegates from 22 countries lauded India's recent elections in Kerala, Assam, and Puducherry, highlighting impressive voter turnout and meticulous planning. Witnessing firsthand the seamless execution, including EVM usage and webcasting, they described the process as a "true festival of democracy." Delegates also noted the well-organized polling stations with facilities and praised the transparency measures in place.

stories.title: Rare Modi-Rahul interaction breaks the internet
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi shared a rare moment of pleasantries and a brief chat at a recent event, sparking interest. Gandhi's presence at the commemorative program for Jyotirao Phule, where he greeted the PM, was noteworthy.

stories.title: IAF chief meets top US def officials to discuss shared strategic priorities, MQ-9B drones
stories.summary: Indian Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal A P Singh met with US Air Force leadership, including Gen Ken Wilsbach, to bolster defense ties and discuss shared strategic goals. Key topics included the procurement of MQ-9B Sky Guardian drones and enhancing Indo-Pacific cooperation.

stories.title: Vance-led team lands in Pak’s Nur Khan base, same air hub targeted by India during Op Sindoor
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance and an Iranian delegation arrived at Pakistan's Nur Khan airbase for peace talks. This base, a key Pakistani military hub, was reportedly targeted by Indian missile strikes last May. The US delegation's choice of the airbase highlights its strategic importance and proximity to Islamabad, despite past damage.

stories.title: Vance-led team lands in Pak’s Nur Khan base, same air hub targeted by India during Op Sindoor
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance and an Iranian delegation arrived at Pakistan's Nur Khan airbase for peace talks. This base, a key Pakistani military hub, was reportedly targeted by Indian missile strikes last May. The US delegation's choice of the airbase highlights its strategic importance and proximity to Islamabad, despite past damage.

stories.title: Eric Swalwell sexual misconduct row: Inside allegations of four women claiming assault by congressman
Milgram’s electric shock experiment: The test that exposed dark side of human obedience to authority
stories.summary: Stanley Milgram’s obedience experiments revealed how ordinary people could follow authority to disturbing extremes, with many participants administering what they believed were harmful shocks. Inspired by the Holocaust, the study became a landmark in psychology while raising serious ethical concerns. Decades later, its findings remain debated, with critics arguing the results reflect pressure, context, and interpretation as much as obedience.

stories.title: Indian LPG tanker crosses Hormuz, first after ceasefire
stories.summary: The Indian-flagged LPG tanker Jag Vikram successfully navigated the Strait of Hormuz, marking the first Indian vessel to pass through the conflict zone since a temporary ceasefire. This vessel, carrying 20,400 tonnes of cooking gas, is expected to reach Mumbai on April 15.

stories.title: Govt mulls sending surplus rice as aid to conflict-hit Iran
stories.summary: India is poised to permit wheat exports to Egypt, Indonesia, and Myanmar due to surplus stocks. Rice shipments, including to war-torn Iran on humanitarian grounds, are also being considered. This move aims to free up storage space for upcoming winter crops and capitalize on increased demand amid global supply chain disruptions.

stories.title: No forum to deal with arbitrators' misdeeds: SC judge
stories.summary: Supreme Court Justice B.V. Nagarathna emphasized that arbitration and mediation are vital to a modern justice system, not just alternatives to court. She noted a gap in addressing complaints against arbitrators, often retired judges, whom courts are hesitant to remove. Maintaining litigant trust is crucial, as bias allegations erode confidence in these dispute resolution methods.

stories.title: Mass arrests at London protest: Massive Attack musician Robert Del Naja among 200 held over Palestine Action rally
Nasha Mukt J&K: LG launches drive to cut off Pak supply, swift punishment for peddlers
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha Saturday launched a 100-day campaign to combat the drug menace, targeting supply from Pakistan and traffickers. The initiative involves revoking licenses, freezing assets, and issuing lookout circulars against drug peddlers. The campaign will proceed through awareness, community engagement, enforcement, rehabilitation, and evaluation phases.
